Native WebGPU teardown reconciliation: requesting, unavailable or failed fences retain leases; already-observed failures are exposed on explicit disposal, and only confirmed loss/destruction permits invalidation. A genuinely waiting fence is treated as transferred to interop, so ResourceLifecycle may report disposed before that fence later rejects; the device then exposes pending/failure but the completed parent is not retroactively re-enrolled. WebGPUDevice transfers an accepted waiting fence to interop, so a synchronous ResourceLifecycle may release the device or buffer and report disposed before that fence later rejects. Interop retains the native lease and records the failure until confirmed invalidation; a subsequent explicit device disposal reports it, but the already-completed lifecycle is not re-enrolled. The existing mock test documents this ordering; it was not run here. This is a completion/notification gap, not evidence of premature native destruction.

taskResults.reason: Root compute follows the selected native device and generation; shared leases submit in queue order and are retained through a fence or genuine invalidation. A focused mock probe confirms ResourceLifecycle retains a borrowed device while a fence waits or fails and releases after completion or confirmed loss. Existing immediate-completion assertions conflict with that behavior; full loss/recreation and late-fence verification remain open.

taskResults.description: Complete an explicitly opt-in functional backend before code freeze; preserve its experimental support label until actual rendered output, native dispatch and repeated lifecycle acceptance pass. An unconditional public-path rejection cannot count as completed backend code. Record software and hardware results separately.
taskResults.reason: Explicit WebGPU selection reaches the real renderer rather than an unconditional rejection, and the root profile remains experimental. The retained browser specification checks selected device, dispatch and pixels, but current-candidate rendered, repeated-lifecycle, and separately identified software/hardware results have not been established; older reports are historical. A focused mock probe confirms borrowed-device ownership remains held during waiting and failed fences, but existing immediate-completion assertions conflict with current behavior.

taskResults.description: Consume full WP-31 draw-state and vertex-layout descriptors, WP-30 depth conventions and WP-05 typed buffer layouts. Warm render and compute variants without presentation; test cancellation, target/layout-dependent cache identity and device-generation disposal.
taskResults.reason: Draws consume the native state mapper, vertex layouts, depth convention and derived shader data layouts; state-key and cache-lifecycle tests exist. Scene precompile creates shader modules without presenting, but the actual WebGPU render pipeline is created later on draw; compute exposes individual synchronous pipeline creation rather than a coordinated cancellable variant warmup. Complete render-and-compute warmup and its requested cancellation/identity/generation test contract are not established. A focused mock probe confirms borrowed-device lifecycle ownership remains held while fences wait or fail.

taskResults.description: Finish each existing bounded material lobe with texture transforms, color-space rules and correct normal/tangent handling.
taskResults.reason: Per-lobe map/UV/tangent features and color-space tests exist, but the support matrix still bounds several lobes and authored tangent identity; independent WebGPU preview rejects some combinations.

taskResults.description: Add rough diffuse and configurable retroreflection; preserve the existing iridescence range while accepting separate minimum/maximum controls.
taskResults.reason: Rough diffuse and retroreflection reach both shader languages. The physical factory includes separate film endpoints, and the root scalar and textured paths resolve and forward them. Broader lobe and real-backend verification remain open.

taskResults.description: Implement photometric profile admission, parsing, light-space orientation, projected images and shadow interaction.
taskResults.reason: Type-C parsing, light-space collection, profile sampling and spot projection/shadow source paths exist. Projection is limited to one nonclustered WebGL2 spot and profile indexing explicitly rejects clustered lighting; LightingRig itself only offers a scalar fallback or error.

taskResults.description: Test both symmetric and two-dimensional angular profiles, linear lamp/multiplier scaling and malformed tables. Feed generated lightmap UV charts/gutters from WP-13 into incremental baking without silently replacing authored UV channels.
taskResults.reason: Existing tests describe rotational and two-dimensional distributions, linear multipliers and malformed tables. The UV-atlas adapter consumes chart bounds, gutters, density and the selected generated channel; a source test uses the real atlas producer and checks the authored UV channel is preserved.

taskResults.description: Add point/spot clustered lighting, probe grids, incremental light baking, voxel-based indirect lighting and cascaded sun behavior with explicit backend limits and WebGL2 fallback.
taskResults.reason: Clustered light bins, SH grids, incremental bakes, cascades and bounded CPU voxel fallback with renderer attachments exist. Clustered profile/projection indexing is expressly unavailable, and complete required backend integration cannot be established across these combinations.

taskResults.description: Independently replace the attributed shader, environment and lookup implementations named in this lane; retain notices until replacement, and validate generated data against documented equations and fixtures. Ship the neutral environment self-contained and make optional presets explicit.
taskResults.reason: Independent room/sky and generated DFG/LTC sources, fixture tests and embedded neutral loading exist, but named physical WGSL twins still declare r185-identical implementations; neutral SH data still describes the earlier r185 room and a complete matched sky/environment replacement is not established.

taskResults.description: Use independently authored calibration scenes, reference equations and per-backend pixel checks.
taskResults.reason: A browser scene contains both-backend pixel-difference checks and a Lambert equation; independent numerical cases exist. The separate physical numeric harness says its shader candidates are not connected to the renderer, tolerances are unresolved, and its conformance gate remains incomplete; no pixel execution was performed.

taskResults.description: Specify typed graph IR, node/value validation, control flow, resources and serialization; generate both shader languages.
taskResults.reason: Typed, validated and serializable IR emits GLSL/WGSL material stages and WGSL compute. Public construction/serialization now has a declared engine subpath. However graph if/loop statements are rejected for material stages; WebGL compute/storage is explicitly unsupported.

taskResults.description: Support color, normal, roughness, metalness, emission, opacity and vertex-position outputs; support compute, storage buffers/textures, multiple UV sets and viewport inputs.
taskResults.reason: All seven graph outputs reach material stages; compute binds storage buffers/textures, UV0/UV1 and viewport inputs. Compute is WebGPU-only and graph storage textures are restricted to 2D; these bounds are explicit, not a claim of universal backend or dimensional support.

taskResults.description: Reuse existing node-material entrypoints through an Aura-owned adapter; preserve clear errors for unsupported operations.
taskResults.reason: material.node accepts graph documents and routes relevant legacy TSL outputs through Aura's migration adapter, retaining the legacy imperative GLSL path and named errors. Some old parity expectations contradict the newly supported outputs and WGSL route; those tests were not run.

taskResults.description: Complete 3D, array, cube, compressed, storage and depth resources, independent mip updates, attachment validation, resolve/copy/readback, bounded GPU sorting and lifecycle.
taskResults.reason: Factories, independent mips, attachment validation and a bounded sorter exist. 3D target descriptors, WebGPU layered targets and generic async transfers remain absent; splats still sort on CPU. Current source retains interop ownership through waiting or rejected fences, and the sorter does not treat a rejected loss notification as confirmed loss. Ambiguous sort submissions now retain scratch and caller buffers until a successful fence or confirmed loss, with a release receipt and reentrant-disposal barrier; focused mock probes and selected existing checks passed. Real-device and broader lifecycle verification remain open.

taskResults.description: Implement integer/bool bit representation and target-specific uniform/storage layouts for mixed scalar/vector/matrix/array/structure data. Validate strides, offsets, padding, non-square matrices, invalid lengths and byte-exact transfers; do not serialize integer uniforms as float bits.
taskResults.reason: Target layouts and byte writers handle signed/unsigned/bool, vectors, non-square matrices, arrays and structures; real std140 and WebGPU uniform paths use them. Graph schemas now support arrays/structs, but do not express matrices, WebGL portable aggregate uniforms are rejected, and compute storage takes raw caller bytes rather than graph-derived structured writes.

taskResults.description: Give depth/color attachments complete format/layer/mip/sample identities, prohibit conflicting reads/writes within a pass, preserve previous-depth attachments during history swaps and define ownership for async copy/readback cancellation.
taskResults.reason: Attachment identity, hazard checks, previous-depth ping-pong and GL cancellation exist; 3D target descriptors and generic WebGPU async transfers do not. A parent ResourceLifecycle can finish while a WebGPU retirement fence waits and cannot reflect a later rejection, even though interop retains the native lease.

taskResults.description: Test graphs on actual renderer paths, not only CPU interpretation or shader string snapshots.
taskResults.reason: Real renderer browser cases are authored for both backends and compute/render sharing, and native-shaped unit draws exist. Two browser compute cases import shaderGraph from the root, which does not export it; the newly declared graph facade is a separate subpath. Browser cases have not been run or certified.

taskResults.description: Implement every effect named in the WP-06 file table and audit all existing effects for the inputs they require. Independently replace the attributed shader and lookup implementations, preserving notices until their replacement is complete.
taskResults.reason: Independent AA/AO sources and generated lookups exist, as do the ordered display effects; native WebGPU still rejects several named effects and the public custom-input contract does not expose normals. Full effect/input audit and backend-complete family are not established.

taskResults.description: Add motion/depth/normal handling for animated, instanced and transparent content; explicitly flag unsupported combinations.
taskResults.reason: Rigid motion and depth are handled and unsupported motion is reported, but built-in deformation/instance motion uses rigid approximation and transparent/reactive coverage requires a populated input; full normal handling is not demonstrated.

taskResults.description: Verify pass order, masking, history reset on camera cut/resize, alpha, view isolation and disposal with visible pixels.
taskResults.reason: Browser source checks mask, alpha, afterimage cut and view isolation; unit source covers ordering, resize and disposal. A focused mock probe confirms the current parent ResourceLifecycle retains a borrowed device through waiting and failed fences; conflicting immediate-completion assertions remain. Visible-pixel coverage of ordering, resize and disposal is not established; acceptance has not run.

taskResults.description: Remove module-global temporal/model caches. Use app/device/view/frame identity, stable runtime object keys, once-per-frame history commits and scoped resets; test multiple cameras/apps/passes, repeated same-frame calls and duplicate object labels.
taskResults.reason: Renderer/view histories use stable keys and once-per-frame commits, with tests for owners, duplicate labels and repeated calls; the shared compatibility history and unscoped reset singleton remain.

taskResults.description: Define and implement separate spatial-upscale and temporal-reconstruction modes. Wire real reactive/disocclusion inputs, preserve previous depth across swaps, handle dynamic resolution and retain existing TAA/sharpening behavior where it already satisfies the contract.
taskResults.reason: WebGL distinguishes spatial and temporal reconstruction and preserves prior depth on a render-size change, but temporal reconstruction requires externally populated velocity/reactive inputs, prior depth defaults to an approximation, and WebGPU rejects v2 resolve.

taskResults.description: Prove motion blur preserves constant color and total weight, uses centered taps and handles one sample, zero/extreme motion, offscreen samples and transparent edges. Test deformation/instance/batch history without assuming rigid transforms are sufficient.
taskResults.reason: GLSL uses centered normalized depth-weighted taps, a single-sample fast path and bounded positions; an unrun synthetic pixel test covers constants, extreme motion, symmetry and transparency. It explicitly does not establish skinned/instanced production, and batch-history proof is not established.

taskResults.description: Resolve nested dependencies relative to their containing file, detect normalized cycles before awaiting in-flight work, and balance duplicate/shared retains on every success, failure and abort path.
taskResults.reason: Managed loads resolve against each containing document, check normalized ancestor and concurrent-flight cycles before awaiting, count duplicate edges, and release acquired references on success and cleanup paths.

taskResults.description: Verify admitted document and subresource bytes against their expected digests before cache insertion or render. Migrate existing single-file manifests safely; reject changed bytes, redirect mismatches and unavailable required hashing.
taskResults.reason: The typed glTF path migrates legacy hashes and verifies document and declared external bytes before use; redirects and unavailable SHA-256 fail closed. GLTFLoader snapshots and forwards document policy to buffers and images. The Gaussian splat loader now carries the effective document policy into child requests, and source probes cover verified dependency snapshots. Catalog-wide provenance and candidate verification remain incomplete.

taskResults.description: Connect native format admission end to end: typed manifest and loader registry, installed optional loader, root model runtime, render resources, error diagnostics and disposal. Distinguish explicit offline conversion from native runtime support.
taskResults.reason: Typed metadata and per-app registry reach the actor and resource builder, reject absent/data-only adapters, preserve offline conversion provenance and dispose leases. Opt-in PLY reaches the root path; the default registry intentionally installs only glTF.

taskResults.description: Make reported texture budgets match actual returned and resident bytes per device; handle duplicate names, eviction, streaming, release and reload.
taskResults.reason: Per-device accounting reflects allocated mip data; the residency controller and WebGL/WebGPU adapters handle sharing, eviction, fences, release, reload and generation changes. Real-device execution was not performed.

taskResults.description: Evict failed decoder initialization, bound worker queues and memory, await cancellation/teardown and permit safe retries.
taskResults.reason: Failed decoder promises are evicted, retries allowed, queues/memory bounded and active cancellation acknowledged or terminated. The KTX2 pool and decoder registry expose awaited cleanup, including late initialization owners; Basis and Draco abort callbacks now safely handle unprintable reasons. Wider decoder teardown and candidate-bound verification remain open.

taskResults.description: Forward the complete request contract to top-level files, external buffers, textures and images.
taskResults.reason: GLTFLoader snapshots and forwards document policy to buffers and images, and the Gaussian splat loader carries the effective document policy into child requests. Default browser image reads and capped custom decoders enforce the strictest document/request input limit before decoding; uncapped custom decoders retain their prior behavior. Custom decoder and transcoder settings are snapshotted for asynchronous acquisition and hashed cache identity. Focused source probes, selected existing cache/integrity and worker-fixture checks, and a two-root typecheck passed; universal loader policy and candidate verification remain incomplete.

taskResults.description: Extend the same policy to exported audio, scene, image-bitmap and generic renderable loaders. Define image-orientation precedence and close decoded resources after cancelled/failed ownership transfer.
taskResults.reason: Audio, scene and bitmap use verified fetch and combined cancellation; bitmap explicit orientation overrides flipY and late bitmaps close. Registry delegates transport to adapters. GLTFLoader forwards document policy to buffers and images, and GaussianSplatLoader carries the effective policy into child requests even with a bare LoadContext. Universal loader-policy verification remains open.

taskResults.description: Eliminate implicit fixture substitution for unknown formats, invalid manifests or unavailable transport. Preserve deliberate canonical content only behind an explicit fixture type; successful loads identify actual requested content and selected adapter.
taskResults.reason: Only an explicitly typed canonical fixture loads synthetic content and its manifest is validated; registry selection rejects unknown formats, and successful results expose requested URL and selected adapter.

taskResults.description: Scope decoded audio caches by content and request identity, bound decoded memory, independently cancel subscribers and generation-guard clear/dispose/replacement against late fetch/decode completion.
taskResults.reason: Decoded audio uses request/content identities, entry and byte budgets, independent subscribers, final leases and in-flight generation checks on clear, dispose and replacement.

taskResults.description: Fix decoder plugin dev/build/static-base agreement. Emit and package a same-origin worker, preserve configured prefixes, validate MIME/path encoding, reject traversal and test a same-origin-only worker policy with only the codec's actual WebAssembly permissions.
taskResults.reason: Vite derives one validated dev/build/preview path, emits a same-origin worker and codec files, rejects traversal/encoding errors and serves MIME types. Existing packed-browser test specifies self-only worker and wasm-unsafe-eval; no browser was run.

taskResults.description: Partition in-flight and persistent caches by effective request context; hash or otherwise protect sensitive material, and ensure one caller's abort cannot cancel another.
taskResults.reason: Request identities hash effective settings; managed and glTF flights isolate subscribers. Disposed-asset and glTF texture diagnostic paths now sanitize sensitive URLs and hostile causes. However, the exported raw AssetCache accepts arbitrary caller keys, and a legacy synchronous glTF key helper embeds caller URL text; universal cache enforcement and candidate verification are not established.

taskResults.description: Implement and render the named new material extensions; finish existing bounded extensions individually, including variants and animated values.
taskResults.reason: The loader and exporter preserve verified required default emissive-strength pointer identity only for the original source track/material; loss or replacement is detected while the original lookup remains. Identity is in-memory and reconstructed/serialized tracks lose it. Draft diffuse-roughness and bump have parsing, bindings and shader code; the support matrix records limited paths while required declarations remain rejected. Other material, pointer and BRDF paths remain bounded. The existing pixel scenario covers emissive strength, variants and pointer animation only; neither it nor the source tests were run.

taskResults.description: Test required/optional declarations, malformed buffers, invalid URIs, cross-origin policy, unsupported codecs, retries, cancellation and progress.
taskResults.reason: Existing tests cover required/optional declarations, malformed material data, policy, missing codecs, retry, cancellation and progress. New source tests specify required emissive-default round trips and loss/replacement detection. A complete invalid-URI and malformed glTF-buffer matrix was not established; no tests were run.

taskResults.description: Independently replace the attributed image decoder, then implement every format and variant listed in the WP-08 table, grouped into independently loadable modules.
taskResults.reason: The EXR decoder has been replaced and opt-in importer modules exist, but 3DM requires a supplied decoder, JXL/UltraHDR require supplied codecs, and the full catalog is not admitted or rendered through typed paths.

taskResults.description: For each format define units, coordinate conventions, scene/hierarchy, geometry, materials, animation, dependencies, binary/ASCII versions and supported extension set.
taskResults.reason: Selected source variants, units and losses are described, but the public inventory explicitly leaves the per-format versions, coordinates, dependencies and loss matrix to future verification.

taskResults.description: Admit inputs through typed asset/provenance workflows. Enforce file, archive expansion, pixel and allocation limits; return stable diagnostics for malformed or unsupported inputs.
taskResults.reason: Typed inspection, provenance hashes and bounded parsers exist for selected models, PVR and NRRD; strict admission and consistent limits/diagnostics are not implemented for the full catalog. Ordinary image loaders and the default glTF raster path now enforce browser byte and pixel limits; custom decoder byte policies are applied separately.

taskResults.description: Provide a valid minimal fixture, a realistic multi-feature fixture where applicable, and hostile/truncated inputs for every format. Render supported scene content through the public API.
taskResults.reason: Scene, mesh, scientific and image fixtures, glTF required-emissive pointer identity source tests and a packed-adapter browser spec exist, but the browser source covers only seven simple mesh/3MF cases plus an OBJ/MTL case, not every typed format. JXL/UltraHDR tests use mock codecs; dedicated BVH, MDD, SVG, MaterialX and 3DL source tests were not found.

taskResults.description: Implement every exporter in the WP-09 table with an independently specified capability matrix and a typed result.
taskResults.reason: The opt-in source barrel and package export expose all eight writer families; a separately declared per-format capability matrix and typed result/diagnostic contracts exist. The CLI and browser-test source are also present; no current-source build or test pass is established.

taskResults.description: Round-trip geometry, transform, hierarchy, material, animation, skin/morph and metadata where each format supports them.
taskResults.reason: Existing source tests round-trip subsets of loaded GLB scenes, skin, morph weights, animation and OBJ material/geometry; additional unrun glTF tests cover required default emissive-pointer identity and material remapping. The runtime snapshot explicitly loses document-level provenance and material variants, and USDZ tests parse ZIP framing but assert stage text rather than independently loading its supported scene semantics.

taskResults.description: Produce structured warnings for loss, missing encoders or unsupported features; never silently omit data. Test independent readers, formats, endianness, units and dependency packaging.
taskResults.reason: Exporters emit typed warnings and explicit missing-codec errors; tests cover dependencies, units, endian variants and several independent readers. Complete independent semantic round trips are not established for all exporters: USDZ stage assertions are textual and PLY tests inspect selected fields rather than a complete independent reader.

taskResults.description: Preserve quantized attributes and indexed lines in formats that represent them, or produce explicit losses. Test HDR RLE/PIZ output and explicit attachment/layer export from multiple-output targets without clamping scene values.
taskResults.reason: glTF writes typed quantized accessors and indexed lines, and other writers explicitly report applicable conversions/losses. The render-target EXR source now selects a concrete float color attachment and reports omitted attachments, subject to backend/subresource restrictions. Existing focused exporter checks passed; actual GPU/browser attachment readback and broader format verification remain open.

taskResults.description: Parse all named splat formats and validate sample count, attributes, covariance, color and spherical-harmonic layouts.
taskResults.reason: PLY, SPLAT, SPZ and KHR glTF paths check counts, array layouts, finite values, opacity, rotations and covariance. KSPLAT still requires an external decoder, as does packed PLY, and the public scene compiler constructs the loader without either codec; therefore not all named formats are parsed on the integrated path.

taskResults.description: Implement camera-dependent ordering, blending, culling, depth interaction, bounds and resource budgets; define what happens on unsupported backends.
taskResults.reason: Per-camera covariance projection, culling and stable distance sorting feed alpha-blended, depth-tested runs; scene bounds, layer/render-order filtering, aggregate instance-buffer budgets and unsupported backend/depth diagnostics are integrated. Transparent mesh intersections are approximated by whole-item sort centers, and nonstandard depth and some target/effect combinations explicitly fail.

taskResults.description: Add scalar-volume slices and rendering with clipping, transfer functions and lifecycle tests.
taskResults.reason: Typed scalar-volume assets mount WebGL2 or WebGPU renderers with X/Y/Z slices, local clip planes and transfer stops; lifecycle tests cover updates, loss, cancellation and disposal. Root rendering is intentionally restricted to supported forward, depth and output combinations. The required lifecycle tests exist, but do not establish end-to-end notification of a late shared WebGPU fence rejection; see the lifecycle limitation.

taskResults.description: Add smooth and Bézier interpolation as distinct modes from glTF cubic spline; preserve authored tangents and serialization.
taskResults.reason: Smooth uses authored or estimated derivatives, Bézier uses absolute controls, and glTF cubic uses per-second derivatives; track JSON retains modes and tangents. The existing test samples their distinct curves and endpoints.

taskResults.description: Independently replace attributed property-binding code and test escaped names, Unicode, indexed bones/morphs, duplicate targets, missing targets and prototype-safe lookup.
taskResults.reason: The working-tree scanner and prototype-safe lookup and the requested edge-case tests exist. The former explicitly attributed implementation was structurally replaced, but independent authorship/provenance is not established by the current source or tests.

taskResults.description: Support requested vector widths and deterministic clock/action semantics: reverse, repeat, ping-pong, time scale, timed fades and end conditions.
taskResults.reason: Explicit vector widths are validated and sampled; core actions implement signed time, repeat, reflection, timed fades, and finite completion. Existing lifecycle and interpolation tests cover those features.

taskResults.description: Align core, compiled-pose and root asset playback for signed time, warp and synchronization. Compare large-step and equivalent small-step updates, multi-wrap marker order, reflected direction, zero duration and paused/stopped states; cap event catch-up and report overflow explicitly.
taskResults.reason: Core actions have warp and synchronization, the glTF mixer returns those actions, and pose playback uses core traversal; ordered crossings and overflow tests exist. Current pose warp uses unpaused action time, and an offline source probe confirmed it stays aligned with core across a pause and resume. Full cross-path and candidate verification remain open.

taskResults.description: Fix object-group subscription and UUID bookkeeping. Test subscribe/remove/resubscribe, middle/final uncache and re-add, duplicates and final disposal; no stale path may resolve to another live binding.
taskResults.reason: Per-member and per-subscription maps preserve ownership, release stale bindings, and reject duplicate UUID ownership. Existing tests cover remove, uncache and re-add, resubscription, duplicates, reentrancy, and disposal.

taskResults.description: Preserve authored values/tangents through optimize/trim/serialize/additive conversion for every interpolation mode; test values along the curve, not just surviving key counts.
taskResults.reason: Optimization retains curved/authored-tangent tracks, exact trim subdivides cubic controls, serialization retains tangents, and additive conversion distinguishes controls from derivatives. Existing tests compare sampled curves for all five modes and additive curved modes.

taskResults.description: Correct audio position under playback-rate changes, scheduled starts, loop regions and pause/resume; add generic source adapters.
taskResults.reason: Buffer position integrates changing rate and detune after scheduled start, with loop and pause/resume accounting. Public element, stream and external-node adapters define borrowed/owned teardown; non-buffer adapters document their narrower controls.

taskResults.description: Compute emitter/listener orientation through nested transforms, including mirrored or nonuniform scale; test disposal and user-gesture rules.
taskResults.reason: The scene bridge resolves ancestor world matrices, transforms emitter axes and orthogonalizes listener axes; tests cover mirrored/nonuniform ancestors, borrowed disposal and gesture rejection. Browser gesture/audio behavior has not been accepted.

taskResults.description: Verify both state and visible deformed pixels; an animation state update alone is insufficient.
taskResults.reason: A browser spec checks a skinned palette and changed WebGL pixels, but its shared harness hard-codes cameraStable and labels every sufficiently bright changed pixel as a subject pixel, without a subject region or mask. Thus the source check does not independently establish that the changed pixels are deformation; no current-source browser receipt was inspected.

taskResults.description: Implement pointer-driven dragging and selection with plane intersection, hover, capture, cancellation, multi-touch and parent transforms.
taskResults.reason: Concurrent multi-touch plane drags, capture, hover and parent transforms exist; the marquee API accepts caller-supplied endpoints and is not wired to pointer events or selection state.

taskResults.description: Complete arcball gestures and test all existing controls for event/listener cleanup.
taskResults.reason: Arcball supports cursor zoom, pinch/pan/roll and cleanup, measures the canvas content box, and the native camera adapter provides projection/near metadata, a ray and up-aware lookAt. Full candidate and browser/device behavior remain unverified.

taskResults.description: Retain per-contact positions/buttons and stable IDs. Define client, canvas-CSS and framebuffer coordinates for embedded/scrolled/resized targets; use timestamps for gestures and stable pinch pairs independent of frame rate.
taskResults.reason: Per-contact coordinates, identity, elapsed tap timing and stable pinch pairs are implemented.

taskResults.description: Treat pointercancel, lost capture, blur and device disconnect as termination without click/tap activation; release one contact without clearing another and verify real hit locations across DPR changes.
taskResults.reason: Contact-specific cancellation and independent release are implemented; a DPR-sensitive rendered-picking browser spec exists, but acceptance has not run.

taskResults.description: Sample native XR viewer poses, hand joints and hit-test results with their reference spaces; acquire/cancel hit-test sources with the session.
taskResults.reason: Native viewer, hand and hit-result poses use the session space; hit-test sources are acquired/cancelled with ownership.

taskResults.description: Add optional hands/controllers, plane/depth data and estimated lighting; integrate GPU composition only when supported.
taskResults.reason: Optional caller visual factories and native plane/depth/light adapters exist; supported WebGL projection composition is capability-checked. No WebGPU XR support is claimed.

taskResults.description: Generation-guard every async session-enter stage; concurrent enters create at most one owned session and exit/dispose closes any late-created session. Route input-source changes, select/squeeze, reference-space reset and visibility events; negotiate optional layer/foveation capabilities with explicit unsupported results.
taskResults.reason: Owner/generation guards cover awaited startup stages; session input/reset/visibility events and optional capability results are routed.

taskResults.description: Distinguish injected session results from actual device results and record each separately.
taskResults.reason: Injected source tests label provenance; separately recorded physical-device results are pending post-freeze acceptance.

taskResults.description: Independently replace the attributed geometry implementations named in the WP-13 file table; preserve notices until their replacements pass equivalent contract tests.
taskResults.reason: Most named builders were rewritten and independent shape/straight extrusion and contract fixtures exist, but Support explicitly retains earlier port portions and general Extrude provenance/compatibility is under review. Earlier per-file origin comments were removed without a current-source passing equivalent-contract receipt.

taskResults.description: Implement rational curve, surface and volume evaluation with knots, weights, derivatives, clipping and degenerate inputs.
taskResults.reason: Public rational curve, surface and volume evaluate weighted points and mixed derivatives using validated knot axes, clipped ranges and finite/singular-input guards; derivative orders are bounded at 16.

taskResults.description: Implement loft, parametric and patch geometry with normals, UV seams, caps and tessellation controls.
taskResults.reason: Public rendering generators provide a seam-aware parametric grid, transported-frame loft with caps and authored bicubic patch teapot with subdivision controls. Browser scenario source exists but was not run.

taskResults.description: Implement every named mesh utility and modifier; preserve or explicitly report changes to groups, attributes, morphs, indices and bounds. Implement bevels on path extrusion or reject them explicitly instead of silently dropping the setting.
taskResults.reason: Named utility and modifier implementations now have an opt-in public subpath, loss diagnostics and path-bevel layers (linear mode explicitly rejects bevel/path). Broad named topology-validation/compression and general mesh-memory contracts remain unestablished, and independent general extrusion provenance is still under review.

taskResults.description: Make weighted surface sampling seeded and deterministic. Verify numerical and rendered outcomes.
taskResults.reason: Seeded area-weighted sampling, within-face density weighting and interpolation are public; deterministic/statistical numerical test source exists. No rendered sample-points scenario or current-source visual receipt was found.

taskResults.description: Build UV charts with an explicit destination channel, seams, texel density, gutter and atlas limits. Return vertex/index remaps and preserve groups/attributes/morphs after seam duplication; test nonoverlap, degeneracy, cancellation and bounded failure, then verify a baked-lighting scene uses the atlas.
taskResults.reason: Public atlas supplies explicit channel, chart seams, packing, limits, remaps and stream preservation; tests include nonoverlap, degeneracy, cancellation and capacity. A public adapter feeds actual generated charts to the native baker in a unit test and scene lightmap attachment exists, but the browser lighting scene uses a hand-authored atlas rather than buildUVAtlas; no generated-atlas baked-lighting scene/receipt was found.

taskResults.description: Implement the advanced helper catalog with scene-driven updates, visibility, transforms and disposal.
taskResults.reason: The public helper namespace contains the advanced glyph builders and a frame-sampled dynamic helper; visibility, node transforms, replacement and disposal are implemented. Inputs are supplied by the caller, including CPU pixels for texture previews. Existing focused unit results are not bound to the current worktree.

taskResults.description: Render accessible DOM labels in 2D and 3D and document occlusion and event limitations.
taskResults.reason: The opt-in DOM renderer projects screen-aligned and perspective elements, preserves accessibility attributes, and documents anchor-only occlusion and DOM-versus-canvas event routing. Browser accessibility and pointer assertions exist but have not been run in this audit.

taskResults.description: Implement vector, text and stereo outputs with clear size, clipping, style, eye-order and resource semantics.
taskResults.reason: SVG, bounded ASCII and stereo implementations specify clipping, sizing, styles, eye order and resource ownership. SVG selects the position stream and uses decoded attributes where available. Candidate-bound and rendered-output verification remain open.

taskResults.description: Test assistive labels, pointer routing, screenshot output, resize and cleanup.
taskResults.reason: Browser test source checks an accessible button, pointer pass-through and interception, resize and DOM restoration, tests vector/outline/stereo pixels, and attaches screenshots; unit source also asserts target disposal. Screenshots are attachments, not retained passing visual receipts.

taskResults.description: Implement every named specialized object, generator and editing tool as an opt-in module.
taskResults.reason: Six typed addon subpaths implement isosurfaces, specialized objects, generators and editing tools. The complete named checklist is not integrated as opt-in modules: the scene surface API only exposes a mirror, standalone glass refraction requires an explicitly supplied lower-level capture, and isosurface material groups are not applied as separate materials by the ordinary scene draw path. Terrain height and collider paths now include vertical origin; complete integration verification remains open.

taskResults.description: Reuse the existing terrain, sky, water and scatter facilities where they satisfy the contract; do not replace working paths.
taskResults.reason: Grounded sky reuses day/night state and forest reuses scatterInArea; public sky, water and world.terrain remain. The generated mesh and world terrain height/raycast/collider paths now include vertical origin. This source inspection does not establish every changed shared-runtime path or candidate-bound behavior.

taskResults.description: Bound memory and polygon generation, support seed reproducibility and undo data, and test invalid inputs and teardown.
taskResults.reason: The addon generators, isosurfaces, sculptor, tubes and fracture have bounded buffers or work, deterministic seeds where applicable, edit patches, invalid-input checks and disposal tests. The broader named lens-flare path accepts an arbitrarily long elements array and allocates a material and render item per element, so the work-package-wide memory/polygon bound is not established; no element-budget test is present.

taskResults.description: Define hidden-page suspension/resume, bounded catch-up, resize/DPR changes while hidden and temporal-history reset without changing explicit manual-step semantics.
taskResults.reason: The scheduler suspends automatic work, coalesces hidden resizes, resets history and preserves manual deltas. Automatic rendering now uses a bounded accumulated clock, and the host remeasures canvas size and DPR before resuming. Full candidate and browser timing verification remain open.

taskResults.description: Expose whether a render failure is terminal or recoverable; suppress late callbacks after disposal and test recovery.
taskResults.reason: The low-level protocol exposes terminal/recoverable severity, suppresses callbacks after disposal begins and has loss/recovery cases. The root app now reports a restored failed scene replacement as recoverable and establishes fresh readiness for the restored owner. Candidate-bound and real-worker verification remain open.

taskResults.description: Transfer canvas ownership once; define message ordering, request IDs, resize/input snapshots, errors and cancellation.
taskResults.reason: Preflight precedes the single canvas transfer, WeakSets reject reuse, increasing request IDs and a worker-side serial tail order operations, and the protocol includes input/resize snapshots, severity-bearing errors and AbortSignal cancellation. Source tests exercise these paths; they were not run for this audit.

taskResults.description: Support initial scene, dynamic updates, asynchronous assets, frame scheduling and backend loss inside the worker.
taskResults.reason: Initial and replacement scenes mount in the worker, the production compiler receives asset options and cancellation, frames are scheduled, and device loss/restoration is handled. The root app publishes the replacement snapshot before acknowledgement and turns a recoverable failed replacement into terminal root state even if the worker restored the old scene; additionally raw wall-clock timestamps can advance rendered animation across suspension. Real backend behavior is not claimed.

taskResults.description: Test unsupported browser fallback, termination, duplicate disposal and no retained workers/listeners.
taskResults.reason: Unit sources assert unsupported fallback, termination, duplicate disposal and zero host/worker/DOM listener counts, with separate pointer-capture coverage. The explicitly requested tests have no passing receipt bound to the current tree; the browser spec is conditional and was not executed. Normal dispose also resolves after a forced-termination timeout without worker cleanup acknowledgement, whereas disposeStrict reports it.

taskResults.description: Connect graph editing to real material state and the renderer compiler; provide typed ports, cycle errors, undo and serialization.
taskResults.reason: The mounted material-graph editor uses the renderer's typed graph model and GLSL/WGSL compiler, exposes compatible ports and cycle diagnostics, records graph changes in command history, and persists graph/resource selections through versioned project serialization. The UI is scoped to material graphs; this is not a browser pass.

taskResults.description: Inspect actual textures, passes, timing and resources; avoid fixture-only visualizations.
taskResults.reason: Real asset texture handles, device counters, measured graph-pass CPU durations, viewport CPU submission time and available per-view GPU timings feed the panels. Shadow, contributor, post and native-device phases remain incomplete; whole-frame CPU/GPU timing and runtime-only texture inventory are not established.

taskResults.description: Provide keyboard operation, compact density and accessible error, loading and empty states. Use the repository's licensed typography and density rules; do not introduce remote font services.
taskResults.reason: Graph and texture panels provide keyboard controls and announced states; local Whitney fonts and compact styles exist. Arbitrary hierarchy reparenting is drag/drop-only, inspector validation errors are written to a non-live console, and asset import promises have no visible loading/error handling. Font source filenames are recorded but an applicable redistribution grant was not found in the inspected repository evidence.

taskResults.description: Prove create/edit/reload changes rendered pixels and that invalid graphs show actionable diagnostics.
taskResults.reason: An existing browser specification compares actual WebGL pixels before and after editing, checks the reloaded result, and asserts invalid-graph diagnostics. No matching current-source browser execution or retained pixel receipt was found, so the requested proof remains deferred acceptance.

taskResults.description: Supply ledger findings to WP-00, its sole owner. Replace historical exclusion language only when the corresponding implementation and installed entrypoint exist.
taskResults.reason: The appendix recasts the old loader/exporter exclusions as historical and requires installed-path evidence before promotion. The WP-18 ledger row still has no implementation or evidence, and the inspected ledger does not establish that findings were handed to sole owner WP-00. Source manifests declare optional entrypoints, but an installed-candidate handoff was not established.

taskResults.description: Document actual backend, hardware, resource, format and lossy-export limitations. Each public feature has an Aura3D-owned runnable example with typed assets.
taskResults.reason: Prototype backend, format, loss and security notes and typed-model scenarios exist. The backend page is stale about root WebGPU selection and vertex types, and the ten indexed scenarios and recipes do not cover each public capability family; for example, the declared worker and interchange exporter surfaces have no dedicated indexed scenario. A separately admitted example asset and its bytes were inspected; no candidate execution is implied.

taskResults.description: Keep the ledger current; complete every row and retain proof of public exposure, not merely internal classes.
taskResults.reason: The untracked ledger and structural validator exist, but aggregation of the current 1,901 outcomes shows zero with source.completion complete, 25 with source evidence, and 21 with public entrypoints. The WP-18 row itself still has neither implementation nor evidence. These are ledger-field counts, not a conclusion that the underlying product code is absent.

taskResults.description: Integrate lanes in dependency order, adding exports, package metadata, generated maps and side-effect declarations. Keep optional packages out of root consumer bundles unless imported.
taskResults.reason: Native opt-in metadata, side-effect declarations, worker finalization and tree-shaking infrastructure exist. However the asset package promises ImportPipeline from its types but selects a browser barrel that omits it; full lane integration and actual optional-root bundle isolation are not established.

taskResults.description: Generate TypeScript, development, test and distribution mappings from one registry; typecheck new source/asset/browser-test files and verify all generated outputs, including emitted worker entrypoints, without hand-editing derived maps.
taskResults.reason: One registry drives TS, Vite, Vitest and generated dist manifests; current TS, Vite, CLI and manifest source mappings match by direct read. Workspace package export conditions are maintained separately, several QR trees are excluded from typechecking, no emitted candidate was verified, and the source runner fails closed on unavailable package-manager custody/isolation.

taskResults.description: Add an independently implemented CommonJS bridge where technically supported; test ESM and CommonJS from packed installations on supported Node versions.
taskResults.reason: The independent math bridge forwards CommonJS to Aura3D ESM on compatible Node versions, and the packed-consumer test exercises both formats using process.execPath. Root has no Node engines declaration and no supported-version execution matrix or candidate-bound result was established.

taskResults.description: Replace generic option-coverage scaffolds with valid typed probes; each supported documented option must change the correct runtime/visual behavior or produce an actionable unsupported error.
taskResults.reason: Typed A/B probes, real consumer observations and an actionable unsupported case replace generic scaffolds. Discovery is restricted to named root builder families and literal executable examples, and correct behavior across every supported documented option is not established.

taskResults.description: Make release planning, tarball checks, package tiers, provenance and verification derive from one versioned inventory; include the new optional package without rewriting historical inventories.
taskResults.reason: Release plan and public verification use versioned inventories retaining historical sets and adding addons. Package tiers remain a separate static map and tarball target discovery scans manifests rather than deriving the set directly from the inventory; exports are independently registry-driven.

taskResults.description: Support source identity in a Git-free staged job by verifying its explicit manifest. Bind unchanged tested source/archive digests to the subsequent freeze commit; reject changed implementation and keep administrative evidence updates separate without weakening signed-source identity.
taskResults.reason: Staged manifests verify bytes, modes and symlink bounds and bind source/lock/archive hashes to the later clean commit; administrative files are separate. A distinct trusted signed approval is implemented for workspace dependency inputs, while freeze proof validates Git object hashes and does not itself show that a trusted signature covers the frozen source; end-to-end signed-source continuity remains unestablished.

taskResults.description: Repair the existing performance script's undefined commands by wiring it to candidate-bound remote-report analysis. Rendered measurement collection occurs after source freeze; source tests cover workload/budget logic without launching a browser.
taskResults.reason: test:performance invokes the candidate-bound analyzer, which validates the global gate before reading measurements; workload and budget tests use synthetic data without launching browsers. The real rendered collection is deferred.

taskResults.description: Remove all external 3D-engine development dependencies, related typings and comparison-only adapters from every required install profile and lock graph. Assign every affected source, test, example and generated file discovered by the audit to exactly one lane in WP-00, with an exact path and action. Convert affected tests and examples to independently authored or open-standard fixtures without sacrificing behavior coverage.

Comparison-only sources still import three and are excluded from typecheck; exhaustive unique WP-00 ownership, every install graph and coverage-preserving conversion remain unestablished.

taskResults.description: Audit source origins and lookup data as well as the transitive package graph, imports, packed artifacts and observed network requests. Track each independently verified replacement in the ledger; no scanner alone proves independent authorship.

A complete reviewed source-origin/replacement ledger, all profiles and candidate-bound observed network evidence have not been established.

taskResults.description: Measure startup, installed bytes, draw calls, frame/CPU/GPU time, allocations and repeated resource lifetimes with fixed versioned workloads; document device and methodology.
taskResults.reason: Seven fixed workloads, 300-frame sessions, GPU timers, WebGL allocation/resource observations and methodology are implemented, but the collector always sets installed bytes, JS allocation count and thread CPU time to null; real device measurements and repeated lifetime results have not been retained for this candidate.

taskResults.description: Change the browser runner install to use the updated independent frozen lock, with equivalent source/browser test coverage.
taskResults.reason: Browser image installs pnpm using a frozen lock, but equivalent independent source/browser coverage is not established: source image is unavailable and every native browser job requires blocked consumer restoration.
