taskResults.reason: Tracked and untracked inputs are enumerated and hashed, argv is allowlisted, and provider/cleanup plumbing exists; the no-argument admission invoked before staging always throws, and the source image separately exits unconditionally.

taskResults.description: Include complete asset/contract suites and Node release tests in source execution. Assert required tests were discovered, and propagate missing/nonzero command status independently of upload success.
taskResults.reason: The source plan includes assets/QR, contracts and Node release inventories with discovery and separate test/upload exits, but the runner refuses before any suite can execute.

taskResults.description: Implement and source-test the single global phase gate. Require its matching code-complete record at acceptance entrypoints before job submission and inside the remote task; the source runner must reject any browser/acceptance argv before starting a process.
taskResults.reason: Exact-set gate, host and in-task validation, and source argv rejection exist; gate tests cover tampering and synthetic handoff, but explicit equal-count/different-ID and unowned-outcome cases and coverage of every acceptance entrypoint were not established.

taskResults.description: Copy staged tests/fixtures into browser images and include the actual template/environment payloads for consumer jobs. Test staging omissions as failures before submission; avoid uploading unrelated repository assets.
taskResults.reason: Gate-enumerated inputs, selected specs and nonempty fixture/template/environment directories are checked before submission. The actual browser-launcher missing-payload test was not located, and the manifest includes all source inputs rather than excluding unrelated assets.

taskResults.description: Add independent project selection and JSON result reporting for all supported browser families; retain test status separately if artifact transport fails.
taskResults.reason: Named Chromium, Firefox and WebKit projects, JSON discovery/results and distinct execution/upload statuses exist, but the required React consumer restoration fails before any native project can start.

taskResults.description: Strengthen subject-aware pixel checks and extend the existing repeated-resource soak; an opaque or intentionally dark frame must be interpreted using fixture expectations.
taskResults.reason: Fixture-specific subject/background tests handle transparent, noisy and dark frames, and the soak counts buffers, textures, programs, listeners and workers. It does not measure WebGPU pipelines and its heap thresholds are calibrated only for Chromium/CDP.

taskResults.description: Add an approved artifact-egress path to the serverless browser runner. Its current ad-hoc mode retains logs but does not provide general screenshot/trace egress.
taskResults.reason: Browser task collects invocation logs, JSON, screenshots/traces and uses bounded, create-only managed-identity Blob egress; actual service authorization and transport were not exercised.

taskResults.description: Run source checks, package tests and source-phase installed consumers before freeze; run remote browser behavior and visual tests afterward. Keep actual test names, versions, run IDs, candidate hashes, backend, device and limitations with results.
taskResults.reason: The source/consumer plan and acceptance metadata are present, but no current candidate-bound source reports exist and the source runner and matrix producer are explicitly unavailable. Browser/visual execution is post-freeze.

taskResults.description: Run repeated mount/load/unload/dispose, backend/context loss and recovery, and security-context isolation tests.
taskResults.reason: Lifecycle and multi-app/security-context tests exist; performing repeated recovery and isolation runs on the frozen candidate is post-freeze acceptance and was not attempted.

taskResults.description: Separate hardware XR/native-GPU receipts from software adapters or injected sessions. Claims may name only the level actually verified.
taskResults.reason: Evidence policy separates software rendering and injected XR from physical GPU/headset support and requires actual environment metadata; no hardware receipt is claimed.

taskResults.description: Introduce app/device-owned runtime context for color and shader policy, world/animation flags, caches, atmosphere, events and diagnostics. A newly created app must not reset or modify another active app.
taskResults.reason: Runtime owners reach compiled and legacy color/matrix frames, shader stores and fog. World builders register app-owned flags and avoid arbitrarily selecting between multiple live apps; explicit owner scopes remain necessary when ownership is ambiguous. Shared-canvas WebGPU and complete multi-app coverage remain open.

taskResults.description: Implement the section 3.5 readiness result for renderer and first-frame stages; distinguish failure, cancellation, disposal and superseded mounts. Keep existing settled-only behavior during its documented transition.
taskResults.reason: Renderer and first-frame outcomes distinguish superseded mounts from caller cancellation and export their public types; settled-only ready remains available. Existing tests expecting the former cancelled result conflict, and the lifecycle migration documentation and complete candidate-bound verification remain open.

taskResults.description: Scope asset callbacks and redacted errors to their owner; unregister on dispose and suppress late async completion. Test two apps sharing a page with different strictness, flags, scenes and failing assets.
taskResults.reason: App-owned texture callback scopes redact errors and use a disposal signal; late texture work is released instead of returning a handle after disposal. Existing tests include an expectation for the former late-error behavior, and complete cross-loader and multi-app verification remain open.

taskResults.description: Make error formatting safe for cycles, large values, unusual getters and big integers. Bound repeated error records and avoid leaking credentials or signed URLs.
taskResults.reason: Diagnostic traversal, top-level bigint formatting and worker listener records are bounded and redacted. Worker runtime conversion now handles unprintable and revoked-proxy thrown values in focused offline probes; three selected existing protocol checks pass. Other transport/error paths and full candidate-bound verification remain open.

taskResults.description: Dispose every owned resource even after one disposer fails; aggregate errors and make repeated disposal idempotent. Cover mount/resize/loss/restore/dispose races and shared-resource ownership.
taskResults.reason: ResourceLifecycle and final app/controller disposal continue across sibling failures and aggregate errors, including shared-owner tests. In contrast remount teardown calls the old loss unsubscribe, compute disposal and physics disposal sequentially without individual guards, so an early throw skips later retirements; the named async lifecycle test does not cover the requested full race matrix.

taskResults.description: Fix pooled target double release; track live leases/idle membership so simultaneous users never share one lease and counters remain nonnegative. Test foreign targets, trim, restore and outstanding handles.
taskResults.reason: The pool tracks distinct token leases, active/idle/retired targets and loss generations; duplicate or foreign releases do not free another lease and counts derive from live sets. The specified source tests cover simultaneous use, foreign/disposed targets, trim, loss/restore and outstanding leases.

taskResults.description: Dispose asynchronously compiled programs that arrive after disposal or generation change; settle held handles accurately and reject new acquisitions on dead caches. Test partial shader allocations, link failures, polling cancellation, supported retry and warmup settlement.
taskResults.reason: Cache generation guards settle old handles and reject dead acquisitions; WebGL tracks and cleans compile polling, and the named tests cover partial allocation, linking, retry and warmup. A late program whose disposer throws is discarded by the stale compile catch with no retained retry/error, and normal cache disposal clears failed programs, so guaranteed late resource retirement is incomplete.

taskResults.description: Coordinate frame pause/resume behavior with WP-16 and asset request ownership with WP-07/WP-05.
taskResults.reason: Pause, visibility, resume and temporal reset are wired. Mount requests and app-owned texture.load use cancellation signals, and late texture work is released. Cross-loader event integration and candidate-bound lifecycle verification remain open.

taskResults.description: Define exact supported browser/OS/backend combinations with version ranges and fallback behavior. Start every untested cell as unverified.
taskResults.reason: The matrix versions the planned automation targets, marks every target unverified, and documents WebGL2/WebGPU selection and fallback. It explicitly does not define any supported browser/OS version range or promote a combination; establishing actual supported ranges requires later candidate-bound acceptance, not an inference from target versions. The existing unit test validates evidence fields, not supported ranges.

taskResults.description: Run public WebGL2, DOM, input, asset and worker workloads remotely on default-flags chromium-automation, firefox-automation and webkit-automation projects. Use the separate chromium-gpu-headless project for native GPU probes. Keep software and experimental GPU flags in separately labeled projects.
taskResults.reason: The automation projects, GPU/software profiles, workload and remote commands exist. The example dev server now admits the runner's private external React 19 candidate with restricted package paths rather than rejecting all outside aliases. Consumer restoration remains blocked by execution custody/isolation; actual browser execution remains post-freeze and was not run.

taskResults.description: Capture the exact browser distribution and executable version, operating system, backend, adapter, driver where available, feature flags, fixture hash and test result. Record unsupported and skipped reasons explicitly. Automation builds do not by themselves establish retail-browser support.
taskResults.reason: The scenario records browser distribution/version, OS, selected WebGL2 observation, adapter/driver or reasons, fixture hash, and per-workload statuses/reasons; automation is distinguished from retail. It records only Aura3D-specified launch flags and explicitly marks the complete effective browser arguments unavailable, rather than capturing all effective flags required by the support policy. The remote spec also has the installed-path integration conflict noted at line 1967, and no current result was collected.

taskResults.description: Treat automated browser builds, retail browsers, software rendering, injected sessions and physical mobile/desktop devices as separate evidence. Do not claim a physical device from an emulator or spend on hardware automatically.
taskResults.reason: Documentation separates automation, retail, software, injection/emulation and physical evidence, and the acceptance plan grants no automatic hardware-spending permission. The evidence validator requires physical provenance and rejects several software/emulator markers, but its marker scan omits os.version and physicalProvenance.observedBy. An otherwise plausible physical record identifying an emulator only in os.version can therefore pass; provenance is also self-asserted rather than independently authenticated.

taskResults.description: Route browser-project forwarding and result/artifact transport through WP-20; document unverified cells without blocking the source freeze.
taskResults.reason: WP-20 validates and forwards the selected project, discovers/executes it, and transports hashed manifests, logs and artifacts with independent upload status; source reports allow unrun browser cells and documentation labels them unverified. End-to-end integration with the WP-22 scenario is broken: the task exports a restored /tmp consumer while the imported example server rejects installed aliases outside /repo, so discovery cannot reach the workload. The mock egress/source-phase tests do not demonstrate this combined path.

taskResults.description: Make the existing adapter's ready callback reflect successful renderer readiness; deliver cancellation/failure through a stable boundary and do not update unmounted components.
taskResults.reason: AuraCanvas waits for renderer-stage readiness before calling the latest committed onReady; non-ready outcomes go to onError or a render error boundary. Mount/revision guards and abort/disposal suppress late callbacks after unmount. Legacy ready()-only engines additionally require mounted WebGL2 diagnostics. Unit and packed-browser test sources exist, not a current passing receipt.

taskResults.description: Scope asset resources by effective loader, request/security context and digest; support independent subscribers, bounded ownership, eviction and retry after failure.
taskResults.reason: Lookup isolates the effective loader, explicit security-context identity, ordered descriptors and digests; signalled waiters cancel independently, failed loads can retry, and the lookup cache is limited to 128 entries. However, ordinary unsignalled read()/useAuraAsset() starts an unbounded interest before a suspended component can commit cleanup, and an owned entry can be evicted while its work continues; 128 bounds lookup entries, not active work. Current source newly accepts a signal on read/useAuraAsset, but that opt-in does not bound the default and its direct-read path has no identified test.

taskResults.description: Exercise both declared supported peer major versions, StrictMode double mounts, Suspense, error boundaries, prop updates, input and scene disposal using packed packages.
taskResults.reason: The authored browser harness requires separate installed React/react-dom 18 and 19 consumers, checks matching installed package hashes, and exercises a development StrictMode tree, Suspense, error boundaries, prop and pointer updates, and repeated app disposal. The remote runner restores candidate-bound consumers. This classifies the harness source only: neither peer's packed browser execution is claimed to have passed.

taskResults.description: Verify server-side import/render avoids DOM access, and hydrate a real client scene without duplicate render loops or leaked listeners/resources.
taskResults.reason: A fresh Node SSR fixture checks DOM-free imports/render and no preload, and the packed-browser source hydrates a real model scene while checking canvas reuse, duplicate frame callbacks, pointer listeners, animation-frame handles and disposal calls. Its dispose counter is installed only after onReady and it does not assert actual renderer/asset resource retirement or await asynchronous cleanup, so the requested no-resource-leak verification is incomplete. No real-client run or passing receipt was inspected.

taskResults.description: Compare every packed public subpath, runtime export, declaration, overload, generic constraint, union, optional field and module condition with the immediately preceding supported release.
taskResults.reason: The comparator reads packed declarations and bounded runtime JavaScript, compares static runtime exports, condition targets and ordering, and chooses the immediate predecessor within captured metadata. Exact null blockers and overlapping wildcard precedence are handled. Metadata origin/freshness and the exact candidate remain unverified.

taskResults.description: Replace fixed legacy baseline selection with explicit verified baseline manifest, candidate plan, release kind and output arguments. Read bounded previous-package declarations without installing/executing the runtime, and preserve prior published digests.
taskResults.reason: Explicit manifest, candidate, release kind and output flags feed verified registry metadata and digest-bound, size-bounded archives; old packages are parsed as data without installation or execution. Predecessor enforcement is a separate requirement.

taskResults.description: Reject undocumented incompatible changes for patch/minor releases; for the next planned major, provide explicit migration instructions and preserve the published deprecation policy.
taskResults.reason: Detected declaration and static runtime export removals, condition retargets and ordering breaks fail patch/minor; an explicit earliest removal version is respected. The required complete 5.0 per-change migration record and candidate-bound comparison remain open.

taskResults.description: Generate reference documentation from actual packed declarations and export conditions; make missing subpath documentation or a broken applicable snippet fail the checker.
taskResults.reason: Packed candidate collection, reference generation and fail-closed snippet checks exist, including conditional/directory exports. The checked-in public reference is explicitly a source inventory rather than the required packed candidate reference.

taskResults.description: Build every promised template and capability-family example from an isolated, untouched scaffold. The harness may substitute the candidate package only; it must report and fail on missing dependencies or skipped required checks.
taskResults.reason: The catalog discovers examples and rejects missing/skipped build checks, but capability projects are generated with new manifest/config/source rather than untouched scaffolds; clean-install source unconditionally aborts before installation, so templates cannot actually be built/retained by that producer.

taskResults.description: Split clean-install and consumer-matrix tools into source and browser phases. Retain untouched source-phase projects and candidate/tarball/project digests; source phase never starts a browser, and browser phase validates its source report before use. Never overwrite source results with acceptance outcomes.
taskResults.reason: Separate phase CLIs, report validation, hashes and output paths exist, but clean-install source always throws at the npm custody guard; matrix source always stops before the per-cell producer/report and both npm and pnpm browser restoration are guarded by unconditional throws.

taskResults.description: Verify plain JavaScript, supported TypeScript resolution modes, module conditions, SSR, workers, absent/present optional peers and both supported React peer majors. Declare only combinations actually tested.
taskResults.reason: Eight npm/pnpm × React 18/19 × optional-peer cells and JS, NodeNext, Bundler, SSR, condition, peer and worker probes exist; the source producer and browser restore cannot execute any matrix cells. Documentation correctly marks browser support and React adapter acceptance unverified.

taskResults.description: Update support policy, environment troubleshooting and template assets; verify offline neutral environment and explicit missing-asset errors without fabricating network success.
taskResults.reason: Policy, troubleshooting, packaged preset assets and a genuine-file offline/404 browser spec exist. The quickstart still recommends a neutral manifest contrary to the embedded loader, and the scaffold copy misses indirectly authored cinematic looks. The spec's portable restoration unconditionally aborts at the custody guard; no browser pass is claimed.

taskResults.description: Establish independently reproducible workloads for one primitive, product scene, dense instances, animation, a game loop, effects and asset import. Fix scene/asset hashes, seed, active look, quality, viewport, device pixel ratio, browser and backend.
taskResults.reason: Seven fixed workloads use the public engine path, fixed seed/look/quality/viewport/WebGL2 and source-bound scene definitions. The two model assets have declared digests, which matched their current files on read-only inspection. Each run records the selected browser, version and device identity; no browser session was audited.

taskResults.description: Run at least 3 independent sessions and 300 timed frames per session where the calibrated workload permits; retain p50/p95/p99 frame and CPU durations, startup/first drawable frame, requests, raw/gzip/Brotli bytes, allocations and live resource counts. If timing or hardware is unavailable, report no-data.
taskResults.reason: The gated probe is written to launch three independent browser processes per workload and retain 300 frames, timing percentiles, startup, requests, per-response raw/compressed estimates, GL allocations and live handles. Unsupported GPU timing and complete JS allocations are explicitly no-data. This WebGL2-only probe cannot establish WebGPU fence retirement. No current sessions or retained measurement manifest exist; the source-server byte estimates are not production wire or bundle sizes.

taskResults.description: Compare like-for-like runs on the same device against a versioned prior baseline. For each lower-is-better metric, take the median of the baseline session results as B and the median of candidate session results as C. Define relative baseline noise as the median absolute deviation of baseline session results from B, divided by B. Flag a regression when C/B - 1 exceeds the greater of 0.05 and twice that noise. For a zero or unavailable baseline, report no-data and use a separately defined absolute bound if one exists. Rerun once if the environment is noisy; if it remains inconclusive, do not manufacture a pass.
taskResults.reason: The analyzer checks same workload/device identity, independent sessions, medians and the specified baseline-MAD threshold; it keeps zero/missing data and persistent noise from becoming a pass. Reruns must be collected and supplied separately, with no automatic rerun orchestration or retained same-device baseline. Moreover the real probe always sets several metrics to null while the aggregate requires every metric, so that probe alone cannot yield an aggregate pass.

taskResults.description: Reproduce and meet the repository's existing gzip budgets: 190,000 bytes for the core critical path, 250,000 for the product starter, 400,000 for the cinematic starter and 480,000 for the mini-game starter. The checked-in overages are historical measurements; rerun before claiming current values. Do not raise budgets to pass.
taskResults.reason: All four stated gzip caps are present and continuity-guarded. The published table and retained bundle report are explicitly historical, with old overages; they do not establish whether the current working candidate meets the caps. No current candidate-bound budget result was found.

taskResults.description: Make installed tree-shaking consume an explicitly selected current source-consumer report, validate package/project hashes and fail stale input without requiring an earlier browser receipt.
taskResults.reason: The tree-shaking command requires an explicit source report and candidate, validates identities and checks installed-slice contributions without a browser receipt. However the real source-report producer and portable project restore both call an unconditional NPM_INSTALL_CUSTODY_UNAVAILABLE throw, so no real candidate can presently reach the measurement. The top-level check:release also invokes the newly required command without --source-report.

taskResults.description: Measure actual memory residency and resource release, not ledger counters alone. Preserve visual quality and rerun the relevant pixel checks when a performance change alters the render path.
taskResults.reason: The probe observes WebGL create/delete calls before and after disposal rather than only renderer ledger counters, but cannot measure actual GPU-resident bytes. A focused mock probe confirms ResourceLifecycle and interop retain borrowed-device leases until a fence passes or confirmed invalidation after failure. No current residency or changed-render-path pixel receipt is retained; existing immediate-completion fence assertions conflict with current behavior.

taskResults.description: Use genuine asynchronous device timers where supported; report CPU timings separately and never substitute them for GPU measurements.
taskResults.reason: WebGL2 uses nonblocking elapsed-query polling and rejects unavailable, disjoint or lost results; WebGPU has an opt-in asynchronous selected-forward-pass timestamp bridge. CPU wall samples remain separately labeled and never substitute for GPU samples. Failed WebGPU submissions are labeled query-failed and query resources are retained for a fence or confirmed loss. The tests are unrun mock/source tests, not a live-device receipt.

taskResults.description: Support admitted licensed fonts, Unicode shaping, kerning, ligatures, right-to-left scripts, fallback glyphs, multiline wrapping and dynamic atlas updates with bounded allocation.
taskResults.reason: The public loader, platform run shaping, fallback and bounded wrapping exist, but a loaded font is rasterized into temporary per-line runs and optional shared whole-label snapshots, not a retained, dynamically updated glyph atlas. Wrapping through an open bidi scope is rejected; font coverage is platform-dependent.

taskResults.description: Preserve the built-in small-glyph fallback; expose an accessible DOM counterpart and dispose glyph/texture resources after final use.
taskResults.reason: The small built-in glyph catalog and extruded/SDF fallback remain; text defaults to an accessible DOM note and compiled geometry, textures and atlas leases are retired. The note can be disabled, an OffscreenCanvas has no DOM layer, and font handles are caller-owned; browser acceptance was not run.

taskResults.description: Complete wide/dashed line widths in world and screen units, per-vertex gradients, segment continuity, pixel-ratio/resize behavior, alpha and clipping; return a stable error for any unsupported combination.
taskResults.reason: Screen/world-width lines, gradients, continuous transformed dash distances, resolution updates, alpha and clipped variants are wired. Builders and compiler now reject gapSize/dashOffset without dashing using coded errors. Complete diagnostic and rendered-output verification remains open.

taskResults.description: Update actual line storage in Geometry.ts, preserving LineGeometry.ts's re-export. Same-capacity edits reuse GPU buffers; growth releases replaced buffers. Test changing positions/colors/distances, bounds and allocation counts over repeated updates and final disposal.
taskResults.reason: The real Geometry implementation and its public re-export update within capacity and retire superseded buffers on growth. The existing counting-device test checks changed positions, colors, distances, bounds, repeated reuse, growth and final disposal; its existence is not a test pass.

taskResults.description: Apply custom materials to supported imported model slots while preserving variants, textures, shadows, morphs, skinning and instances. Implement model LOD/collider options; reject only specified unsupported variants and never accept and ignore a setting.
taskResults.reason: Imported LOD and PBR overrides are wired and custom materials replace render items, but custom shaders do not select individual imported slots and textured authored materials and custom-plus-variant are rejected; certified graph skinning has restricted admission. Bounds colliders ignore the model scale and default to unit bounds if asset bounds are missing. The named collider test checks the descriptor, not collision behavior.

taskResults.description: Request existing geometry and public type changes from their WP-01/WP-19 owners; verify source, pixel output, interaction and resource teardown.
taskResults.reason: Geometry and public types plus source and browser test definitions exist, but no inspected record establishes the requests to WP-01/WP-19 owners or a candidate-bound source run. The browser spec defines pixel checks but does not assert pointer/keyboard interaction; no pixel or interaction acceptance was run.

taskResults.description: Complete and test supported primitive, convex, static-mesh and heightfield collision; fixed/hinge/spring/motor joints; contact/sensor/layer queries; deterministic stepping and continuous collision.
taskResults.reason: The public Rapier-backed world implements validated primitives, convex hulls, static meshes and heightfields, the requested joints, contacts, sensors and filtered queries, repeatable fixed stepping and native/bounded-substep CCD. Existing numerical source tests cover these paths; they were not run. Plane, mesh and heightfield are static-only and adaptive CCD may reject its substep budget.

taskResults.description: Verify scene/physics synchronization with parent transforms, multiple worlds, character/vehicle reset and teardown. Report unsupported backend or shape combinations explicitly.
taskResults.reason: Parent-affine synchronization and cross-world ownership have source tests; a public-world test covers a held vehicle across world reset and a lower-level character resetTo is tested. Although root reset reconstructs both controller kinds, a corresponding public-world test for a held character surviving world reset was not found. Unsupported backends, non-static terrain, shear and reflection are explicitly rejected.

taskResults.description: Keep the full game entrypoint working and cycle-free. Replace the ambiguous root headless behavior with an actionable, versioned migration error; do not re-export through a dependency cycle.
taskResults.reason: The root exports the versioned throwing migration contract, not a reverse re-export of the full game, and the game subpath installs its own implementation; both migration tests now match that contract. However the full entry still exposes no-op loading-progress/track shell methods, and the agent boundary documentation incorrectly says the root only logs once and returns a headless stub.

taskResults.description: Validate installed games with manual keyboard and touch, HUD, audio/effects, pause/reset, replay and cleanup. Promote only features backed by the applicable root or subpath evidence.
taskResults.reason: The installed-consumer browser fixture exercises the requested categories using scripted keyboard and synthetic touch, but the requested manual installed-game/device validation and a matching frozen-candidate receipt were not supplied or run. The fixture is not evidence of a manual pass.

taskResults.description: Build a versioned, independently licensed fixture manifest with content digest, origin, format version, extension combinations, expected numerical/visual output, limits and license.
taskResults.reason: The version-1 manifest contains 21 fixture records with authorship, MIT or CC0 license, byte digest, format version, used/required extensions, independent expected geometry, pixels or rejection, and limits. It is a bounded corpus, not evidence for every format variant; its conformance test has not been run for this audit.

taskResults.description: Run actual decode, resource creation, root rendering and disposal for each supported claimed variant. A file classification, parser return or metadata-only test is not enough.
taskResults.reason: Source tests load and create/dispose resources for selected glTF, ETC1S and mesh fixtures, and the maturity spec attempts root rendering and device cleanup. Its createAuraApp call omits formatRegistry, so the root validator rejects the OBJ, PLY, STL and 3MF cases before loading. A separate packed-import spec registers these adapters and renders them, but uses loadRenderableAsset and Renderer rather than the root app. The manifest also omits claimed Draco and Meshopt variants, and no matching current-candidate root-render receipt was found.

taskResults.description: Cover nested external dependencies, invalid required/optional extensions, corrupt/truncated files, archive expansion, strict/fallback texture failures, byte integrity and independently verified export round trips.
taskResults.reason: Conformance tests cover nested buffers/images, unknown optional and required extensions, truncated inputs, archive expansion, strict/fallback texture failure and altered document/dependency hashes. Independent readers are authored for OBJ/MTL, STL, KTX2 and a glTF instancing accessor. The edited glTF scene round trip reloads with Aura's own loader, and no current-candidate passing independent-reader round-trip result was found; broader export semantics therefore remain unestablished.

taskResults.description: Verify the texture budget against returned CPU bytes and live device residency, including same-name textures on separate devices, eviction and release.
taskResults.reason: The current budget implementation partitions ledgers by device and records actual returned mip allocation sizes; unit suites cover CPU bytes, duplicate labels, release and simulated eviction. Their WebGL and WebGPU devices are recorders rather than live GPUs. The browser streaming spec covers funded/starved telemetry but not the complete two-device, same-name, eviction and release matrix. An older pre-integration budget run reported 8 failures in 9 tests and is not a result for the current mutable source.

taskResults.description: Keep unavailable assets, devices and formats visibly unverified rather than silently skipping them.
taskResults.reason: The manifest explicitly inventories unverified formats, the documentation labels each targeted render and physical-device/browser combination unverified, and the browser spec attaches the inventory and throws for missing fixtures or unavailable WebGL2 rather than silently skipping. This disposition does not constitute a device or rendering pass.

taskResults.description: Enumerate every workspace manifest, direct/dev/peer/optional dependency, alias, override, lock snapshot and peer edge; remove all external 3D-engine dependencies from required installs and published runtimes.
taskResults.reason: The untracked graph collector inventories workspace manifests, dependency fields, overrides, pnpm snapshots, peer bindings and supplied package payloads; synthetic cases exist. The root manifest and lock no longer name the historical three dependency, but active scaffold profiles without locks have no complete transitive graph and no current candidate-bound packed-runtime audit was found. A private standalone showcase still declares three, but it is outside the workspace and was not established to be a required install.

taskResults.description: Inspect source, generated artifacts, source maps, encoded tables, workers, binary payloads, packed packages and actual runtime network requests. Test synthetic direct/transitive/aliased/optional/peer cases and a clean offline consumer.
taskResults.reason: Source, map, encoded-data and payload scanners and synthetic graph and network tests exist. The source CLI now includes the root public and fixtures trees in its configured paths. The offline browser specification exists, but packed-consumer restoration still reaches an unconditional execution-readiness refusal; no current candidate-bound archive scan or actual runtime network observation was found.

taskResults.description: Record per-file hash, source kind, license, owner, replacement status and review evidence in the WP-00 capability ledger. Coordinate already assigned source rewrites with their owning WPs.
taskResults.reason: The scanner can accept digest-bound owner, license, replacement status and review evidence, and the ledger records some ownership coordination. The WP-29 provenance row has no evidence or provenance entries; its four historical G27 records do not contain the complete required fields, and the recorded hashes for ShapeUtils, ConvexHull and OBB no longer match those current files. Complete per-file review and coordination are not established.

taskResults.description: Treat textual references, standardized equations and fingerprint hits as review candidates, not automatic proof of copied implementation. A scanner alone cannot prove independent authorship.
taskResults.reason: Text and supplied fingerprint matches are explicitly review candidates rather than proof, and tests include false positives; the source report never establishes independence. There is no explicit standardized-equation review classification in the scanner, and complete current human review of equation and other candidates is not recorded in the ledger.

taskResults.description: Keep existing license/copyright notices until corresponding material has actually been independently replaced. Convert tests and goldens to independently authored or appropriately licensed open-standard fixtures without reducing behavior coverage.
taskResults.reason: The distributed reference-following mutable math entry retains its MIT notice, and the tangent test uses a separately licensed codec and analytic fixtures. Reference-generated math and shader goldens still remain. The rewritten UV fixture expects the opposite rotation direction from the current implementation, so its independent expectation is not integrated with the current contract; preservation of all notices and equivalent coverage has not been established.

taskResults.description: Implement section 3.7 clipping through root scene/material APIs, compiler, graph, forward, depth and shadow paths. Define local/global composition, retained half-spaces, invalid-plane errors and supported mesh/line/point/sprite semantics.
taskResults.reason: Live global/material groups, compiler snapshots and certified graph/generated shaders are wired; arbitrary custom shaders and packed draws fail closed, while clipped points, wide lines and sprites lack depth/shadow submission.

taskResults.description: Add physical film/focal-length perspective controls and tiled/asymmetric view offsets. Define precedence when FOV and focal length are both supplied; preserve current defaults and distinguish camera projection from depth-of-field effect settings.
taskResults.reason: Root and scene cameras implement film gauge, focal length, lens shift and tiled full-image frusta; focal length wins over authored FOV, existing defaults remain, and DoF is a separate effect.

taskResults.description: Implement standard/reversed/logarithmic depth as explicit negotiated conventions. Carry clip range, projection/inverse, compare/clear, bias and reconstruction consistently; validate perspective/orthographic near/far independently and support infinite far only where the declared mode allows it.
taskResults.reason: Math supports multiple conventions and far-plane validation. Production does not implement reversed/logarithmic rendering, but an explicit allowFallback now negotiates standard depth and rebuilds the projection. Root orthographic/isometric builders pass their modes to validation, accepting valid zero/signed near planes and rejecting infinite far. A focused source probe confirmed these cases; nonstandard production depth and candidate verification remain open.

taskResults.description: Coordinate shadows, culling, query reconstruction, multi-view, fog, AO/reflections/depth-of-field, temporal histories and readback with their owners. Never infer every projection from conventional finite matrix coefficients.
taskResults.reason: FrameGraph carries projection/inverse and explicit metadata, with frame-scoped temporal histories and shadow camera propagation. Only standard depth reaches production; specialized clipped depth and arbitrary custom materials fail closed. A focused mock probe confirms ResourceLifecycle retains a borrowed device while its fence waits or fails; broader effect and device coverage remains unverified.

taskResults.description: Test near/far mapping, large depth ranges, tiled seams, clipping transforms, animated/instanced geometry, target changes, depth-aware effects and unsupported-device fallback through source and packed-browser paths.
taskResults.reason: Unit and packed-root browser specifications cover projection, clipping, deformation, effects and resize, and separate mock-queue specifications cover target teardown and later fence failure. The current orthographic builders accept near 0 and explicit production fallback is supported, although existing preflight tests still expect fallback to throw. The specifications were not run for this checkpoint.

taskResults.description: Implement every supported depth/stencil/blend/color-mask/cull/winding/offset/sample field in each device; distinguish dynamic state from pipeline state and include all relevant attachment/layout/feature fields in cache identity.
taskResults.reason: WebGL applies and restores extensive per-draw state, and WebGPU keys fixed state separately from dynamic scissor, blend constant and stencil reference. The material/pipeline API cannot express all command-state fields; WebGL rejects independent attachment state, partial sample masks and offset clamps, and generated WebGPU materials reject alpha-to-coverage.

taskResults.description: Connect normalized/integer/interleaved/multiple-stream/per-instance vertex layouts to actual buffer slots, shader inputs and draws. Test values and pixels, not only descriptors.
taskResults.reason: Typed stream descriptors, byte-preserving buffers and actual GL/GPU slot bindings are wired through forward submission, with explicit backend limits. Unit specifications inspect integer and normalized values, and the browser fixture exercises normalized instance pixels, but an integer shader-input pixel specification was not found and no pixels were run.

taskResults.description: Preserve stable opaque/masked/transmissive/transparent ordering and explicit render ordering. Implement weighted accumulation/revealage and composition with defined alpha/depth/MSAA rules, capability limits and sorted fallback.
taskResults.reason: A stable sorter and weighted accumulation/revealage, sampled opaque depth, composition, capability gates and sorted fallback exist. Current forward source routes non-blended, non-transmissive cutouts to the distinct mask bucket using their live material or instance cutoff; an offline probe and two selected existing checks passed. Split renderer phases still impose bucket order across renderOrder values. The renderer's weighted integration excludes WebGPU and multi-view frames and only admits bounded generated unlit WebGL2 alpha triangles; no pixel acceptance is claimed.

taskResults.description: Test intersecting transparent layers under different submission orders, opaque occluders, premultiplied alpha, multisampling, views and teardown. Document weighted transparency's approximation and keep refraction/dispersion in their own supported path.
taskResults.reason: A browser specification covers permuted intersections, opaque occlusion, premultiplied inputs, view resources and teardown, and documentation describes the approximation and bounded fallback. It drives the lower-level pass, supplies its own WebGPU weighted shader and injects transmission fallback rather than testing actual renderer transmission; its MSAA case requests fallback on a single-sample target. Separately, WebGPU interop retains a failed-fence lease, but a ResourceLifecycle may already have completed before that asynchronous failure; the new source specification explicitly documents this boundary. No browser/device or unit test run is claimed.

taskResults.description: Integrate clipping/depth/output into program generation and warmup; a change in shader-affecting state must select the correct variant, while ordinary uniform edits must not cause needless recompilation.
taskResults.reason: Generated clipping and output bits, normalized structural keys and clipping/output warmup are present, with plane and camera values kept as uniforms. The forward selector does not derive log depth from the active convention, the renderer rejects nonstandard depth, and generated depth variants are explicitly excluded from warmup. Complete graph/depth variants and no-recompile behavior are not established for all paths.

taskResults.description: Implement shared scene-referred color transforms with extended-range linear identity, independently derived primary conversion and explicit tone/gamut/output stages. Preserve existing normalized helpers through a versioned contract where necessary.
taskResults.reason: The exported managed API retains finite extended linear values, derives primary matrices from chromaticities and provides explicit tone, gamut and output transfer stages. The older normalized/clamped helpers remain separate.

taskResults.description: Support requested sRGB and Display-P3 output when the context supports them; report active output/fallback and distinguish float rendering, wide gamut and physical HDR display evidence. Keep colorless maps linear and alpha handling consistent.
taskResults.reason: Both devices negotiate output and the public renderer label reports active color or unknown; the visual report separates float, gamut and physical HDR. Current app output diagnostics include the negotiated colorSpace fallback object in a source probe. WebGPU restricts P3 to opaque unorm canvases; packed-browser and display behavior remain unverified.

taskResults.description: Preserve existing video polling, canvas uploads and data subregion updates. Extend only gaps demonstrated in the declared 3D/layer/mip/media contract; keep correct source lifetime, orientation, dimensions, color metadata and storage reuse.
taskResults.reason: Video polling, canvas uploads, retained 2D/array and CPU-authoritative 3D regions, full mips and borrowed-source cleanup exist; WebGPU retires native textures behind fences. Compressed fallback handling and source dimension preflight have source implementations, but full device/browser coverage remains unverified. A focused mock probe confirms a borrowed-device ResourceLifecycle retains ownership through pending and failed fences; existing immediate-completion assertions conflict.

taskResults.description: Verify known color vectors, HDR values above one and below zero, output readback, layered/mip update isolation, changing media frames, compressed-block validation and final cleanup on supported backends.
taskResults.reason: Test source covers vectors, HDR, readback, subresources, media and blocks. The current output collector supplies the formerly missing colorSpace diagnostic, but its packed P3 fixture is WebGL2-only and browser evidence is unrun. The dynamic browser fixture counts logical WebGPU resources without observing native handles. A focused mock shows fence ownership retained through waiting and rejection; conflicting legacy assertions and real-device lifecycle coverage remain open.

outcomeResults.description: Create the ledger named in WP-00 with one row per concrete user-observable capability, format variant, option and backend. Include G01–G55 and every specific item named in WP-01–WP-32.
outcomeResults.reason: The ledger contains 1,901 outcome IDs, all 55 gap references and WP-00–WP-32 ownership, but the G04 row bundles multiple observable behaviors and leaves options and backends empty. Only two outcomes populate option arrays and two populate backend arrays; the public filmGauge and filmOffset fields are not individually named outcomes. The reported nine-test structural run is unbound and cannot prove exhaustive enumeration.

outcomeResults.description: For each row record: stable ID; category; priority; root/package/internal exposure; current status; Aura3D source path and symbol; desired behavior; owning WP; implementation files; relevant tests; backend/device limits; and evidence link.
outcomeResults.reason: Stable IDs, priorities, owners, status and generic limitations are recorded, with some more specific entries. G01 now has implementation and source evidence details. No outcome has a category or explicit exposure field; only 23 have symbols, 22 public entrypoints and two backends. The 26 outcomes with source-evidence entries have no candidate run IDs.

outcomeResults.description: Recheck every “not found” or “unverified” row against source, public exports, installed package and existing tests. Merge semantically identical rows; do not infer behavior from names.
outcomeResults.reason: The ledger contains source observations, but 1,848 rows remain unverified and a comprehensive recheck, installed-package comparison and semantic reconciliation are not established. G01 now records the source implementation and four focused passing checks on the mutable tree. The ignored local distribution is not candidate-bound installed-package evidence.

outcomeResults.description: Break any newly discovered option or feature into a named row with exact file actions and acceptance. Do not mark the program complete while a row is unowned, untriaged, implemented only as a placeholder, or has missing required evidence.
outcomeResults.reason: Ownership entries name new files, the gate checks every ledger outcome for ownership, completion, details and checks, and no global go has been issued. G01 now records file actions and a focused check. The coverage obligation remains incomplete, including individually inventoried camera film options. Synthetic gate tests cannot establish exhaustive discovery.

outcomeResults.description: For each public capability, track the exact package/subpath, backend, version, asset format, browser/OS/device class, known limitations and evidence level in the WP-00 ledger. A capability can be **source-tested**, **browser-tested on software**, **browser-tested on hardware**, **device-tested**, **unsupported**, or **unverified**; do not promote one level into another. Desktop browser-family coverage, mobile browsers, native GPU and physical spatial devices are separate cells. A missing physical device receipt is an explicit acceptance limitation, not a fabricated pass or a blocker to freezing completed source work.
outcomeResults.reason: The ledger distinguishes source and not-run acceptance, and a few rows describe backend-specific limitations. It does not provide the required per-capability package/subpath, version, format, browser/OS/device and distinct evidence-level cells: only 22 outcomes have public entrypoints and two have backends. The earlier ledger-test result is an unbound structural observation. No physical-device pass is inferred or required to freeze completed source work.

outcomeResults.description: Record each capability, implementation ownership, status, public API, tests, limitations and evidence. WP-00 owns this file for the entire program; WP-18 supplies documentation updates through WP-00.
outcomeResults.reason: The WP-00 ledger records ownership, descriptions and some file/test references. G01 now has those source details and unbound focused-check evidence, but most capabilities still lack complete implementation, API, limits and evidence. The ledger contract test is structural and its earlier pass is not candidate-bound.

outcomeResults.description: Complete the capability ledger in WP-00; enumerate every public capability and option, map it to an existing implementation or a named work package, and close every row with executable evidence.
outcomeResults.reason: The G26 row and owner mappings exist, and a small number of outcomes have source observations. The complete public capability/option inventory and closure with executable evidence are not established: only two outcomes populate options, 1,007 contain an owner-triage check instruction, all 1,901 have incomplete source completion, and their ledger checks are not-run. These are ledger state counts, not a claim that no product implementation exists.

outcomeResults.description: Every supported option must produce its documented observable behavior or a stable actionable error. Compile-only success, a counter change, parsing metadata, an opaque canvas, or a mock device alone does not establish a visual or hardware claim.
outcomeResults.reason: Some public options do reach real source consumers: perspective lens fields are preserved and used in projection, with focused tests. However, camera.perspective accepts the publicly typed roll field, documented as diagnostic-only, but silently drops it before any diagnostic; the renderer's single-view matrix path hard-codes the up vector. The curated option-discovery rule excludes the camera namespace, so its existing tests cannot establish the universal behavior-or-actionable-error contract. No rendered or hardware result is claimed.

outcomeResults.description: Keep the existing bounds behavior available for callers that depend on it. Mesh mode accounts for world transforms, geometry topology, material side, skinning, morphs and instancing. Near/far, layer masks, stable nearest-first ordering, missing geometry, degenerate triangles and disposed nodes have defined behavior.
outcomeResults.reason: Bounds and mesh paths, transforms, deformation, filters, sorting and disposed/missing handling exist. The declarative mesh path, however, does not match production culling for transparent materials and planes, and refuses all custom-shader geometry, so the full material-side/render correspondence is not established.

outcomeResults.description: indexed
outcomeResults.reason: Explicit index streams are range-validated and width-selected, compiled to an index buffer, and consumed by triangle queries. Existing indexed-query and geometry tests were not run.

outcomeResults.description: two-bone
outcomeResults.reason: Two-bone IK rotation solver is exported in the animation lane and dispatched by the actor pose-constraint path; the focused reachable/unreachable and blending tests exist but were not run.

outcomeResults.description: normalization
outcomeResults.reason: Integer custom attributes are decoded with signed/unsigned normalization and explicit stride/offset validation; normalized floating-point data is rejected, and compatible layouts reach production buffers. Focused tests exist.

outcomeResults.description: integrate triangle/BVH intersection and live geometry, including skinning, morphs, instances, UV/barycentric data, sidedness, near/far and layers.
outcomeResults.reason: Contrary to the older checkpoint, static scene queries now call the real cached BVH; live skin/morph geometry uses the triangle scan and supports instances, UVs, barycentrics and filters. Declarative plane/transparent sidedness differs from the renderer, and custom shaders are excluded rather than queried.

outcomeResults.description: Preserve default-origin, disposed batch and typed attribute geometry query correctness. Exclusive execution owner: wp01_geometry. Source verification: tests/unit/engine/scene-queries.test.ts; tests/unit/agent-api/scene-query-mesh.test.ts.
outcomeResults.reason: The grouped references are present: default-origin and disposed-batch queries with typed decoded streams, independently derived transform/graph fixtures, and fixed 0/1/2 morph slots with an empty normal slot for tangent-only packing. The packed-data tests cover combinations, vertices, layers and formats. No test was run.

outcomeResults.description: Expose typed attribute layout, normalized/interleaved data, update ranges and safe geometry operations.
outcomeResults.reason: Public geometry authoring exposes typed custom attributes, normalization, stride/offset, safe merge/deindex operations and runtime update ranges; validation rejects unsupported layouts and names. Tests exist, not a current-source pass receipt.

outcomeResults.description: Exact ray
outcomeResults.reason: Public exact triangle rays produce world hit data and use a BVH for eligible persistent geometry. They fail closed for custom shaders, even simple non-deforming shaders, and the declarative side decision can disagree with rendered plane/transparent materials.

outcomeResults.description: Invalidate position-derived bounds after edits; verify an object moved outside its original bounds stays visible.
outcomeResults.reason: Position edits clear old authored bounds and refresh live render bounds; an installed-app test contains visible-movement and culling assertions. Visual acceptance is not run, and unrelated pointer/slot-reuse assertions in that same test suite contradict the current implementation.

outcomeResults.description: batched
outcomeResults.reason: Batched geometry is rendered and queried with per-member transforms, visibility and disposal. After slot reuse, however, query lifetime IDs differ from packed-loop batchMemberId and from public mutation slot indices, so member identity is not consistently integrated across paths.

outcomeResults.description: mesh compression helpers
outcomeResults.reason: CLI asset optimization can encode meshopt-compressed GLBs and asset loaders have Draco/meshopt decoder adapters. A general runtime geometry compression encoder/helper, as implied by the runtime-tools checklist, was not established in the inspected public geometry API.

outcomeResults.description: Consume bounds invalidation and updated attribute layouts on the render path.
outcomeResults.reason: Production geometry builds typed custom layouts and uploads their values, while the dynamic resource path consumes attribute updates and refreshes bounds after position changes. Tests include normalization, dirty ranges and bounds; none were run.

outcomeResults.description: Invalidate position-derived bounds after edits
outcomeResults.reason: Position-attribute updates remove old authored bounds from CPU query state and cause a fresh bounds calculation on the live geometry resource; focused partial-edit assertions exist.

outcomeResults.description: animation bounds
outcomeResults.reason: Rendering bounds include weighted morphs and skin palettes and transform the result for instances; the joint-box path tracks live palette and geometry state. Arbitrary shader displacement is not covered. Existing source tests were not run.

outcomeResults.description: Compose transforms, include default-origin nodes, preserve bounds mode and implement mesh-mode query/hit semantics.
outcomeResults.reason: Hierarchical transforms, bounds/mesh modes, authored batch source identity and finalized model/primitive render-item handoff are implemented; reuse tests cover ancestor movement and draw ranges. Declarative sidedness/custom-shader picking and packed-versus-query member identity remain inconsistent.

outcomeResults.description: iterative IK
outcomeResults.reason: CCD iterative IK is exported in the animation lane and dispatched as an actor pose constraint. Source tests cover convergence, limits, unreachable targets and zero weight; no execution was performed.

outcomeResults.description: deindexing
outcomeResults.reason: Public deindex expands indexed built-in, custom and morph channels, preserving draw metadata and rejecting incomplete topology or unsupported fields. Existing tests check actual expanded values.

outcomeResults.description: Correct transforms; preserve topology, groups, attributes and morphs or reject incompatible inputs explicitly.
outcomeResults.reason: The confirmed geometry gap is addressed by inverse-transpose normals and validated merge/deindex paths that preserve supported topology, groups and streams or reject incompatible data. This is source inspection, not a passing test result.

outcomeResults.description: bounds
outcomeResults.reason: Runtime bounds use live primitive positions and loaded model evidence when available, with declared-model and unit-box fallbacks. General scene bounds are not necessarily exact for animated objects or custom-shader displacement, and undersized authored custom-geometry bounds are accepted.

outcomeResults.description: Make merge and deindex operations preserve or explicitly reject every attribute, morph, group, draw range and topology
outcomeResults.reason: Deindex and merge preserve supported attributes, morphs, groups, topology and representable ranges, with explicit rejection of unknown and incompatible streams and disjoint ranges. Existing tests cover those contracts.

outcomeResults.description: update ranges
outcomeResults.reason: Public attribute updates validate offset and ranges, copy caller input, synchronize to live vertex storage and dirty the changed range. Tests for partial integer and float writes exist.

outcomeResults.description: deformed meshes
outcomeResults.reason: Mesh queries use live morph weights and skin palettes, including multi-stream attributes, but fail closed on arbitrary custom vertex programs and instance attributes that may displace vertices. Tests exist; deformation coverage is not universal.

outcomeResults.description: Make merge and deindex operations preserve or explicitly reject every attribute, morph, group, draw range and topology; never return silently corrupted geometry.
outcomeResults.reason: Supported streams are expanded or concatenated with groups and compatible draw ranges; incompatible stream layouts, morph channels, unknown fields and disconnected draw intervals throw instead of being silently dropped.

outcomeResults.description: Recompute/invalidate culling bounds and verify visibly moving geometry.
outcomeResults.reason: Live position writes invalidate and recompute culling bounds; an authored installed-app browser test asserts a previously offscreen triangle becomes visible. Visual acceptance is not run, and other assertions in that same suite need reconciliation with current query behavior.

outcomeResults.description: Add accurate mesh/instance/deformed-geometry hits with world transforms, UVs, face data, side rules and deterministic ordering.
outcomeResults.reason: Submitted mesh/instance morph and skin data, world transforms, UVs, face information and ordering are queried. Declarative sidedness does not match rendered transparent/plane materials, and custom-shader deformation cannot be evaluated.

outcomeResults.description: Skeleton hierarchies, bind/inverse matrices, skinned rendering, morph targets, facial controls, procedural poses, two-bone and iterative IK, animation bounds and disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: Skeleton palettes, skinned/morph render paths, actor pose and named morph controls, two-bone/CCD constraints, animation bounds and cleanup have concrete implementations. Complete facial-control/procedural-pose variants and all lifecycle interactions are not established from the inspected paths.

outcomeResults.description: Skeleton hierarchies
outcomeResults.reason: Skeleton construction validates parent order; world matrices compose parent/local transforms and palette matrices multiply world by inverse bind. Binding tests exist.

outcomeResults.description: Invalidate updated position bounds and expose live runtime mesh/instance/deformation data to queries.
outcomeResults.reason: Runtime position bounds and live submitted mesh/instance/deformation handoff are implemented. The specifically required native-batched-loop source file asserts captured IDs, ranges and transforms but only attaches a callback; it does not assert callback dispatch or fallback. Companion renderer tests cover those behaviors, but do not satisfy the named file's full stated coverage.

outcomeResults.description: Test exact triangles, hierarchy, instances, morphs, skinning and filtering.
outcomeResults.reason: The specified test file contains assertions for exact triangle/UV/barycentric hits, parent transforms, instances, morphs, skinning and filters. Existence of those tests is not an execution result.

outcomeResults.description: transform
outcomeResults.reason: TransformControls has interactive gizmo picking, constrained drag, cancellation and idempotent disposal. It owns no DOM listeners; pointer capture, touch, keyboard and focus routing must be integrated by the caller, so the full checklist is not provided by this control alone.

outcomeResults.description: triangles
outcomeResults.reason: The public math entry exports Triangle, including normals, barycentric operations and robust closest-point handling; a focused public-entry test exists.

outcomeResults.description: mesh primitives
outcomeResults.reason: The public geometry namespace creates custom meshes, and production geometry dispatch constructs triangle, line and point topologies with validated streams and indices. Relevant geometry regressions exist.

outcomeResults.description: Add index, transform, merge, morph, attribute and bounds regressions.
outcomeResults.reason: The requested source test contains regressions for index width, affine transforms, merge/deindex, morphs, attributes and bounds. It exists in the working tree but was not executed.

outcomeResults.description: Apply inverse-transpose normal transforms, including nonuniform scale, shear, negative determinant and singular-matrix errors.
outcomeResults.reason: Normal transforms use the inverse-transpose and reject singular matrices when normals are present; the named fixture independently checks shear, nonuniform scale, reflection and the error.

outcomeResults.description: Fix index selection at 65,535/65,536/65,537 boundaries and verify indexed/non-indexed meshes.
outcomeResults.reason: Index-width synthesis changes after 65,536 vertices, explicit numeric indices use their maximum, and source tests cover 65,535/65,536/65,537 and both indexed and non-indexed paths.

outcomeResults.description: interleaving
outcomeResults.reason: Public geometry inputs accept interleaved typed custom attributes with validated component stride/offset. Internal interleave/deinterleave utilities also validate storage and layout; their standalone root export was not established. Tests cover nonzero offsets and normalized inputs.

outcomeResults.description: non-indexed

outcomeResults.reason: Explicit WebGPU root selection awaits and validates a native device and routes scene frames to it; the backend remains experimental pending acceptance.

outcomeResults.description: test cancellation, target/layout-dependent cache identity and device-generation disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: Separate tests cover render-state target/layout/generation key differences and program-cache cancellation on loss/disposal. No complete test of cancellable render and compute variant warmup with those identities and generation disposal was located; the corresponding coordinated warmup is not implemented. Another test documents, rather than fixes, premature parent completion if a borrowed-device fence later rejects.

outcomeResults.description: Test selection, fallback, feature errors, loss/recovery and resource lifetime.
outcomeResults.reason: The named unit suite contains feature/limit forwarding, owned and borrowed initialization cleanup, loss/recovery, interop lifetime, and root selection/fallback checks. A separate fence test explicitly records the remaining late-rejection parent-completion behavior. Test existence is not a passing result or proof that this gap is fixed.

outcomeResults.description: batching
outcomeResults.reason: Forward collection supports static batching and mesh consolidation; incompatible alternate paths explicitly fail or fall back to forward.

outcomeResults.description: Supported native GPU scene rendering, compute interop, backend diagnostics, fallback, recovery and disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: The supported opt-in subset has native scene submission, selected-device compute interop, diagnostics, explicit fallback, loss recovery and disposal paths. On a borrowed device, ResourceLifecycle can declare disposal complete before a waiting fence later rejects; interop keeps the lease, but the parent cannot automatically resume its ownership or report the failure. Experimental support and unrun device/pixel acceptance remain separate.

outcomeResults.description: explicit fallback
outcomeResults.reason: WebGPU-to-WebGL2 fallback is gated by allowFallback, with auto itself opting in; native drawing-path fallback is also explicitly gated and records its reason.

outcomeResults.description: clustered lighting plus independently implemented deferred
outcomeResults.reason: Forward resolves clustered lighting and generated native PBR emits clustered lookup; deferred is a separate G-buffer and resolve path with restricted admission and explicit fallback.

outcomeResults.description: WebGL2
outcomeResults.reason: WebGL2 is the default root intent and the device factory constructs its WebGL2 implementation; native WebGPU is a separate explicit selection.

outcomeResults.description: verify WebGL2 fallback only when explicitly allowed.
outcomeResults.reason: The named source test asserts default WebGL2, strict explicit WebGPU failure and authorized auto fallback; it has not been run for this audit.

outcomeResults.description: device/context loss
outcomeResults.reason: On confirmed native loss the observer invalidates the device generation; on a rejected loss promise it conservatively retires behind fences rather than assuming invalidation. The root reports loss, retires compute and attempts a single remount; WebGL has a context-restoration route.

outcomeResults.description: capability negotiation
outcomeResults.reason: The WebGPU device validates adapter features and limits and root selection also requires native pipeline and canvas-surface capabilities; explicit failure or allowed fallback is reported.

outcomeResults.description: barriers
outcomeResults.reason: Compute shader graphs validate workgroup/storage barrier scope and emit the corresponding WGSL barrier; a source test checks storageBarrier. Inter-pass ordering uses WebGPU queue semantics.

outcomeResults.description: Prove adapter, active backend, dispatch, rendered result and pixels; report adapter identity.
outcomeResults.reason: The packed-candidate root browser spec requests an adapter, asserts the active backend, shared-device dispatch and changed pixels, and attaches diagnostics/screenshots. Actual proof and adapter identity for this audited candidate require a retained post-freeze browser/device receipt; none is established here.

outcomeResults.description: Forward
outcomeResults.reason: Forward is the default path and includes collection, sorted opaque/transparent work and clustered-light resolution; permitted alternate-path fallback selects it.

outcomeResults.description: Implement real scene submission, depth, shadows, materials, resources, resize and disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: The native backend requires a usable WebGPU device, delegates scene/frame submission, and supports async pixel proof, resize and disposal; synchronous native readback and its proof-only transmission capture are explicitly rejected. Borrowed-device teardown retains failed-fence leases, but a ResourceLifecycle owner can finish before a waiting fence later rejects and cannot re-enroll that owner.

outcomeResults.description: Add photometric profiles and projected images to typed light options.
outcomeResults.reason: Typed point/spot profiles and projected-image options exist. This outcome also bundles 85 other file references; not all their contracts were established, and projected spot draws explicitly reject WebGPU and clustered indexing.

outcomeResults.description: Replace attributed physical shader implementations independently while preserving lobe behavior. Exclusive execution owner: wp04_materials/physical_shaders. Source verification: tests/unit/rendering/native-physical-shaders.test.ts.
outcomeResults.reason: Some GLSL lobes and independent WGSL candidates exist, but named WGSL twins still retain r185-identical math and the generated independent path is a restricted opt-in preview.

outcomeResults.description: structs

outcomeResults.description: Replace the attributed external port with an implementation derived from the published sky model.
outcomeResults.reason: The sky implementation documents an independent Preetham/Perez derivation, with numerical reference cases. Source authorship is inferred from the implementation, not a forensic provenance certification.

outcomeResults.description: Independently replace attributed scene construction and light values with an Aura-owned environment.

outcomeResults.description: preserve the existing iridescence range while accepting separate minimum/maximum controls.

outcomeResults.description: Add rough diffuse and configurable retroreflection
outcomeResults.reason: Rough-diffuse and retroreflection controls are passed by primitive compilation to GLSL and WGSL direct-light formulas.

outcomeResults.description: atomics

outcomeResults.description: rectangular-area

outcomeResults.description: Specify profiles, clustered light limits, cascades and probes.

outcomeResults.description: specular

outcomeResults.description: sky

outcomeResults.description: shadow maps/filters

outcomeResults.description: Supply equivalent native-GPU material and light evaluation.
outcomeResults.reason: Generated native WebGPU PBR implements numerous light and material terms, but feature/UV/environment limits and preview-only layered combinations prevent general equivalence.

outcomeResults.description: projected lights

outcomeResults.description: voxel-based indirect lighting where supported
outcomeResults.reason: Voxel collection/update and bounded cone tracing exist with CPU voxelization fallback and explicit renderer texture bindings; GPU voxelization is not claimed.

outcomeResults.description: Typed shader graphs, functions, flow control, variables, arrays, structs, math, noise, color, texture sampling, UV transforms, lighting hooks, screen/depth inputs, storage, atomics, barriers and compute dispatch. Generate and validate shaders for each supported backend.
outcomeResults.reason: The current typed graph now includes functions, arrays, structs and noise and is consumed by material.node. Mutable general locals and custom lighting hooks remain limited, WebGL2 rejects compute/storage, and exhaustive real-backend compiler validation is unestablished.

outcomeResults.description: Replace attributed shader code with independently authored, standards-based behavior and preserve supported material inputs.

outcomeResults.reason: The public ambient builder and authored lighting collection retain the ambient light; legacy and physical routes remain distinct.

outcomeResults.reason: Probe building, cache and prefilter infrastructure exist, but generated WebGPU restricts which environment variants can use the probe path and complete cross-backend correctness is unestablished.

outcomeResults.description: spot
outcomeResults.reason: The public spot builder retains cone, power, profile, projected image and shadow fields; execution restrictions for profiles/projection are independently reported.
