outcomeResults.reason: Legacy TSL provides mutable typed variables, but the serializable cross-backend graph local is restricted to u32 loop indices and its statement model has no general assignment.

outcomeResults.description: depth
outcomeResults.reason: Depth texture factory and GL depth allocations exist, but standalone WebGPU depth textures are not uploaded and depth-only/layered WebGPU targets are rejected.

outcomeResults.description: filtering
outcomeResults.reason: Min/mag filters are mapped and float32 filterability is checked, but WebGPU emits no LOD clamp for non-mip nearest or linear filters. On a texture with mip levels those filters can therefore sample other mips instead of only level zero.

outcomeResults.description: Base color
outcomeResults.reason: Public physical materials expose base color, texture and per-slot UV selection, and the native PBR material binds the base-color texture.

outcomeResults.description: Test sorting, stability policy, limits and resource cleanup.
outcomeResults.reason: The grouped test/document deliverables exist: simulated sort tests cover order, stability, limits, abort and fence cleanup; resource-limit and storage-layout tests and the contact note also exist. The sort tests do not cover a rejected device-loss promise with a pending fence, and are not a GPU pass receipt.

outcomeResults.description: 2D array
outcomeResults.reason: The dataArray factory validates layered input and both native upload paths create array textures; format and capability restrictions still apply.

outcomeResults.description: Complete 3D, array, cube, compressed, storage and depth resources, independent mip updates, attachment validation, resolve/copy/readback, bounded GPU sorting and lifecycle.
outcomeResults.reason: Factories, mips, validation and a bounded sorter exist; 3D target descriptors, WebGPU layered targets and generic transfers are missing, and splats use CPU sorting. A parent lifecycle can finish before a later retirement-fence rejection; a rejected sorter loss promise also releases scratch without a fence.

outcomeResults.description: independent async readback ownership
outcomeResults.reason: Compute-buffer readback allocates independent staging per request, copies the mapped bytes, validates lifetime and destroys staging; a unit case covers disposal during read.

outcomeResults.description: synchronization
outcomeResults.reason: Attachment hazards and ordered same-device compute/render submissions are checked; failed fence leases remain retained. WebGPU lacks generic async target transfers, and a ResourceLifecycle already completed while a fence was waiting cannot report its later rejection.

outcomeResults.description: flow control
outcomeResults.reason: IR includes if/loop and compute tests cover bounded flow and barriers, but statement control flow is explicitly disallowed in material graphs.

outcomeResults.description: texture sampling
outcomeResults.reason: Graph sampling supports 2D and 3D color textures and 2D depth loads; graph resource types omit cube and 2D-array samplers.

outcomeResults.description: Add 3D/storage and compressed-cube paths where missing; complete independent mip updates, readback, multisample/resolve, format validation and resource ownership.
outcomeResults.reason: 3D/storage and compressed-cube factories and mip updates exist. 3D target descriptors, WebGPU layered targets and generic transfers remain absent; accepted BC1-RGB cubes lack the required WebGPU fallback. A parent lifecycle can also finish before a later fence rejection.

outcomeResults.description: multisampling
outcomeResults.reason: Both native backends allocate multisampled color targets and resolve for rendering. WebGPU allows sample counts 1 or 4 and explicitly rejects sampleable depth resolve.

outcomeResults.description: roughness
outcomeResults.reason: Physical material exposes roughness and its map; typed graphs have a roughness surface output.

outcomeResults.description: structures
outcomeResults.reason: Recursive structures are laid out and written in std140/WGSL paths, and graph structs can reach WebGPU storage and portable uniforms; WGSL buffer bool is lowered or rejected as appropriate.

outcomeResults.description: Color-managed textures, data, canvas, video, cube, 2D array, 3D, compressed, depth and storage textures; format selection, filtering, anisotropy, wrapping, mip generation/update, upload and readback.
outcomeResults.reason: Factories and uploads cover many formats and dimensions. WebGPU standalone depth, accepted BC1-RGB cubes, non-mip filter/anisotropy semantics and generic target readback are incomplete; compressed 3D and public 3D wrap-R are also absent.

outcomeResults.description: Dynamic geometry accepts 16- or 32-bit indices as needed and declares component type, normalization, stride, offset, update range, topology, groups and morph attributes. Mutating positions invalidates bounds. Normal transforms use an inverse-transpose matrix.
outcomeResults.reason: Geometry normalizes typed/interleaved attributes, chooses 16/32-bit indices, carries topology/groups/morphs, supports partial attribute updates and refreshes changed position bounds; transforms use inverse-transpose normals.

outcomeResults.description: occlusion
outcomeResults.reason: Material surface exposes occlusion map/strength and UV selection and binds the native occlusion slot.

outcomeResults.description: resolving
outcomeResults.reason: WebGL implements the generic color resolve; WebGPU resolves within render passes but does not implement the optional generic resolveRenderTarget interface or sampleable multisample depth resolve.

outcomeResults.description: Byte-correct mixed shader data
outcomeResults.reason: Byte-owned staging uses DataView integer, unsigned and float setters and validates compound values; bool has an explicit WGSL u32 lowering.

outcomeResults.description: copy
outcomeResults.reason: WebGL supplies validated async color/depth target copy; WebGPU exposes a narrower synchronous color-region copy but not the generic async method.

outcomeResults.description: Complete target attachment, sampling, resolve, copy, readback and disposal contracts.
outcomeResults.reason: Attachment validation and transfer/disposal contracts exist, but the descriptor lacks 3D targets and WebGPU lacks generic async transfers. Its interop retains failed-fence resources, while an already-completed parent lifecycle does not reflect a later fence rejection.

outcomeResults.description: Node graphs have typed values, explicit inputs/outputs, compile diagnostics, stable serialization and per-backend feature negotiation. A graph must support material color, normal, roughness, metalness, emissive, alpha and vertex position; additional render, compute and storage operations are owned by WP-05.
outcomeResults.reason: Typed graph values, outputs, diagnostics and stable serialization are integrated with material.node. Contrary to the checkpoint, the construction/serialization facade is now declared on the public shader-graph-runtime subpath; backend validation rejects unsupported compute/storage.

outcomeResults.description: Reuse existing node-material entrypoints through an Aura-owned adapter; preserve clear errors for unsupported operations.
outcomeResults.reason: material.node accepts graph documents or migrates supported legacy nodes, and migration rejects unrepresentable nodes with a named diagnostic.

outcomeResults.description: Implement integer/bool bit representation and target-specific uniform/storage layouts for mixed scalar/vector/matrix/array/structure data. Validate strides, offsets, padding, non-square matrices, invalid lengths and byte-exact transfers
outcomeResults.reason: Low-level layouts, integer/boolean bytes and tests exist for all target classes; integration is incomplete for graph matrix schemas and WebGL portable aggregate data, while compute storage uploads raw caller bytes.

outcomeResults.description: cube/array/3D layers
outcomeResults.reason: WebGL targets support cube and 2D-array layers; the common descriptor cannot specify 3D targets and WebGPU rejects layered target creation.

outcomeResults.description: Derive uniform/storage layouts, strides, padding and typed writes from the graph's target-language type schema.

outcomeResults.description: Carry explicit frame/view identity, previous-depth ownership and scoped reset semantics through velocity providers.

outcomeResults.description: Replace attributed operator implementations with independently authored formulas and preserve output contracts.

outcomeResults.description: masks

outcomeResults.description: pixelation
outcomeResults.reason: Pixelation is typed, lowered and rendered by GL/GPU display shaders; GPU input must be single-sample rgba8.

outcomeResults.description: Provide an independently authored native-GPU counterpart.
outcomeResults.reason: An independently described GTAO WGSL counterpart exists, but the native post pass admission set excludes GTAO.

outcomeResults.description: depth
outcomeResults.reason: View-owned previous/current depth swaps and survives temporal render-size changes; expected prior depth defaults to an approximation and native GPU v2 is disconnected.

outcomeResults.description: alpha/depth
outcomeResults.reason: Splat draws blend alpha with depth testing; scalar volume accumulates alpha and consults a copied opaque depth texture. Both have standard-depth restrictions.

outcomeResults.description: glitch
outcomeResults.reason: Glitch is typed, lowered and executed in GL/GPU display shaders; GPU requires a compatible rgba8 source.

outcomeResults.description: outlines

outcomeResults.description: Propagate output color and alpha policy through legacy post path. Exclusive execution owner: wp06_post; serialized transfer from wp32_color before edits. Source verification: tests/unit/rendering/native-color-management.test.ts.
outcomeResults.reason: Legacy GL forwards tone defaults, but the non-WebGPU default remains hardcoded sRGB; alpha-preserving policy is explicitly restricted to the WebGL v2 OutputPass rather than the legacy fused chain.

outcomeResults.description: Remove module-global temporal/model caches. Use app/device/view/frame identity, stable runtime object keys, once-per-frame history commits and scoped resets
outcomeResults.reason: View/frame state and stable object keys are implemented, but shared compatibility history and its module-global reset registration still exist.

outcomeResults.description: Add motion/depth/normal handling for animated, instanced and transparent content

outcomeResults.description: reflections

outcomeResults.reason: MD2 v8 parsing and a disposable static/morph-animation adapter exist, but strict typed root-model admission is not established.

outcomeResults.description: Scene hierarchy, mesh, materials, skinning and animation.
outcomeResults.reason: The FBX loader produces bounded hierarchy, meshes, supported materials, skinning and animation, and diagnoses nonrepresentable blend shapes and other content.

outcomeResults.description: Import and use PDB through its admitted typed public path with documented supported variants, malformed-input limits, provenance and resource disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: PDB parsing retains angstrom positions, bonds and attributes, but scientific rendering reports attribute loss and strict typed admission is unavailable.

outcomeResults.description: Import and use EXR deep through its admitted typed public path with documented supported variants, malformed-input limits, provenance and resource disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: A separate bounded deep EXR parser and compositing API exist, but the typed HDRI path uses flat parseEXR and explicitly rejects deep parts; deep subsampling and compression beyond ZIP are unsupported.

outcomeResults.description: Import and use DDS through its admitted typed public path with documented supported variants, malformed-input limits, provenance and resource disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: DDS parses supported block/uncompressed formats with CPU fallback but rejects cubes/volumes and has no admitted typed DDS texture route.

outcomeResults.description: Replace the attributed external port with an independently authored decoder, then add PXR24, B44/B44A and DWAA/DWAB plus bounded deep-data handling; reject unsupported tiled modes explicitly.
outcomeResults.reason: The changed EXR source declares an independent implementation and contains PXR24, B44/B44A, DWAA/DWAB and bounded deep decoding; unsupported tiled/deep subsampling and compression modes fail explicitly. Independent fixture tests exist.

outcomeResults.description: photometric profiles
outcomeResults.reason: Bounded IES LM-63 Type-C parsing is exposed to validated public point/spot lights; unsupported photometric types and invalid tables are rejected.

outcomeResults.description: Provide a valid minimal fixture, a realistic multi-feature fixture where applicable, and hostile/truncated inputs for every format. Render supported scene content through the public API.
outcomeResults.reason: Independent mesh/scene/scientific fixtures, glTF required-emissive identity source tests and a browser adapter spec exist, but real JXL/UltraHDR codec fixtures and dedicated BVH/MDD/SVG/MaterialX/3DL coverage are absent; the browser spec does not cover all typed scene formats.

outcomeResults.description: AMF, 3DS, VRML, LDraw and KMZ, with dependency and archive limits.
outcomeResults.reason: The five legacy loaders are opt-in, with bounded parsing and archive/dependency resolution; unsupported constructs such as AMF constellations are explicitly rejected or diagnosed.

outcomeResults.description: SVG paths, shapes, fills, strokes and transforms.
outcomeResults.reason: SVG paths, shapes, solid fills, strokes and transforms have parser/geometry source, but paint servers, effects and nested viewports are not represented and no dedicated SVG test was found.

outcomeResults.description: PLY and STL meshes; ASCII/binary variants, attributes, endianness and malformed input.
outcomeResults.reason: PLY 1.0 ASCII and both binary byte orders and ASCII/binary STL have bounded parsing, attribute handling and malformed-input checks, with unmapped properties diagnosed.

outcomeResults.description: GCode
outcomeResults.reason: GCode modal motion produces bounded millimetre toolpath arrays; rotary axes and multi-turn arcs are rejected and strict typed admission is unavailable.

outcomeResults.description: SVG
outcomeResults.reason: An optional SVG parser and geometry adapter exist but important paint/effect/viewport cases are unsupported, no strict typed admission exists, and no dedicated SVG test was found.

outcomeResults.description: Import and use 3DL through its admitted typed public path with documented supported variants, malformed-input limits, provenance and resource disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: 3DL parsing, bounds and trilinear sampling exist; a typed 3DL asset/use path and a dedicated test were not found, and the image LUT loader delegates predecode bounds to the caller.

outcomeResults.description: LDraw
outcomeResults.reason: LDraw resolves parts with dependency/cycle bounds and request policies, but strict typed admission and a complete public version/loss contract are absent.

outcomeResults.description: 3MF package geometry, units, resources, transforms and materials.
outcomeResults.reason: The bounded 3MF package parser converts supported geometry, units, resources, component transforms and materials, rejecting unsupported required extensions and invalid packages.

outcomeResults.description: subject to explicit codec capabilities
outcomeResults.reason: Image decoders report unsupported cases and allow caller-declared GPU formats, but JXL/UltraHDR require injected codecs and the entire image catalog is not wired to capability-aware typed loading.

outcomeResults.description: 3DL and image-based color tables, interpolation, ranges and validation.
outcomeResults.reason: 3DL and decoded-image LUT conversion, range validation, trilinear interpolation and texture baking exist, but image decoding is delegated with caller-owned predecode limits and no dedicated format tests were found.

outcomeResults.description: Import and use USDZ through its admitted typed public path with documented supported variants, malformed-input limits, provenance and resource disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: Stored USDZ with USDA has a bounded optional loader, but binary crate layers and strict typed admission are unavailable.

outcomeResults.description: Scene, geometry, materials, skins and animation with external references.
outcomeResults.reason: The optional Collada loader converts scene hierarchy, geometry, supported materials, skins and animation, including scoped external references; unsupported constructs are diagnosed.

outcomeResults.description: 3DM scene geometry, object metadata and material conversion.
outcomeResults.reason: Rhino decoded mesh, object metadata and approximate material conversion are bounded, but actual 3DM decoding is delegated to a required caller-provided codec and texture/non-mesh objects may be omitted.

outcomeResults.description: Import and use VTK through its admitted typed public path with documented supported variants, malformed-input limits, provenance and resource disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: VTK legacy ASCII/binary point/cell parsing and a limited render projection exist, but unsupported datasets/cells fail and strict typed admission is unavailable.

outcomeResults.description: Import and use GCode through its admitted typed public path with documented supported variants, malformed-input limits, provenance and resource disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: The bounded GCode parser produces millimetre toolpaths and rejects rotary axes/multi-turn arcs, but strict typed model admission is unavailable.

outcomeResults.description: VOX
outcomeResults.reason: VOX 150/200 has typed async admission, explicit version-checked opt-in adapter and bounded palette/transform projection; hierarchy/animation and physical material losses are disclosed.

outcomeResults.description: MaterialX documents
outcomeResults.reason: MaterialX graph parsing and material construction exist with unsupported-node diagnostics, but displacement is not automatically applied and typed admission plus a dedicated test were not found.

outcomeResults.description: Import and use AMF through its admitted typed public path with documented supported variants, malformed-input limits, provenance and resource disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: AMF plain/zip parsing is bounded and diagnoses unrepresented features, but constellations are rejected and strict typed admission is unavailable.

outcomeResults.description: TIFF
outcomeResults.reason: Classic TIFF strips have a bounded parser and fixture tests, but tiled TIFF and admitted typed TIFF textures are unsupported.

outcomeResults.description: Import and use 3DS through its admitted typed public path with documented supported variants, malformed-input limits, provenance and resource disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: The 3DS parser handles bounded geometry and material chunks, but strict typed admission and a complete format-specific version/loss contract are absent.

outcomeResults.description: return stable diagnostics for malformed or unsupported inputs.
outcomeResults.reason: Individual loaders emit bounded, named errors and unsupported-feature diagnostics, but preflight recognizes only a subset and uniform diagnostics across the required catalog are not established.

outcomeResults.description: Import and use LDraw through its admitted typed public path with documented supported variants, malformed-input limits, provenance and resource disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: LDraw supports bounded MPD/dependency expansion and propagates request policies, but strict typed admission and full per-format documentation are absent.

outcomeResults.description: PVR
outcomeResults.reason: The PVR v3 parser, digest-bound async admission and caller-owned typed texture loading cover documented supported layouts and explicitly reject unsupported ones.

outcomeResults.description: MDD
outcomeResults.reason: MDD frame parsing and clamped interpolation exist, but topology is external, typed admission/render binding is absent, and no dedicated MDD test was found.

outcomeResults.description: DDS
outcomeResults.reason: DDS parsing and BC fallbacks exist, but cube/volume inputs are rejected and the typed native texture path accepts PVR only.

outcomeResults.description: UltraHDR
outcomeResults.reason: UltraHDR validates a JPEG envelope and bounded codec result, but requires an injected gain-map decoder and has no admitted native texture route; the existing codec test is mocked.

outcomeResults.description: Import and use STL through its admitted typed public path with documented supported variants, malformed-input limits, provenance and resource disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: STL ASCII/binary parsing, strict typed admission and an opt-in disposable adapter exist, but the public format documentation does not record its specific admission/resource limits and lifecycle contract as required.

outcomeResults.description: MaterialX graphs, displacement, unlit and standard surface translation; explicit unsupported node diagnostics.
outcomeResults.reason: MaterialX translates supported graphs and unlit/standard surfaces and evaluates displacement values, but material creation samples expressions rather than installing a spatial graph, displacement is not applied to geometry, and no dedicated test was found.

outcomeResults.description: Import and use Collada through its admitted typed public path with documented supported variants, malformed-input limits, provenance and resource disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: Collada converts supported hierarchy, geometry, materials, skin, animation and external dependencies, but strict typed admission is unavailable.

outcomeResults.description: Expand supported image and mesh variants with fixtures, strict limits and clear errors.
outcomeResults.reason: EXR and OBJ have expanded bounded decoders with fixtures, but OBJ still omits several texture maps and numerous image/mesh variants lack strict typed admission or real codec fixtures.

outcomeResults.description: NRRD
outcomeResults.reason: NRRD/NHDR typed scalar-volume admission snapshots and hashes embedded or single detached data, and the root volume path validates format and owns resources; unsupported variants are rejected.

outcomeResults.description: Import and use EXR DWAB through its admitted typed public path with documented supported variants, malformed-input limits, provenance and resource disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: DWAB is decoded by the bounded EXR reader used by the typed HDRI path; codec and typed HDRI source tests exist, while deep and tiled-subsampled cases remain excluded.

outcomeResults.description: Exercise public, typed imported assets through scene rendering.
outcomeResults.reason: Source unit tests exercise supported required glTF material-pointer playback through a typed actor. A packed-public-adapter browser spec renders seven mesh/3MF cases and an OBJ/MTL case, but it uses explicit URL/format requests rather than generated typed root-model assets and does not cover the entire catalog.

outcomeResults.description: KTX1/KTX2
outcomeResults.reason: KTX1 parsing and KTX2/Basis transcoding exist with capability-dependent fallbacks, but the standalone admitted typed native texture route is PVR-only.

outcomeResults.description: ordinary web images
outcomeResults.reason: ImageLoader supports browser-decoded PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF/AVIF with policy-checked fetch and cleanup, but it imposes no default file-byte or predecode pixel/allocation bound; browser codec support is conditional.

outcomeResults.description: Import and use PLY through its admitted typed public path with documented supported variants, malformed-input limits, provenance and resource disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: PLY 1.0 ASCII/binary parsing, strict typed admission and an opt-in disposable adapter exist, but the public format documentation does not record its specific admission/resource limits and lifecycle contract as required.

outcomeResults.description: Import and use SVG through its admitted typed public path with documented supported variants, malformed-input limits, provenance and resource disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: SVG parsing and an optional geometry adapter exist, but paint servers/effects/nested viewports are limited, strict typed admission is absent, and no dedicated SVG test was found.

outcomeResults.description: BVH
outcomeResults.reason: BVH parsing produces skeleton/channel/frame data, but a typed admitted scene path and dedicated BVH test were not found.

outcomeResults.description: 3DL/image color tables
outcomeResults.reason: 3DL and image LUT parsing and sampling exist, but typed 3DL admission/use is missing, image predecode bounds are delegated, and no dedicated test was found.

outcomeResults.description: PLY
outcomeResults.reason: PLY 1.0 import supports ASCII and both binary byte orders; export returns structured losses, and source tests independently inspect exported positions, faces and edges for all three encodings. No test pass is claimed.

outcomeResults.description: HDR
outcomeResults.reason: Radiance RGBE is decoded by the typed environment path with request policy and resource ownership; bounded decoder tests exist.

outcomeResults.description: Import and use XYZ through its admitted typed public path with documented supported variants, malformed-input limits, provenance and resource disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: XYZ numeric/molecular points have typed arrays and units, but rendering drops source attributes and strict typed admission is unavailable.

outcomeResults.description: TGA
outcomeResults.reason: Selected TGA palette, grayscale and RLE representations are parsed, with unsupported interleaving rejected; admitted typed native texture loading is PVR-only.

outcomeResults.description: PCD
outcomeResults.reason: PCD 0.7 ASCII, binary and LZF-compressed point fields are parsed, but projection can reject nonfinite positions and drops attributes, and strict typed model admission is unavailable.

outcomeResults.description: STL
outcomeResults.reason: STL ASCII/binary import and export are bounded, unsupported material/hierarchy content produces structured loss warnings, and an independent test reader checks binary facets; no test pass is claimed.

outcomeResults.description: Import and use 3DM through its admitted typed public path with documented supported variants, malformed-input limits, provenance and resource disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: Rhino inspection and bounded conversion exist, but actual 3DM decoding needs a supplied codec, supported objects/materials are limited and strict typed admission is unavailable.

outcomeResults.description: Import and use NRRD through its admitted typed public path with documented supported variants, malformed-input limits, provenance and resource disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: NRRD/NHDR scalar-volume admission hashes root and optional detached bytes; the typed root route validates the volume and exposes resource lifecycle, with unsupported variants documented.

outcomeResults.description: Import and use VOX through its admitted typed public path with documented supported variants, malformed-input limits, provenance and resource disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: VOX 150/200 has bounded typed admission, version-checked optional adapter, palette and static-frame mesh projection with documented losses and disposal.

outcomeResults.description: Export KTX2 through its public path, preserving supported data with explicit structured loss and independently verified round trips.
outcomeResults.reason: Public KTX2 supports raw layouts and explicitly injected compressors, with structured codec/loss diagnostics. Independent ktx-parse tests cover raw mips and a zlib codec, but no passing receipt binds those checks to this working tree; compressed-codec metadata preservation is explicitly unverified.

outcomeResults.description: Export compressed mesh through its public path, preserving supported data with explicit structured loss and independently verified round trips.
outcomeResults.reason: The public Draco writer uses an optional supplied codec, reports material/morph losses and rejects line topology with a structured error. An encoder/vendor-decoder round-trip test exists, but no passing current-source receipt establishes independent verification.

outcomeResults.description: bump
outcomeResults.reason: The material interchange contract carries bump factor/texture, the glTF writer emits EXT_materials_bump, and the loaded-material snapshot test checks the emitted extension and reloaded factor. This is export support, not a claim of rendered bump parity.

outcomeResults.description: GLTF/GLB, OBJ, PLY, STL, USDZ, compressed mesh, EXR and KTX2 export; embedded/external dependencies; independent round-trip validation and explicit structured loss reports.
outcomeResults.reason: All named exporter families and dependency/loss contracts have source entrypoints. Full independent validation remains incomplete, notably the USDZ stage and PLY semantics; glTF snapshots also report material-variant and original-encoding loss. No current-source passing receipt was identified.

outcomeResults.description: Test each exporter with independently implemented readers or conformance validators, round-trip data and loss warnings.
outcomeResults.reason: Independent OBJ/MTL, glTF instance, KTX2 and limited binary-STL readers plus EXR and Draco decoding tests exist. PLY tests check selected fields, and USDZ validates archive framing while checking USDA as text rather than using an independent USD stage reader or validator.

outcomeResults.description: Produce structured warnings for loss, missing encoders or unsupported features
outcomeResults.reason: Results have code/path/message warnings; the scene writers report unsupported properties and losses, while missing Draco or compressed KTX2 encoders produce structured errors. Diagnostic truncation is itself reported.

outcomeResults.description: embedded/external dependencies
outcomeResults.reason: glTF/GLB embeds or returns image and buffer dependencies, OBJ returns its MTL and texture files, and USDZ embeds supported image dependencies in its archive. Unsupported or unreferenced dependencies are reported.

outcomeResults.description: OBJ
outcomeResults.reason: The public OBJ writer serializes baked geometry, groups, MTL bindings and texture dependencies, with explicit warnings for unsupported scene/material semantics. A separate small OBJ/MTL reader test covers the supported topology and dependencies.

outcomeResults.description: Verify a loaded, edited scene exports and reloads without losing supported semantics.
outcomeResults.reason: A browser test loads a glTF scene, edits its transform, exports/reloads GLB and checks hierarchy, geometry, material and a rendered pixel. No matching current-source browser acceptance receipt was found, and the test covers that fixture rather than every possible scene semantic.

outcomeResults.description: compressed mesh
outcomeResults.reason: Standalone compressed geometry is produced by an explicitly injected Draco codec for triangles or points; missing encoders and unsupported line topology fail explicitly and omitted scene semantics are reported.

outcomeResults.description: Encode supported HDR channels including RLE/PIZ, choose an explicit source attachment/layer and preserve HDR values with bounded memory.
outcomeResults.reason: For supplied planar CPU samples, EXR requires explicit attachment/layer selection, writes float or half channels with native RLE/PIZ and budgets working memory. It preserves float HDR values and reports half conversion or omitted attachments. This does not establish a render-target readback bridge.

outcomeResults.description: Export GLB through its public path, preserving supported data with explicit structured loss and independently verified round trips.
outcomeResults.reason: The public GLB writer emits hierarchy, accessors, materials, skins, morphs and animation; its common glTF path preserves proven required default emissive pointers or rejects known identity loss. A test uses an independent glTF reader for instancing, but comprehensive independent round-trip verification and a source-bound passing receipt are not established; material variants are dropped by the snapshot.

outcomeResults.description: Write ASCII/binary triangles, transformed normals and solid boundaries.
outcomeResults.reason: STL writes ASCII or little-endian binary triangle facets with normals derived from transformed positions and corrected reflection winding. ASCII retains distinct solid boundaries; binary's inability to retain them is explicitly warned.

outcomeResults.description: explicit structured loss reports
outcomeResults.reason: Writer results carry structured warning codes, paths and messages; the CLI includes them in its JSON loss report or prints individual warnings. Tests assert representative unsupported-property and format-loss diagnostics.

outcomeResults.description: Export glTF through its public path, preserving supported data with explicit structured loss and independently verified round trips.
outcomeResults.reason: The public glTF JSON writer emits embedded or external resources and typed warnings. Loader-proven required default emissive pointers can be remapped and known identity loss fails export, with source tests present but unrun. Broader scene semantics lack comprehensive independent round-trip verification tied to this source identity; snapshot material variants and original attribute encoding are explicitly lost.

outcomeResults.description: instancing
outcomeResults.reason: Current untracked source now snapshots runtime instance transforms/colors and emits required EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing TRS accessors; an independent glTF reader test exists. Shear and skinned instancing are rejected, and custom instance colors carry an interoperability warning; the earlier missing checkpoint is stale.

outcomeResults.description: Encode supported texture layouts with explicit encoder capability.
outcomeResults.reason: KTX2 exposes six raw pixel layouts, mip/layer/face metadata and explicit capability-checked injected encoders for compressed output; unavailable or malformed encoders fail with structured diagnostics.

outcomeResults.description: Export EXR through its public path, preserving supported data with explicit structured loss and independently verified round trips.
outcomeResults.reason: The public EXR writer selects supplied HDR channels and produces RLE/PIZ with explicit warnings; source tests decode RLE and PIZ. No independently verified passing round-trip receipt is bound to the current source, and tests use supplied CPU samples rather than an actual MRT.

outcomeResults.description: Write ASCII/binary geometry with supported vertex/face attributes and endianness.
outcomeResults.reason: PLY writes ASCII and binary little/big endian vertex positions, normals, UVs, colors, triangle faces and indexed edges, baking transforms and reporting unsupported attributes.

outcomeResults.description: Preserve quantized attributes and indexed lines in formats that represent them, or produce explicit losses. Test HDR RLE/PIZ output and explicit attachment/layer export from multiple-output targets without clamping scene values.
outcomeResults.reason: Typed quantized accessors and indexed glTF lines are written, STL/USDZ report conversion losses, and CPU-supplied HDR attachments exercise RLE/PIZ without clamping. Actual MRT attachment/layer HDR readback into EXR is not integrated or source-tested; float readback lacks an attachment parameter.

outcomeResults.description: Export STL through its public path, preserving supported data with explicit structured loss and independently verified round trips.
outcomeResults.reason: STL supports facets and explicit format losses; a current independent test reads a single binary triangle, while the ASCII case checks text. Complete independent format round trips and a passing receipt for the current source are not established.

outcomeResults.description: Implement every exporter in the WP-09 table with an independently specified capability matrix and a typed result.
outcomeResults.reason: All listed source writers are exported from the opt-in barrel, with an independently declared format capability matrix and shared typed result/warning contracts. The current-source tests exist but have not been established as passing.

outcomeResults.description: Add a typed CLI export command with loss report and output-path validation.
outcomeResults.reason: The assets export verb is registered through the CLI registry, accepts typed format/options and bounded JSON inputs, reports warnings/dependencies, checks project-relative output paths and uses exclusive writes with rollback.

outcomeResults.description: Produce structured warnings for loss, missing encoders or unsupported features; never silently omit data. Test independent readers, formats, endianness, units and dependency packaging.
outcomeResults.reason: Typed loss and missing-encoder diagnostics and tests for units, endian formats and dependency packaging exist. An independent USDZ stage reader and complete PLY reader round trip were not found, so the all-format test requirement is not fully established.

outcomeResults.description: animation
outcomeResults.reason: glTF writes validated translation, rotation, scale and morph-weight channels with LINEAR/STEP/CUBICSPLINE interpolation and bounded property animation pointers. For loader-proven required default emissive-strength tracks, it restores the authored default only with matching track/material identity and declarations; removed or duplicated original tracks with the retained loader lookup and changed targets fail export. Without that lookup, origin/requiredness is unknown and warned, not recovered. Relevant tests exist but were not run.

outcomeResults.description: materials
outcomeResults.reason: Core PBR material factors/textures and the declared material extension fields are written, including texture settings; tests inspect a loaded extension-rich material snapshot. Material-variant mappings are a separate documented loss.

outcomeResults.description: Export supported compressed geometry through an explicitly optional codec.
outcomeResults.reason: Standalone Draco geometry export requires an explicitly supplied encoder, validates its output and emits a semantic-to-attribute-ID descriptor plus loss diagnostics; unsupported line topology is rejected.

outcomeResults.description: compression
outcomeResults.reason: The glTF writer supports Basis KTX2 texture dependencies and standalone Draco can encode a separate primitive, but the glTF interchange primitive has no Draco/meshopt mesh-compression representation or encoder path. Runtime snapshots report original attribute encoding lost.

outcomeResults.description: independent round-trip validation
outcomeResults.reason: Independent OBJ/MTL, glTF instance, KTX2, EXR/Draco and limited STL checks exist, but USDZ stage semantics are asserted as text and PLY checks selected bytes. No retained pass is bound to the current full source identity.

outcomeResults.description: Export PLY through its public path, preserving supported data with explicit structured loss and independently verified round trips.
outcomeResults.reason: The public PLY writer handles ASCII and both binary endiannesses with warnings; source tests inspect vertices, faces and indexed edges. A complete independent PLY-reader round trip and a current-source passing receipt were not established.

outcomeResults.description: Package supported geometry, materials, transforms and animation with dependency rules.
outcomeResults.reason: USDZ writes a USDA scene with supported geometry, hierarchical transforms, preview materials, animation and embedded PNG/JPEG dependencies; unsupported features receive warnings. Archive tests check ZIP alignment, dependencies and representative stage contents, not independent USD interpretation.

outcomeResults.description: Shared source traversal, loss diagnostics, provenance, dependency naming and cancellation.
outcomeResults.reason: Shared validation/traversal, structured diagnostics, safe dependency names and cancellation exist. Loader-owned weak identity evidence protects required default emissive-strength material/track provenance, and a retained lookup detects original tracks removed, reconstructed or duplicated; the writer rejects known required loss. If that lookup is removed, requiredness is unknown and warned rather than recovered. The runtime snapshot still cannot retain original document-level metadata, license or provenance.

outcomeResults.description: Export OBJ through its public path, preserving supported data with explicit structured loss and independently verified round trips.
outcomeResults.reason: Public OBJ/MTL exports geometry, groups and texture dependencies with structured losses, and an independent reader test checks these values. The required independently verified pass is not bound by any identified receipt to the current source.

outcomeResults.description: Round-trip geometry, transform, hierarchy, material, animation, skin/morph and metadata where each format supports them.
outcomeResults.reason: Source tests reload glTF geometry, hierarchy, material, skin, morph and animation, including loader-proven required default emissive pointers after material remapping, and independently parse OBJ subsets. These tests were not run. The snapshot loses source document provenance/variants; USDZ's supported stage semantics are not independently loaded in its archive tests.

outcomeResults.description: cameras
outcomeResults.reason: glTF writes validated perspective and orthographic camera definitions with node bindings; runtime snapshot code recognizes both camera kinds.

outcomeResults.description: skins
outcomeResults.reason: glTF emits skins, joint indices, inverse-bind matrices and node bindings with validation; tests reload a skin/joint hierarchy and associated animated morph data. Snapshot warns when source joints cannot be resolved.

outcomeResults.description: Export scene graph, meshes, materials, cameras, lights, skins, morphs, animation and dependencies with explicit loss warnings.
outcomeResults.reason: The glTF writer emits scene nodes, meshes, materials, cameras, punctual lights, skins, morphs, animation and embedded/external dependencies, returning structured warnings for unsupported or unavailable data. It rejects known required animation-pointer identity loss rather than silently downgrading it; if the loader lookup is unavailable, the origin is warned as unknown. Separate requirements for variant/compression parity and independent verification remain partial.

outcomeResults.description: lights
outcomeResults.reason: The glTF writer validates directional, point and spot light definitions and emits KHR_lights_punctual bindings; the snapshot warns for unsupported runtime light kinds.

outcomeResults.description: Export USDZ through its public path, preserving supported data with explicit structured loss and independently verified round trips.
outcomeResults.reason: The public USDZ writer packages a supported USDA stage and texture dependencies with warnings. Tests independently inspect stored-ZIP framing and CRCs but only assert strings in the stage; an independent USD semantic-reader round trip and current-source pass are not established.

outcomeResults.description: morphs
outcomeResults.reason: glTF writes morph targets and weights with count/semantic validation and supports weight animation; unsupported morph attributes are reported rather than silently emitted.

outcomeResults.description: KTX2 export
outcomeResults.reason: KTX2 export writes the supported raw layouts and mip chains, offers explicit injected codecs for compressed encodings and reports absent codecs, unverified codec metadata or lossy output.

outcomeResults.description: including diffuse roughness
outcomeResults.reason: The glTF material contract retains diffuse-roughness factor/texture, the writer emits KHR_materials_diffuse_roughness, and snapshot/reload test code asserts the factor and texture. This does not assert rendered diffuse-roughness parity.

outcomeResults.description: never silently omit data. Test independent readers, formats, endianness, units and dependency packaging.
outcomeResults.reason: Writers report numerous losses and tests inspect units, dependencies, byte order and several independent readers. A complete independent USDZ stage reader and PLY round trip were not found, so all-format verification and the universal no-silent-omission claim remain unestablished.

outcomeResults.description: Write geometry, groups, materials and texture dependencies.
outcomeResults.reason: OBJ writes transformed positions/topology, distinct groups and material bindings, emits MTL and safely named texture dependencies, and warns on incompatible maps, attributes and scene data.

outcomeResults.description: glTF/GLB geometry, buffers, textures, compression, materials, animation, skins, morphs, cameras, lights, variants, instancing and every declared material extension, including diffuse roughness and bump.
outcomeResults.reason: Current glTF source handles core scene data, declared material factors including bump/diffuse roughness, GPU instancing, and loader-proven required default emissive-pointer identity with fail-closed handling of known loss. It still drops material-variant mappings and original source encoding, and does not provide glTF Draco/meshopt mesh-compression output.

outcomeResults.description: Validate every format, version, malformed buffer, memory limit and metadata case.
outcomeResults.reason: The merged file references include functioning exports, scene mounting, ordered color composition, WebGL2/WebGPU surfaces, worker-backed Zstandard with provenance/notices, and their source tests. However KSPLAT and packed PLY tests exercise rejection or mock codecs rather than native wire versions and malformed data. The supposedly exhaustive handler test expects gaussian-splat but omits the now-registered scalar-volume key. WebGL drawToScratch restores framebuffer/view/scissor and invalidates the cache rather than establishing restoration of every draw-state field. The WebGPU splat adapter marks itself retired before scratch disposal: on a thrown scratch cleanup the device retains an uncertain failure rather than safely retrying the adapter.

outcomeResults.description: Parse all named splat formats and validate sample count, attributes, covariance, color and spherical-harmonic layouts.
outcomeResults.reason: The common validator checks count, finite arrays, SH lengths, color space, opacity, rotation and covariance; dispatch covers standard PLY, SPLAT, SPZ and glTF. KSPLAT and recognized compressed PLY require caller-provided codecs that the public scene compiler does not inject.

outcomeResults.description: Add scalar-volume slices and rendering with clipping, transfer functions and lifecycle tests.
outcomeResults.reason: The typed volume node validates slice coordinates, transfer stops and up to eight clip planes; its scene lease creates WebGL2 or WebGPU renderers and owns cancellation and cleanup. Source tests exercise clipping, uploads, updates, context loss and disposal. Root rendering explicitly rejects unsupported effect, target and depth combinations. These required tests do not establish end-to-end notification of a late shared WebGPU fence rejection; see the lifecycle limitation.

outcomeResults.description: Ingest, validate and render SPZ with ordering, material semantics, budgets and explicit unsupported-device diagnostics.
outcomeResults.reason: SPZ versions 1–3 use bounded gzip and version 4 uses bounded Zstandard streams, with version, count, SH and stream-size validation. The resulting color/opacity data reaches the common ordered, budgeted splat renderer and unsupported-device checks; unavailable worker, WebAssembly or unsupported rendering states fail explicitly.

outcomeResults.description: Ingest, validate and render PLY splats with ordering, material semantics, budgets and explicit unsupported-device diagnostics.
outcomeResults.reason: Splat-specific ASCII and little-/big-endian binary PLY 1.0 is validated and uses the common ordered renderer. Recognized packed/compressed PLY is not decoded natively and requires a callback unavailable to the typed scene compiler.

outcomeResults.description: Ingest, validate and render glTF splats with ordering, material semantics, budgets and explicit unsupported-device diagnostics.
outcomeResults.reason: glTF 2.0 KHR Gaussian primitives, active scenes, instances, separate clouds, per-cloud color/material metadata and aggregate budgets feed the common renderer. The ellipse kernel ignores material shading as documented in source; morphs, animated or skinned splats and Draco/meshopt-compressed splat data explicitly fail.

outcomeResults.description: spherical harmonics
outcomeResults.reason: Spherical-harmonic layouts are validated and real camera-dependent coefficients through degree four are evaluated during projection. Supported degree varies by input format: SPLAT carries no higher-order SH and the glTF parser admits degrees through three.

outcomeResults.description: define what happens on unsupported backends.
outcomeResults.reason: The public backend diagnostic identifies unknown backends as unsupported and the mock as non-rasterizing; the scene compiler accepts only WebGL2, WebGPU or mock. Nonstandard depth, unsuitable color/depth targets and missing native features produce explicit errors rather than a silent device fallback.

outcomeResults.description: transfer functions
outcomeResults.reason: Typed volume nodes validate ordered RGBA transfer stops, and both native renderer paths build and upload a sampled transfer table. Updates and interpolation have source tests; stop count is bounded to 2–4096.

outcomeResults.description: Ingest, validate and render KSPLAT with ordering, material semantics, budgets and explicit unsupported-device diagnostics.
outcomeResults.reason: A caller-supplied KSPLAT codec can return a validated cloud for the common renderer, which has ordering, budgets and backend checks. There is no native KSPLAT wire decoder, the scene compiler supplies no codec, and the existing KSPLAT test uses a fabricated callback rather than an independent KSPLAT file.

outcomeResults.description: volume
outcomeResults.reason: This is the physical-material volume item, not scalar-volume slicing. Thickness and attenuation parameters reach PBR materials, and imported glTF can bind a thickness texture; however the public typed material declares thicknessMap without a corresponding compiler mapping, so relevant-map support is incomplete on that path.

outcomeResults.description: volume slicing
outcomeResults.reason: The public node and renderer validate X/Y/Z slice axes and positions in [0,1], submit slice state, and sample the field with clipping and transfer functions. Root-scene route restrictions are explicit.

outcomeResults.description: Render scalar volume textures/slices with transfer functions and clipping.
outcomeResults.reason: VolumeRenderer owns a 3D scalar texture and transfer texture, validates and applies up to eight clip planes, and draws raymarched or axis-slice modes. A separate WebGPU scalar-volume renderer supplies its corresponding native path.

outcomeResults.description: registered glTF splat data with versioned validation
outcomeResults.reason: The importer selects glTF 2.0 KHR_gaussian_splatting primitives, validates attributes and complete SH layouts, and checks that the draft compressed extension contains SPZ v2 with matching counts. Unsupported animation, deformation and mesh compression are rejected.

outcomeResults.description: PLY/SPLAT/KSPLAT/SPZ and registered glTF splat data with versioned validation and resource limits.
outcomeResults.reason: Version and resource validation exist for standard PLY, SPLAT, SPZ and KHR glTF, including aggregate cloud budgets. KSPLAT parsing is only an external callback and packed PLY also needs one; neither codec can be supplied by the typed scene compiler.

outcomeResults.description: Test camera movement, depth, transparency, visible color, clipping, resize and disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: The requested browser spec exists with WebGL pixel assertions for splat camera reversal, alpha/depth, resize and disposal, a WebGPU ordering case, and volume color, clipping, depth, resize and disposal cases. The spec was not run in this audit; no visual or device pass is claimed.

outcomeResults.description: Add typed splat assets, PLY/SPLAT/KSPLAT/SPZ and glTF ingestion, ordering, spherical harmonics and GPU rendering.
outcomeResults.reason: Typed asset-backed nodes, PLY/SPLAT/SPZ and glTF import, spherical harmonics and GPU ordering/draw integration exist. The named KSPLAT format still needs an externally supplied decoder and the typed scene path cannot supply one; packed PLY has the same integration gap.

outcomeResults.description: PLY/SPLAT/KSPLAT/SPZ
outcomeResults.reason: Built-in parsers cover standard PLY, 32-byte SPLAT and SPZ versions 1–4. KSPLAT is only dispatched to an external codec and packed PLY also requires one; public typed compilation provides neither.

outcomeResults.description: Ingest, validate and render SPLAT with ordering, material semantics, budgets and explicit unsupported-device diagnostics.
outcomeResults.reason: The loader validates 32-byte SPLAT records and converts their positions, scales, quaternion, RGB and alpha into owned arrays. The public scene path creates the common camera-sorted, alpha/depth renderer with point/GPU budgets and backend diagnostics.

outcomeResults.description: Provide typed asset-backed splat scene nodes and backend diagnostics.
outcomeResults.reason: The exported typed builder checks asset kind, format and render options, the handler catalog registers the node, and the compiler mounts an owned splat renderer. Backend diagnostics distinguish WebGL2/WebGPU, non-rasterizing mock and unknown devices; the separate KSPLAT decoding gap remains.

outcomeResults.description: covariance
outcomeResults.reason: Input scales are checked for nonnegative values and float32 covariance overflow, and the renderer projects the rotated three-dimensional covariance into anisotropic screen-space ellipses for each camera. The source test checks rotation and resize effects.

outcomeResults.description: Parse PLY, SPLAT, KSPLAT, SPZ and registered glTF splat content; validate sizes, covariance and spherical harmonics.
outcomeResults.reason: The loader implements and validates standard PLY, SPLAT, SPZ and registered glTF content, including covariance and SH array layouts. KSPLAT and compressed PLY remain externally decoded, and the integrated typed compiler supplies no decoder.

outcomeResults.description: Implement camera-dependent ordering, blending, culling, depth interaction, bounds and resource budgets; define what happens on unsupported backends.
outcomeResults.reason: Camera-dependent projection, filtering, sorted transparent runs, alpha/depth state, bounds and per-node budgets are implemented; backend/depth limitations fail explicitly. Sorting transparent meshes at their centers is an acknowledged approximation for intersections.

outcomeResults.description: Exercise volume and splat rendering math, lifecycle and limits with source mocks. Exclusive execution owner: wp10_splats. Source verification: Direct Vitest for each file.
outcomeResults.reason: Both specified source test files exist: the volume suite asserts interpolation, uploads, clipping, updates and disposal; the splat suite asserts allocation limits, ordering, projection, restoration and ownership. Their presence is not a direct Vitest pass.

outcomeResults.description: scalar volumes: format parsing
outcomeResults.reason: The public scalar-volume path accepts NRRD/NHDR, parses through the scientific loader, validates three dimensions, supported finite scalar arrays, voxel limits and coordinate metadata, and mounts the result through the scene compiler. Unsupported types and spaces are explicit errors.

outcomeResults.description: Gaussian splats and scalar volumes: format parsing, camera-dependent projection/order, covariance, spherical harmonics, alpha/depth, volume slicing and transfer functions.
outcomeResults.reason: Splat projection/order, covariance, SH and alpha/depth and scalar NRRD slices/transfer functions have integrated source paths. The aggregate format-parsing requirement is incomplete because KSPLAT and compressed PLY require codecs not provided through typed scene compilation.

outcomeResults.description: Implement camera-dependent ordering, blending, culling, depth interaction, bounds and resource budgets
outcomeResults.reason: Splat instances are projected, culled and stably camera-sorted, then submitted with alpha blending and depth testing; world bounds, layer/render-order filtering and aggregate GPU limits are integrated. Unsupported depth/backends are explicit, and transparent mesh intersection ordering is approximate.

outcomeResults.description: Gaussian splats
outcomeResults.reason: Typed splat nodes and the common SH/covariance renderer are integrated for several inputs. Broad Gaussian-splat ingestion remains incomplete because KSPLAT and packed PLY have no native decoder or codec injection on the typed scene path.

outcomeResults.description: blending
outcomeResults.reason: This checklist row concerns general material blending. Low-level named and custom blend equations/factors are implemented and exercised by source tests, but the public custom-material compiler rejects custom factors and silently lowers its advertised subtractive option to ordinary alpha.

outcomeResults.description: resource limits
outcomeResults.reason: Input bytes, point count, decoded arrays, glTF aggregates and GPU instance buffers are bounded on built-in paths. KSPLAT and compressed PLY invoke externally supplied callbacks before validating returned arrays; their internal memory use is not bounded by the loader, and typed scenes cannot inject those codecs.

outcomeResults.description: Render, sort/cull, blend, project covariance and manage GPU resources.
outcomeResults.reason: The renderer projects anisotropic covariance, filters and sorts each camera frame, submits alpha-blended depth-tested instances, and bounds and rebuilds owned GPU resources. Its disposer marks itself disposed before sequential child disposal; a throwing child can prevent later cleanup and a renderer-level retry is a no-op. WebGPU interop safely retains leases until a fence passes or confirmed invalidation, but a parent ResourceLifecycle can report complete before a later fence rejection and cannot be re-enrolled automatically. Nonstandard depth is rejected and intersecting transparent meshes use center-based approximation.
