outcomeResults.description: Scalars, angles, interpolation, seeded randomness, color conversion and color spaces; 2D/3D/4D vectors; quaternions and Euler angles; 3×3/4×4 matrices; rays, planes, spheres, boxes, frustums, triangles, capsules, oriented boxes and spatial trees.
outcomeResults.reason: Public math exports scalar/vector/matrix/color and spatial types including OBB and Octree. Individual implementations impose numerical/input limits; this does not establish unspecified alternate spatial-tree types.

outcomeResults.description: UV unwrapping
outcomeResults.reason: Public atlas supports planar charts and bounded projection/intrinsic unfolding with explicit seams, but documents that it is not general unwrapping and splits incompatible folds/loops.

outcomeResults.description: text
outcomeResults.reason: Root text3D provides an extruded bitmap glyph mesh and SDF option. Loaded-font extrusion is rejected, and unsupported built-in glyphs are reported.

outcomeResults.description: Attribute formats and normalization; interleaving; shared buffers; update ranges; deindexing; merge, weld, remap, crease normals, tangent generation, morph evaluation, group preservation, mesh memory estimation and safe bounds.
outcomeResults.reason: Typed attributes, public interleaving/remap/weld/crease/morph tools, shared buffers, merge and bounds are present, but a general mesh-memory estimator and full cross-backend vertex-format coverage remain unestablished.

outcomeResults.description: Verify topology and counts against independently authored expectations.
outcomeResults.reason: Current geometry contract test source uses analytical topology, count, winding, normals and UV expectations independently of another engine.

outcomeResults.description: Independently implement extrusion including bevels on paths, or reject unsupported combinations explicitly; retain supported inputs and topology.
outcomeResults.reason: General extrusion creates bevel layers along a supplied path; independent linear mode rejects path/bevel settings, but the general rewrite itself explicitly states provenance and compatibility remain under review.

outcomeResults.description: preserve notices until their replacements pass equivalent contract tests.
outcomeResults.reason: Support and general Extrude retain origin/provenance warnings, but several other rewritten files no longer carry earlier port-origin comments and no current-source equivalent-contract passing receipt was found.

outcomeResults.description: shapes
outcomeResults.reason: This exact checklist item concerns public math shapes: Shape extends Path with hole paths and outline extraction. The rendering shape primitive is independently authored; the separate historical Support and extrusion adapters remain under review outside this narrow outcome. Triangulation accepts only bounded simple contours and disjoint holes.

outcomeResults.description: Add attribute interleave/deinterleave, weld, remap, group merge, triangle conversion, morph evaluation and creased normals.
outcomeResults.reason: All listed utilities are now exported via the opt-in public subpath. They copy or preserve relevant streams; strip/fan conversion explicitly rejects unsegmented groups/draw ranges and creased normals reject directional morph deltas.

outcomeResults.description: Independently replace the attributed geometry implementations named in the WP-13 file table; preserve notices until their replacements pass equivalent contract tests.
outcomeResults.reason: Independent replacement of the whole named file table is incomplete: Support explicitly retains old-port adapter/rotation portions; general Extrude provenance and compatibility remain under review despite independently authored shape and linear extrusion.

outcomeResults.description: Build the additions in WP-13 and retain correct attributes, groups and topology.
outcomeResults.reason: Public rational types, atlas, surface generators and geometry-tools now exist; earlier source origin remains in Support and broader missing compression/topology and generated-atlas scene verification prevent declaring the entire addition complete.

outcomeResults.description: Test topology, groups, morphs, attributes, reproducibility and resource ownership.
outcomeResults.reason: Unit test source exercises modifier topology, group/draw ownership, morph/attribute streams, reproducible sampling and unchanged inputs; public-subpath tests are also present.

outcomeResults.description: seams
outcomeResults.reason: The atlas supports explicit original-index edge cuts and reports boundary, requested, chart and nonmanifold seams.

outcomeResults.description: merge
outcomeResults.reason: geometry.merge is public and merges compatible geometry while validating topology, attributes, morphs and ranges.

outcomeResults.description: lathe
outcomeResults.reason: Public lathe builder reaches the renderer geometry dispatch with its declared inputs. Lathe requires at least two profile points.

outcomeResults.description: generated UVs reach the real baking path
outcomeResults.reason: Generated atlas output reaches the public native lightmap baker through bakeOptionsFromUVAtlas, and baked render data can be attached through the production lighting state. A unit test uses actual generated charts; no current-source browser receipt or generated-atlas baked scene was established.

outcomeResults.description: spatial trees
outcomeResults.reason: Public Octree constructs a triangle hierarchy for spatial/ray and collision queries; this establishes the octree, not arbitrary tree variants.

outcomeResults.description: Integrate rational curve and surface types into the public math surface.
outcomeResults.reason: The public math barrel exports Curves, whose current source exports all three rational types.

outcomeResults.description: seeded randomness
outcomeResults.reason: SeededRandom and seededRandom are exported; reproducibility uses an explicit seed.

outcomeResults.description: Implement rational curves, derivatives, knots and limits.
outcomeResults.reason: NURBSCurve validates knot axes and clipped ranges, exposes weighted points and derivatives, clamps samples and rejects singular results.

outcomeResults.description: mesh memory estimation
outcomeResults.reason: Batched-mesh telemetry counts vertex/index and shared buffer bytes, but a general custom geometry memory-estimation utility was not established.

outcomeResults.description: Fix closed tangent seam, oriented-box plane constant and collision depth/normal. Exclusive execution owner: wp13_geometry_tools/rational. Source verification: tests/unit/parity/curves.test.ts; tests/unit/parity/math.test.ts; tests/unit/math/native-rational-curves.test.ts.
outcomeResults.reason: Closed finite-difference tangents wrap the seam; the independent public OBB uses the public plane signed-distance convention and Octree computes contact normals/depth. Representative independent tests and public OBB declaration checks exist.

outcomeResults.description: Box
outcomeResults.reason: Public box builder reaches the renderer geometry dispatch with its declared inputs.

outcomeResults.description: decal
outcomeResults.reason: The public projected decal geometry clips source triangles to the projector; the engine decal path consumes this geometry.

outcomeResults.description: Build bounded UV charts, seams and packed atlases with gutters/texel density; return remaps for duplicated vertices and preserved attributes/morphs/groups.
outcomeResults.reason: Bounded charting and packing honor gutters and texel density; seam duplicates return both vertex and index maps with copied groups, attributes and morphs.

outcomeResults.description: deterministic surface sampling
outcomeResults.reason: The seeded public sampler snapshots source data, selects triangles by area and interpolated density, interpolates base/custom/morph attributes, and exposes reset/reproducible samples; invalid domains reject.

outcomeResults.description: Add runtime simplify, edge split, tessellation and curve deformation with explicit loss diagnostics.
outcomeResults.reason: The public geometry-tools subpath exports simplify, edge split, tessellate and curve deformation. Results include loss diagnostics, and unsupported directional morph cases explicitly reject.

outcomeResults.description: torus knot
outcomeResults.reason: Public torus knot builder reaches the renderer geometry dispatch with its declared inputs.

outcomeResults.description: morphs
outcomeResults.reason: Atlas seam duplication copies position, normal and tangent morph channels through the output vertex remap.

outcomeResults.description: ellipses
outcomeResults.reason: Public math exposes ellipses through the curve/shape surface and independent numerical fixture tests exist; support is for the declared curve types and valid input domains.

outcomeResults.description: Make weighted surface sampling seeded and deterministic. Verify numerical and rendered outcomes.
outcomeResults.reason: Public seeded weighted sampling and numerical assertions now exist, but no browser scenario rendering sampler output or bound render receipt was found.

outcomeResults.description: convex hull
outcomeResults.reason: Public geometry.convex consumes convex hull mesh generation and rejects too few or degenerate points.

outcomeResults.description: spheres
outcomeResults.reason: The public Sphere type supports bounds and intersection queries; numeric inputs are required.

outcomeResults.description: quaternions
outcomeResults.reason: Quaternion operations are public; a zero axis is rejected.

outcomeResults.description: capsules
outcomeResults.reason: Capsule is public with endpoints, radius and intersection helpers; it is distinct from mesh geometry.

outcomeResults.description: Verify nonoverlap, gutters, seams, texel density, mirrored/degenerate inputs, capacity limits and geometry remapping.
outcomeResults.reason: Atlas test source covers density, nonoverlap, explicit seams, mirrored/degenerate geometry, remapping, limits and cancellation.

outcomeResults.description: Provide a parametric patch-based reference geometry with controllable tessellation.
outcomeResults.reason: The public authored bicubic reference teapot exposes selectable components and bounded tessellation and checks output float32 fidelity.

outcomeResults.description: Generate lofted surfaces with frames, cap and degeneracy handling.
outcomeResults.reason: Public loft builds profile/path or section surfaces using transported frames, caps and explicit degeneracy checks.

outcomeResults.description: Build UV charts with an explicit destination channel, seams, texel density, gutter and atlas limits. Return vertex/index remaps and preserve groups/attributes/morphs after seam duplication; test nonoverlap, degeneracy, cancellation and bounded failure, then verify a baked-lighting scene uses the atlas.
outcomeResults.reason: Atlas test source covers nonoverlap, degeneracy, cancellation and limits, and the public baker accepts actual generated charts. The advanced-lighting browser scenario uses a manually authored atlas; no baked scene using buildUVAtlas or current-source visual receipt was found.

outcomeResults.description: quadratic curves
outcomeResults.reason: Public math exposes quadratic curves through the curve/shape surface and independent numerical fixture tests exist; support is for the declared curve types and valid input domains.

outcomeResults.description: weld
outcomeResults.reason: Public weld retains vertices only when positions meet tolerance and all attributes and morphs match; it returns both remaps and preserves groups/draw range.

outcomeResults.description: Replace attributed external geometry implementation with an independently authored equivalent; retain supported inputs, topology and documented output contracts.
outcomeResults.reason: Independent replacement of the whole named file table is incomplete: Support explicitly retains old-port adapter/rotation portions; general Extrude provenance and compatibility remain under review despite independently authored shape and linear extrusion.

outcomeResults.description: crease normals
outcomeResults.reason: Public crease-normal utility duplicates corners, retains indexed metadata and explicitly rejects normal/tangent morph deltas it cannot preserve.

outcomeResults.description: density
outcomeResults.reason: A finite positive texelDensity controls chart pixel extents per local-space unit; capacity failure is explicit when packing cannot fit.

outcomeResults.description: Runtime simplification
outcomeResults.reason: Public simplifyAuraMesh collapses bounded valid edges without crossing groups; output includes loss diagnostics. Inputs are triangle-only and unsupported direction-changing morph cases are rejected explicitly.

outcomeResults.description: capsule
outcomeResults.reason: Public capsule builder reaches the renderer geometry dispatch with its declared inputs.

outcomeResults.description: Use independent mathematical reference fixtures.
outcomeResults.reason: Math test source uses independent analytical references for vectors, rotations, rays, bounds and collisions; current execution was not performed.

outcomeResults.description: Paths, splines, cubic and quadratic curves, ellipses, arcs, shapes, contours, holes, triangulation, rational curves/surfaces/volumes, derivatives and consistent arc-length sampling.
outcomeResults.reason: The public math surface exposes the listed curve, shape and rational types plus length-based queries. Arc-length queries use a sampled approximation; singular rational denominators are rejected.

outcomeResults.description: packing with preserved/remapped groups
outcomeResults.reason: Packed chart rectangles remain disjoint and can rotate; the original triangle order is retained so material groups and draw ranges stay aligned.

outcomeResults.description: ring
outcomeResults.reason: Public ring builder reaches the renderer geometry dispatch with its declared inputs.

outcomeResults.description: rounded box
outcomeResults.reason: Public rounded box builder reaches the renderer geometry dispatch with its declared inputs.

outcomeResults.description: holes
outcomeResults.reason: Public math exposes holes through the curve/shape surface and independent numerical fixture tests exist; support is for the declared curve types and valid input domains.

outcomeResults.description: angles
outcomeResults.reason: Degree/radian conversions are exported; no alternate angle-unit format is implied.

outcomeResults.description: splines
outcomeResults.reason: Public math exposes splines through the curve/shape surface and independent numerical fixture tests exist; support is for the declared curve types and valid input domains.

outcomeResults.description: Implement loft, parametric and patch geometry with normals, UV seams, caps and tessellation controls.
outcomeResults.reason: Rendering public exports provide parametric, loft and bicubic patch generators, including normals, UV seams, loft caps and parametric/patch subdivision.

outcomeResults.description: Implement seeded, area-weighted surface sampling and attribute interpolation.
outcomeResults.reason: The seeded public sampler snapshots source data, selects triangles by area and interpolated density, interpolates base/custom/morph attributes, and exposes reset/reproducible samples; invalid domains reject.

outcomeResults.description: rays
outcomeResults.reason: Public Ray supports geometric queries and rejects a zero direction.

outcomeResults.description: Implement rational curve, surface and volume evaluation with knots, weights, derivatives, clipping and degenerate inputs.
outcomeResults.reason: Public rational curve, surface and volume validate knots, weights, range clipping and degenerate input, and evaluate mixed partial derivatives with bounded orders.

outcomeResults.description: curve deformation
outcomeResults.reason: Public deformAuraMeshAlongCurve maps base/morph positions and reports approximate normals; output includes loss diagnostics. Inputs are triangle-only and unsupported direction-changing morph cases are rejected explicitly.

outcomeResults.description: test nonoverlap, degeneracy, cancellation and bounded failure, then verify a baked-lighting scene uses the atlas.
outcomeResults.reason: Atlas test source covers nonoverlap, degeneracy, cancellation and limits, and the public baker accepts actual generated charts. The advanced-lighting browser scenario uses a manually authored atlas; no baked scene using buildUVAtlas or current-source visual receipt was found.

outcomeResults.description: Box, sphere, plane, circle, ring, cylinder, cone, capsule, torus, torus knot, polyhedra, lathe, extrude, shape, tube, rounded box, convex hull, decal, text, parametric, loft and patch geometry.
outcomeResults.reason: Public primitive dispatch, convex geometry, projected decal, text3D and rendering surface/loft/patch generators implement the named kinds; loaded-font extrusion is explicitly unsupported.

outcomeResults.description: Extend reusable dynamic helper geometry and lifecycle.
outcomeResults.reason: DynamicSceneHelper resamples and copies lines, applies affine transforms and visibility, retains the previous valid geometry on failed updates, and releases its reader on disposal. Both specified port tests now contain independent trigonometric, geometry and numeric expectations; the old focused run is not identity-bound.

outcomeResults.description: Test transforms, hot updates, empty geometry and disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: The named unit test source asserts changed and invalid updates, affine transforms, hidden and empty geometry, idempotent disposal and frame/registry lifecycle. A prior focused log reported a pass but did not hash the worktree.

outcomeResults.description: Verify output structure, resizing, accessible labels, stereo pixels and pointer routing.
outcomeResults.reason: The specified browser spec asserts DOM structure and accessibility, DOM and SVG resizing, pointer routing, SVG pixels and both stereo eye pixels; it also exercises cleanup. It is authored test source, not a browser pass.

outcomeResults.description: Implement the advanced helper catalog with scene-driven updates, visibility, transforms and disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: Advanced builders are exposed through helpers, and helpers.dynamic resamples the caller's scene state on app frames, respects visibility and node transforms, replaces changed nodes and unsubscribes/removes the owned node. The earlier focused test run is unbound.

outcomeResults.description: Test assistive labels, pointer routing, screenshot output, resize and cleanup.
outcomeResults.reason: The browser spec checks the accessible role/name, click routing, resize and restoration, asserts output pixels and attaches vector, outline and stereo screenshots. An attachment or unrun test is not a visual acceptance result.

outcomeResults.description: Spatial DOM labels, embedded interactive DOM surfaces, vector output, text output, stereo/anaglyph/parallax output and accessible event behavior.
outcomeResults.reason: Spatial DOM, interactive elements, ASCII and stereo modes have public addon source implementations. The vector path handles clipped static primitives but fails valid multi-stream positions and reads normalized integer positions as raw values, so the combined output capability is not complete.

outcomeResults.description: stereo/anaglyph/parallax output
outcomeResults.reason: StereoOutput renders left and right perspective views to separate targets and composes side-by-side, over-under, red/cyan anaglyph and left-first parallax strips; it restores the prior target and disposes owned targets. The earlier mock-unit pass is not a current identity-bound or browser-pixel pass.

outcomeResults.description: accessible event behavior
outcomeResults.reason: Labels retain authored ARIA, hide off-frustum or occluded anchors from the accessibility tree, and either receive normal DOM events or pass pointers to the canvas. Interactive events are explicitly not forwarded to the canvas; the real browser test is unrun.

outcomeResults.description: vector output
outcomeResults.reason: The independent SVG renderer clips and projects static triangles, lines and points with flat explicit styles, but its primary-buffer raw position read fails valid multi-stream geometry and misinterprets normalized integer positions. Prior tests cover only other layouts and are unbound.

outcomeResults.description: Add an opt-in object-space outline path with material/alpha rules.
outcomeResults.reason: The opt-in inverted-hull path handles strict versus approximate alpha rules, creates front-culled shells and owns their disposal. It reads both positions and normals from the primary buffer, however, so valid static meshes with either attribute in a different vertex stream throw rather than receiving an outline; normalized attributes are also read raw.

outcomeResults.description: Add advanced inspection helpers, spatial DOM/vector output, missing specialized scene objects, procedural generators, editing tools and a live material graph.
outcomeResults.reason: Advanced helpers, addon outputs, specialized objects, generators, geometry tools and a viewport-connected shader graph all have source implementations. This broad cross-package gap is not fully established: the required vector output has a demonstrated valid-geometry stream/decoding defect, and the entire WP-15/WP-17 catalog was not exhaustively audited here.

outcomeResults.description: Environment helpers
outcomeResults.reason: The rendering public entry exports environment-stage, ground-grid and sky-dome builders, and the engine exposes environment builders. The named ground grid is finite and the unlit dome uses a solid palette color; the existing tests are not a current passing receipt.

outcomeResults.description: Spatial DOM labels
outcomeResults.reason: Spatial DOM labels support screen and perspective transforms, frame-sampled matrices, depth ordering, accessible visibility and caller-defined anchor occlusion. The earlier unit log is unbound; depth-buffer/per-pixel occlusion is explicitly not provided.

outcomeResults.description: animation
outcomeResults.reason: The editor timeline lists glTF clips and changes preview, scrub and playback metadata, while a separate runtime bridge can tick and apply animation callbacks. The actual editor panel does not connect that bridge or tick/apply preview to its viewport; the browser spec only checks metadata.

outcomeResults.description: embedded interactive DOM surfaces
outcomeResults.reason: A caller-owned HTMLElement can be projected as a perspective plane and marked interactive; its own DOM events are received and its parent, styles and ARIA are restored. Occlusion is anchor-only and events are not forwarded to the canvas; iframe-specific behavior has no established browser receipt.

outcomeResults.description: resources
outcomeResults.reason: Dynamic helpers remove and replace owned runtime nodes and unsubscribe on disposal; the runtime registry removes compiled subtrees or uses remount fallback. The debug line helper owns no GPU resources. Existing registry/compiled-subtree tests are not an identity-bound lifecycle pass.

outcomeResults.description: camera/light/skeleton/audio/probe/physics/normal/tangent/texture helpers
outcomeResults.reason: Typed camera, light, skeleton, audio, probe, collider, normal, tangent and texture glyphs are exposed. They visualize caller-supplied data; the texture helper reads retained CPU pixels, not arbitrary GPU textures. Existing unit coverage is partial and its prior result is unbound.

outcomeResults.description: Axes/grids, camera/light/skeleton/audio/probe/physics/normal/tangent/texture helpers; dynamically updated transforms and resources.
outcomeResults.reason: Axes, Cartesian and polar grids, the named helper families, frame-driven resampling, transforms, visibility and registry disposal are present. Tests cover representative helpers and lifecycle; the complete catalog and compiled resource lifecycle have no current bound pass.

outcomeResults.description: Add animation path, audio orientation, probe/grid, octree, collider, area light, texture, vertex-normal and tangent helpers.
outcomeResults.reason: AdvancedHelpers implements animation paths, orientation, probes and grids, octrees, collider shapes, area lights, CPU textures, normals and tangents; debug and engine exports expose the builders. Bounded inputs and inverse-transpose normal handling are tested, with only an unbound prior result.

outcomeResults.description: Expose typed scene helpers with live runtime updates.
outcomeResults.reason: Typed helpers produce line-node builders, and dynamic samples a builder each frame, validates segments, replaces changed runtime nodes, supports visibility and cleans up subscriptions and owned nodes. The historical focused unit pass predates changes to runtime dependencies and is unbound.

outcomeResults.description: text output
outcomeResults.reason: ASCII output bounds dimensions and sampling, converts RGBA luminance to text, optionally updates an accessible element, captures a private target and restores caller-owned DOM on disposal. It documents black-background/straight-alpha semantics; the previous unit result is unbound.

outcomeResults.description: Render accessible DOM labels in 2D and 3D and document occlusion and event limitations.
outcomeResults.reason: Screen and perspective DOM labels retain accessible semantics and the renderer and exported capability explicitly describe anchor-only occlusion and pointer limitations. A browser test exists but no matching current visual or accessibility pass was inspected.

outcomeResults.description: Axes/grids
outcomeResults.reason: The public helpers namespace builds colored axes, Cartesian grids and polar grids with finite dimensions and bounded segment counts. A parity unit test enumerates and checks these builders; no current source-identity-bound result was found.

outcomeResults.description: Produce independent SVG output with clipping, projected geometry and supported styles.
outcomeResults.reason: SVG output implements homogeneous clipping, projected triangles/lines/points, painter ordering and supported flat styles. Its position read assumes the primary stream and returns raw values, despite valid Geometry supporting separate and normalized position streams, so projected geometry coverage is incomplete.

outcomeResults.description: Implement vector, text and stereo outputs with clear size, clipping, style, eye-order and resource semantics.
outcomeResults.reason: The addon supplies vector, ASCII and stereo output with explicit clipping/sampling, resize, eye ordering and disposal. The vector implementation nevertheless cannot correctly project valid separate-stream or normalized-position Geometry, so the combined source requirement remains incomplete.

outcomeResults.description: Provide 2D and perspective DOM labels with transforms, stacking, accessibility and documented occlusion.
outcomeResults.reason: The DOM output projects screen and perspective planes, sorts by order/depth, preserves accessibility, supports caller-defined anchor occlusion, and restores borrowed elements. The existing focused unit result is unbound and real-browser acceptance remains unrun.

outcomeResults.description: Replace the previous spatial-label exclusion with an opt-in, explicitly bounded capability contract.
outcomeResults.reason: The engine exports an opt-in spatial-DOM capability with screen/perspective modes, accessibility, anchor occlusion, clipping and pointer boundaries. The old exclusion remains only as a deprecated compatibility constant; the previous public-export test result is unbound.

outcomeResults.description: Supply stereo, anaglyph and parallax-barrier outputs with correct viewport and eye ordering.
outcomeResults.reason: Separate eye views and targets use left-first side-by-side and over-under rectangles; anaglyph selects left red/right cyan and the barrier selects left-first strips. Resize, pointer mapping, prior target restoration and owned-resource disposal are implemented; prior mock tests are unbound.

outcomeResults.description: Provide bounded text-based output and disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: ASCII output limits cells, pixels and sampling work, supports character ramps and a supplied accessible DOM element, and disposes targets/restores element state. The focused unit log is historical and has no binding to the current source.

outcomeResults.description: dynamically updated transforms
outcomeResults.reason: The debug helper transforms lines on read, while public dynamic helpers resample caller state on frames and replace changed line nodes, including their transform options. Source tests cover affine changes and frame updates; the prior run is unbound to the current tree.

outcomeResults.description: Add grounded sky, shadow projection and volume slice objects using existing renderer facilities.
outcomeResults.reason: The addon builds grounded gradient/panorama nodes, projected bounds or triangle shadows, and editable grayscale volume slices using renderer facilities. Triangle projection rejects overlapping projected interiors, as occur for ordinary closed solids, and handles only static horizontal snapshots; native WebGPU rejects the grounded gradient when background fog is enabled. Focused and dedicated tests exist, but no current-identity-bound result was found.

outcomeResults.description: sky/water
outcomeResults.reason: Public sky and water builders and world-water passes exist. WebGPU explicitly rejects public Preetham/HDRI and gradient bands, stars, clouds, moon and background fog. Water reflection/refraction is tier-dependent, falls back when planar input is absent, and its reflection producer currently redraws only terrain from its requested layers.

outcomeResults.description: Test determinism, bounds, topology, budgets, undo data and teardown.
outcomeResults.reason: The requested unit file contains assertions for seeded determinism, bounds, outward topology, budgets, undo/redo, invalid inputs and idempotent teardown. An earlier log reports 16 tests passed, but it records no content identity for the shared working tree; this audit did not run tests.

outcomeResults.description: Environment helpers, reflection/refraction surfaces, sky/water, lens flares, marching surfaces, grounded backgrounds, procedural tree/forest/terrain/city/street objects, sculpting, tube painting and convex fracture.
outcomeResults.reason: The listed capabilities have substantial implementation, including public sky/water and lens-flare paths and addon generators and tools. The complete checklist is not integrated: scene-level refraction is not exposed as an addon surface, WebGPU rejects several sky variants, and material-index groups do not select materials through the standard primitive draw. Terrain height/raycast/collider paths include vertical origin.

outcomeResults.description: Implement every named specialized object, generator and editing tool as an opt-in module.
outcomeResults.reason: Six optional addon subpaths and their barrel exports exist. The broader named object list includes reflection/refraction and lens flares: the engine exposes a mirror and lens flare, but no separate scene-level refractor addon is established, and lower-level glass requires a caller-supplied capture. Isosurface material-group rendering and terrain adapter integration also have concrete gaps.

outcomeResults.description: Add bounded interactive deformation with normals and undo-compatible edits.
outcomeResults.reason: Sculptor enforces vertex, triangle and displacement limits, recalculates normals, emits independent dynamic geometry snapshots, and records conflict-checked reversible edits. It explicitly rejects unsupported attribute streams; callers own picking and mounted GPU resources. The previous focused test log is not bound to current source content.

outcomeResults.description: Verify visible procedural outputs, picking and edit operations.
outcomeResults.reason: The requested browser spec is authored with visible-pixel assertions for generated geometry and specialized objects, plus real mesh picking, sculpt edits and undo. The row asks for rendered verification, which is post-freeze acceptance; no matching current-source browser receipt was found and no browser was run in this audit.

outcomeResults.description: Bound memory and polygon generation, support seed reproducibility and undo data, and test invalid inputs and teardown.
outcomeResults.reason: Bounded generator/isosurface/brush/tube/fracture implementations and representative repeatability, undo, invalid-input and teardown tests exist. The named lens-flare implementation has no element-count limit and allocates a material and render item for each element, leaving the general memory and polygon-generation requirement incomplete. An earlier focused unit pass is unbound and did not cover that gap.

outcomeResults.description: tube painting
outcomeResults.reason: TubePainter accepts bounded path points, creates transported-frame side geometry with normals, UVs and optional caps, supports removing points, and disposes its owned path. It rejects duplicate/reversing points and collapsed or inverted triangles. The prior focused pass does not bind the current tree.

outcomeResults.description: marching surfaces
outcomeResults.reason: The opt-in marching surface polygonizes a bounded editable scalar field, produces normals, colors and material groups, and supports sample undo. However materialIndex groups are only copied into production geometry: the public primitive accepts one material and the forward draw resolves a single draw range, so the authored per-sample material slots do not become separate rendered materials. Deferred admission explicitly rejects grouped geometry.

outcomeResults.description: Add deterministic convex fracture geometry and explicit unsupported cases.
outcomeResults.reason: fractureConvex validates closed, consistently wound convex triangle solids, clips seeded or explicit planes, caps fragments and enforces triangle and fragment budgets. Unsupported UV/color/custom streams, morphs, draw ranges and non-convex or open solids are explicitly rejected. The emitted cap material group is metadata; the ordinary primitive path does not itself choose a separate material for each group.

outcomeResults.description: Generate editable isosurfaces with bounded buffers, normals and material data.
outcomeResults.reason: Editable tetrahedral isosurfaces have hard sample/triangle caps, reversible sample edits, normals, interpolated RGBA and material-index groups. Those group indices are not integrated into multi-material rendering through geometry.custom: its primitive has a single material, the forward path draws the resolved range without iterating groups, and deferred geometry rejects groups.

outcomeResults.description: reflection/refraction surfaces
outcomeResults.reason: The public scene API exposes horizontal planar mirrors and world-water has reflection/refraction passes; the rendering package can construct glass/water surfaces from live capture results. There is no corresponding scene-level refractor addon in the inspected surface API, and an unbound lower-level request reports unsupported rather than creating a live refraction capture.

outcomeResults.description: convex fracture
outcomeResults.reason: Seeded and explicit-plane convex fracture constructs capped independently renderable geometry, preserves deterministic output and refuses unsupported streams, open/nonmanifold meshes and concavities. The cap's material group is returned as data, not automatically rendered as a separate material by the single-material primitive API. The prior focused pass is not candidate-bound.

outcomeResults.description: procedural tree/forest/terrain/city/street objects
outcomeResults.reason: Seeded terrain, tree, forest, city and four street-furniture kinds emit geometry and placements within resource budgets. The generated mesh and reused terrain height/raycast/collider paths all include vertical origin. The existing generator test checks its own result; candidate-bound integration remains open.

outcomeResults.description: lens flares
outcomeResults.reason: lights.lensFlare is public, creates a lensflare scene node and the production compiler generates additive sprite items with resource disposal. The documented occlusion modes only use frustum/edge visibility, not scene-geometry occlusion, and element count is currently unbounded; no current-bound pass was found.

outcomeResults.description: Reuse the existing terrain, sky, water and scatter facilities where they satisfy the contract
outcomeResults.reason: The grounded sky uses createDayNightSky, forest uses the existing scatterInArea, and water and terrain builders remain public. The generated relative grid and world terrain height/raycast/collider paths incorporate vertical origin. Full candidate-bound integration remains open.

outcomeResults.description: Reuse the existing terrain, sky, water and scatter facilities where they satisfy the contract; do not replace working paths.
outcomeResults.reason: Sky and scatter are directly reused, and existing terrain and water APIs remain. The world terrain height/raycast/collider paths include vertical origin. This limited source inspection cannot establish that every shared-runtime path is unchanged.

outcomeResults.description: asset licensing
outcomeResults.reason: The optional package declares MIT and the asset pipeline has SPDX allowlists and rejects unknown/noncompliant candidates; provenance tests exist. Those controls do not establish license and attribution coverage for every shipped asset/example. The WP-15 browser spec uses an in-memory panorama rather than an external image fixture; a project-wide rights inventory was not independently audited.

outcomeResults.description: grounded backgrounds
outcomeResults.reason: Grounded gradient and equirectangular panorama backgrounds are exposed with bounded geometry and caller-owned textures. The background's gradient sky inherits an explicit WebGPU rejection when background fog is enabled. Existing unit/browser sources are not a retained rendered pass.

outcomeResults.description: sculpting
outcomeResults.reason: The opt-in Sculptor implements bounded local-space brush deformation, normals and bounds, replayable typed undo/redo edits, dynamic snapshots and idempotent disposal. It rejects unsupported attribute streams and leaves input/picking integration to the caller. The earlier focused pass has no current content binding.

outcomeResults.description: Add deterministic terrain, tree, forest, city and street-asset generators with seeds and resource budgets.
outcomeResults.reason: All five seeded generators and geometry/instance budgets are present and have deterministic-output tests. The generator stores heights relative to origin, and world.terrain now adds vertical origin to height/raycast/collider calculations. Candidate-bound adapter integration is not established.

outcomeResults.description: do not replace working paths.
outcomeResults.reason: The ledger baseline commit is the current HEAD. A scoped read-only diff shows the original sky, water, terrain and scatter builder files match it, and the water-runtime change only substitutes an import. Other shared runtime and rendering files are modified, so this limited source comparison does not prove all pre-existing working paths preserve their behavior.

outcomeResults.description: Add path-based tube drawing with normals, caps and disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: TubePainter creates editable local-space path geometry with transported normals, optional end caps, UVs and limits, and drops owned points on disposal. Fewer than two points return null; duplicate/reversing points and degenerate float32 triangles are rejected. The earlier test pass is not bound to the current source identity.

outcomeResults.description: assets
outcomeResults.reason: This associated editor-assets row is outside the worker files but was inspected: the shell mounts an asset panel with placement and record operations, yet its two import actions use a generated triangle and a hard-coded Fox fixture, and reimport only changes metadata rather than loading an arbitrary asset again.

outcomeResults.description: Support initial scene, dynamic updates, asynchronous assets, frame scheduling and backend loss inside the worker.
outcomeResults.reason: Worker initialization and serialized replacement use the production compiler with asset cancellation; scheduler and device loss/recovery exist. The root bridge publishes a new scene before it succeeds and marks an explicitly recoverable replacement failure terminal even if the old renderer is restored; raw frame timestamps also let animated rendering jump after suspension.

outcomeResults.description: Transfer canvas ownership once; define message ordering, request IDs, resize/input snapshots, errors and cancellation.
outcomeResults.reason: The transfer guard, increasing IDs, ordered worker tail, typed resize/input/error messages and out-of-band cancellation are implemented. Protocol test source exercises transfer, ordering and cancellation, but no passing current-source receipt was located.

outcomeResults.description: worker failure
outcomeResults.reason: Transport failure rejects pending work and terminates, and the worker classifies frame/device failures. The root integration loses the recoverable classification for a failed replacement after the old renderer is restored, leaving the public app in a terminal failure state until another replacement succeeds.

outcomeResults.description: Transfer canvas ownership once
outcomeResults.reason: The host checks support, scene, dimensions and cloneability before transfer and records both the original and offscreen canvas to reject reuse. The explicit unsupported fallback is chosen before transfer.

outcomeResults.description: Verify worker OffscreenCanvas compositing and unavailable fallback. Exclusive execution owner: wp16_workers. Source verification: Direct Vitest for this file.
outcomeResults.reason: Offscreen compositing, manifest export/validation, VFX URL resolution, an explicit atlas override, nested worker lookup and packaged factory sources exist. The texture test checks thrown errors when canvas/2D is unavailable but does not verify the production scalar-material fallback, although the outer texture upgrade implements that fallback. The specified retarget-timeout test checks timeout and cleanup but not nested URL resolution; another asset test covers the URL. The required direct current-source Vitest result is not evidenced.

outcomeResults.description: Implement and source-test worker frame scheduling, pooled workers and same-origin fixture worker. Exclusive execution owner: wp16_workers. Source verification: Direct source Vitest for worker scheduler and pool; source typecheck browser fixture.
outcomeResults.reason: Scheduler, bounded pool, test sources and the same-origin fixture worker exist. The scheduler passes unclamped wall-clock time to rendering despite bounding its delta, and no passing direct scheduler/pool source-test or browser-fixture typecheck receipt for the current source was found.

outcomeResults.description: Define typed init, scene, input, resize, frame, error and dispose messages with request IDs.
outcomeResults.reason: The discriminated protocol declares ID-bearing init, scene, input, resize, frame, visibility, cancellation, dispose and error responses, with ID zero reserved for unsolicited device/presentation events.

outcomeResults.description: Verify rendered pixels, resize, input and clean teardown on supported backends.
outcomeResults.reason: Browser test source checks real WebGL2 pixels, input-driven scene changes, resize and duplicate disposal, and separately checks WebGPU pixels and termination when an adapter exists. The actual supported-backend rendered verification is deferred; WebGPU explicitly skips when unsupported, and no matching current-candidate browser receipt was found.

outcomeResults.description: Test message ordering, transfer ownership, errors, cancellation and disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: Protocol test source covers ordering, transfer ownership, errors, cancellation and disposal, but this row explicitly requires the test and no passing execution bound to the audited source was located. Existence of the assertions is not a test pass.

outcomeResults.description: Expose whether a render failure is terminal or recoverable; suppress late callbacks after disposal and test recovery.
outcomeResults.reason: The low-level host suppresses unsolicited callbacks during disposal, error messages carry severity, and recovery test sources exist. Public root scene replacement still reports a recoverable, restored failure as terminal, and no current bound recovery-test result was found.

outcomeResults.description: Add worker-owned rendering with a typed message protocol, input/resize bridging, safe transfer and teardown.
outcomeResults.reason: The public worker entry and createAuraApp worker option are wired to typed messages, event bridging, guarded transfer and worker teardown. The root bridge misclassifies a recoverable failed scene replacement as terminal; low-level dispose can resolve after forced termination without acknowledgement. Current integration and backend execution is not evidenced.

outcomeResults.description: Own the transferred canvas and renderer; synchronize resources, cancellation, loss and shutdown.
outcomeResults.reason: The worker owns the transferred canvas and renderer, mounts and restores scenes, cancels operations, watches device loss and disposes owned snapshot textures. Synchronization is limited to explicitly transferable resources and bounded CPU-backed 2D textures; source-backed, storage, render-attachment and shared mutable backings are rejected. Normal dispose resolves on an unacknowledged timeout; disposeStrict now reports that condition.

outcomeResults.description: Test unsupported browser fallback, termination, duplicate disposal and no retained workers/listeners.
outcomeResults.reason: There are source cases for pre-transfer fallback, one termination, repeated disposal, listener removal and pointer capture cleanup, plus a conditional browser fallback case. The requested tests have no current-source-bound pass; browser acceptance was not run.

outcomeResults.description: define message ordering, request IDs, resize/input snapshots, errors and cancellation.
outcomeResults.reason: Host requests have increasing IDs, the worker serializes ordinary operations while cancellation aborts the target, and typed snapshots and severity-bearing errors are forwarded. Pointer and key event buffers are bounded and expose overflow for state reconciliation.

outcomeResults.description: Define hidden-page suspension/resume, bounded catch-up, resize/DPR changes while hidden and temporal-history reset without changing explicit manual-step semantics.
outcomeResults.reason: Explicit steps remain exact, hidden scheduling is suspended and queued resizes/history are maintained. Automatic delta is clamped but the unbounded wall timestamp is still sent to render-time animation, and visibility resume does not itself remeasure DPR or size, so the full hidden catch-up and resize contract is not established.

outcomeResults.description: Expose whether a render failure is terminal or recoverable
outcomeResults.reason: Low-level AuraWorkerError and protocol responses expose recoverable versus terminal, but the root integration's failed setScene handler defaults to terminal even for a recoverable worker response after restoration. A caller of the root app therefore cannot rely on this distinction on that path.

outcomeResults.description: Add explicit OffscreenCanvas handling without breaking DOM targets.
outcomeResults.reason: Canvas resolution and configuration explicitly recognize OffscreenCanvas while retaining DOM selector, canvas and container paths; worker backing size and DPR are validated. Source tests exercise the offscreen case; no browser pass is claimed.

outcomeResults.description: Worker-owned rendering
outcomeResults.reason: The public worker factory/entry and createAuraApp worker branch transfer the canvas and install a worker-owned production renderer. Supported scene restrictions and explicit fallback are part of the implementation; real WebGL/WebGPU rendering has not been verified in this audit.

outcomeResults.description: Emit a same-origin worker entry for packaged rendering consumers. Exclusive execution owner: wp16_workers. Source verification: Worker source and installed subpath tests.
outcomeResults.reason: The host-only source factory uses a statically discoverable module-worker URL; the worker installs the manifest/runtime, and finalization is wired to emit a bundled worker and explicit asset URLs. Package-layout and bundle tests use synthetic fixture/build data and an installed-consumer fixture exists, but the specifically required installed-subpath execution has no current-candidate receipt.

outcomeResults.description: resource transfer
outcomeResults.reason: Canvas and explicitly supplied transferable resources are sent, and eligible CPU-backed 2D textures are copied and reconstructed with bounded ownership. The unqualified resource-transfer checklist is not fully implemented for live canvas/video/GPU, storage, render-attachment, compressed/depth, array/3D or shared-mutable texture resources; those are rejected or require another path.

outcomeResults.description: Support worker scheduling and input snapshots; define hidden-page catch-up, resume/history reset and terminal versus recoverable frame errors.
outcomeResults.reason: The dedicated scheduler serializes frames, delivers input snapshots, handles hidden visibility, history reset and classified failures. Its catch-up limit applies to deltaSeconds but not the render timestamp used by animated scenes, and the host does not remeasure DPR on visibility resume. The ordinary frameLoop independently retains DOM visibility handling.

outcomeResults.description: suppress late callbacks after disposal and test recovery.
outcomeResults.reason: The host suppresses device/frame/error callbacks after disposal starts and source cases cover loss, explicit recovery and late messages. The root integration can nevertheless publish a recoverable failed replacement as terminal, and the requested current recovery-test pass is unestablished.

outcomeResults.description: Provide bounded tasks, cancellation and worker teardown for opt-in processing.
outcomeResults.reason: The opt-in publicly exported WorkerPool bounds concurrency and waiting tasks, delays transfer until dispatch, removes cancelled queued tasks, terminates a worker on running cancellation, and retires workers/listeners during disposal. Unit test source covers these cases.

outcomeResults.description: input/resize bridge
outcomeResults.reason: The host bridge forwards content-box pointer and keyboard snapshots, bounded event history, visibility and measured resize/DPR, and cleans up listeners, observer and captures. However, visibility restoration sends only a visibility message and does not remeasure; a DPR change without an associated resize notification is missed.

outcomeResults.description: Worker-owned rendering, input/resize bridge, task pool, resource transfer, worker failure and teardown.
outcomeResults.reason: Worker rendering, the input bridge, bounded pool and failure/teardown paths exist. Full generic resource transfer remains restricted to explicit transferables and bounded CPU texture snapshots; DPR can remain stale on resume, root replacement can misclassify recoverable failure, and normal teardown can resolve without worker acknowledgement.

outcomeResults.description: teardown
outcomeResults.reason: Acknowledged worker shutdown waits for scheduling, renderer and snapshot cleanup; host disposal is shared/idempotent and attempts all listener and worker cleanup. Unlike the stale checkpoint, disposeStrict now reports timeout/host cleanup failures and root disposeAsync uses it. Nevertheless the public low-level dispose still resolves after forced termination without worker cleanup acknowledgement, so completed worker-side disposal is not guaranteed on that path.

outcomeResults.description: resource-lifetime verification with scoped
outcomeResults.reason: Resource-lifetime test sources cover worker snapshot ownership, listener removal and repeated renderer resource release, and documentation explicitly scopes browser/device evidence. No current-candidate source/integration verification receipt or post-freeze browser, performance, visual and device matrix was found; those are not inferred from tests or historical artifacts.

outcomeResults.description: Provide keyboard operation, compact density and accessible error, loading and empty states. Use the repository's licensed typography and density rules; do not introduce remote font services.
outcomeResults.reason: Local compact Whitney styling and announced graph/texture states exist without a remote font service. Arbitrary reparenting lacks a keyboard path, inspector errors go to a non-live console, asset import lacks visible loading/error handling, and the applicable font-use grant is not established by inspected evidence.

outcomeResults.description: Inspect real texture metadata, formats, mips and resource state.
outcomeResults.reason: The mounted panel inspects real direct and embedded asset texture handles, reporting descriptor format, dimensions, mip data and resource status. Its scope excludes runtime-only textures and it correctly labels GPU residency unavailable.

outcomeResults.description: Include licensed editor font assets with recorded provenance. Exclusive execution owner: wp17_editor. Source verification: Typography source contract and license verification.
outcomeResults.reason: Three local WOFF2 assets exist, byte-match the named Whitney library cuts, and their source filenames and EULA reference are recorded. The test checks files and typography, but no retained grant establishing this editor's use and redistribution, including the embedded export font, was found in the inspected evidence.

outcomeResults.description: Provide keyboard operation, compact density and accessible error, loading and empty states. Use the repository's licensed typography and density rules
outcomeResults.reason: Graph and texture panels have keyboard-friendly controls and status announcements, and the editor uses compact self-hosted typography. Arbitrary hierarchy reparenting is mouse drag/drop-only, inspector errors lack a live announcement, asset import lacks visible loading/error handling, and the specific font-use grant was not established.

outcomeResults.description: Connect graph editing to real material state and the renderer compiler
outcomeResults.reason: The shell stores material-targeted graph edits and compiles GLSL/WGSL; ProjectSceneRuntime builds, device-compiles and installs real graph materials in the WebGL2 viewport. Some imported geometry, including morph targets and eight-influence skins, remains explicitly unsupported.

outcomeResults.description: Integrate persisted graph state, live renderer inspection and licensed compact typography. Exclusive execution owner: wp17_editor. Source verification: tests/unit/editor/native-shader-graph-editor.test.ts and typography source contract.
outcomeResults.reason: The app serializes graph/editor state, uses local compact Whitney styles, and reads real renderer inspection data. Frame instrumentation explicitly omits phases and whole-frame timings, and the inspected records do not establish the font redistribution grant; the existing source contract has no current-source passing receipt.

outcomeResults.description: Replace bounded fixture behavior with a real typed graph backed by WP-05.
outcomeResults.reason: The publicly exported ShaderGraphModel edits the native compiler's graph IR, describes typed inputs, validates and compiles through the rendering package, and supports history. The older fixture function remains separately exported, but the mounted editor uses the live model.

outcomeResults.description: Test graph validation, undo, persistence, resource selection and errors.
outcomeResults.reason: The requested source test file contains assertions for typed graph edits, cycles and invalid drafts, undo/redo, migration and persistence, resource selection, texture state and error handling. Its presence is not evidence that it passed on this working tree.

outcomeResults.description: Inspect actual textures, passes, timing and resources
outcomeResults.reason: Panels consume real asset textures, renderer counters and observed graph-pass timings; the profiler now shows a measured viewport CPU sample or 'Unavailable'. Actual renderer tracing remains explicitly incomplete for multiple phases and whole-frame CPU/GPU timing is null.

outcomeResults.description: frame inspector
outcomeResults.reason: The mounted frame inspector displays real counters and observed graph passes with explicit unavailable states. The renderer marks every capture partial and leaves whole-frame CPU/GPU times null; its separate per-view GPU timing is not passed through this inspector.

outcomeResults.description: serialization
outcomeResults.reason: Versioned graph documents, resource bindings and editor selection state serialize and migrate; the editor Save/Load path uses the app serializer and clears obsolete history on load.

outcomeResults.description: Connect graph editing to real material state and the renderer compiler; provide typed ports, cycle errors, undo and serialization.
outcomeResults.reason: The mounted material-graph path connects typed model ports to native compiler validation, supports cycle diagnostics and chronological graph undo, serializes graph records, and installs compiled material candidates on the renderer. Compute graph editing is explicitly unavailable.

outcomeResults.description: provide typed ports, cycle errors, undo and serialization.
outcomeResults.reason: The graph model exposes compatible typed ports and native validation, including cycles; edits use undoable commands and the project serializer preserves graph documents and resource choices, including invalid drafts.

outcomeResults.description: live shader graph
outcomeResults.reason: The selected material graph is edited and automatically compiled from current project records, then attached to the real viewport material. The editor intentionally exposes material graphs rather than compute preview, and not all imported deformation modes are supported.

outcomeResults.description: Scene/project editor, hierarchy, properties, assets, animation, live shader graph, frame inspector, texture inspector, profiling, serialization, undo/redo and static export.
outcomeResults.reason: The shell mounts the editor panels, persists projects, renders real graph materials, and exports a standalone scene. Remaining gaps include incomplete frame telemetry, no general user-selected glTF import, timeline preview/play controls not connected to the actual animation mixer, and hierarchy reorder bypassing and invalidating scene command history.

outcomeResults.description: Expose actual frame passes, draw/resource counts, timings and diagnostics.
outcomeResults.reason: FrameInspector exposes observed graph passes, draw/resource counters, timings where supplied and diagnostics. The actual renderer marks shadow/contributor/post/native phases unobserved and provides null whole-frame CPU/GPU timings; the separate partial view GPU timing is not exposed by FrameInspector.

outcomeResults.description: Connect live material graphs to compiler output and diagnostics without exposing secrets.
outcomeResults.reason: The public ShaderGraphInspector compiles the supplied current graph and returns allowlisted binding/stage information with sanitized diagnostics and anonymized expressions; the mounted shell supplies the material record. It intentionally omits raw source, literals and graph-owned names.

outcomeResults.description: Create/edit/reload a graph and verify the rendered material changes.
outcomeResults.reason: The requested browser-spec source creates and edits a material graph, compares actual WebGL pixels, saves/reloads, and checks the reloaded pixels against the edited result. This establishes the test implementation only, not a browser execution or rendered-pixel acceptance pass.

outcomeResults.description: Provide graph editing, typed ports, validation, errors, undo and compile feedback.
outcomeResults.reason: The mounted graph panel provides node editing, type-filtered ports and outputs, undo/redo, compile feedback and announced diagnostics via the live graph controller. Its explicit scope is material graphs and supported resource kinds, not compute graph editing.

outcomeResults.description: profiling
outcomeResults.reason: The profiler displays a real synchronous viewport preparation/submission CPU sample and counters, or explicitly 'Unavailable' without a sample. The earlier unlabeled capped timing fallback is no longer present; this is CPU profiling and does not claim complete GPU/pass timing.

outcomeResults.description: Regress per-app stage trace isolation, timing, failure and disposal. Exclusive execution owner: wp17_editor/debug_inspectors. Source verification: Direct Vitest for this file.
outcomeResults.reason: The dedicated test covers trace-instance isolation, CPU timing, failure propagation, late work and disposal. It instantiates trace objects directly rather than exercising two actual applications or renderers, so the requested per-app integration regression is not established; no current passing receipt was found.

outcomeResults.description: texture inspector
outcomeResults.reason: The mounted texture inspector selects live direct and embedded asset handles and displays format, mips and resource status, including an honest unavailable GPU-residency state. Runtime-only textures outside the project asset lists are not enumerated.

outcomeResults.description: Mount functional graph/texture/frame inspector panels and keyboard-accessible actions.
outcomeResults.reason: Graph, texture and frame panels are mounted and provide native controls and announced statuses. The frame panel receives explicitly incomplete telemetry, and arbitrary hierarchy reparenting has no keyboard equivalent.

outcomeResults.description: Inspect actual textures, passes, timing and resources; avoid fixture-only visualizations.
outcomeResults.reason: Inspection is not fixture-only: project texture handles, actual device counters, observed pass measurements and viewport CPU timing are used. Several render phases are untraced, whole-frame CPU/GPU timings remain null, and available per-view GPU samples are not shown in the editor inspector.

outcomeResults.description: properties
outcomeResults.reason: The mounted properties inspector edits transforms and project fields with commands, validates input, and supports an empty selection. Its error announcement and undo after a hierarchy rebuild are separate limitations.

outcomeResults.description: Scene/project editor
outcomeResults.reason: The scene/project shell mounts an actual renderer, hierarchy and property editor with save/load and standalone export. Its asset browser only offers a generated sample or a fixed Fox GLB rather than a general user-selected model import; hierarchy reorder also bypasses and invalidates scene history.

outcomeResults.description: Trace per-renderer post stages and resources without cross-app state. Exclusive execution owner: wp17_editor/inspectors. Source verification: Editor inspector source tests.
outcomeResults.reason: Trace objects are renderer-owned and record executed graph passes, resource names, CPU durations and draw deltas without global trace state. The actual renderer expressly marks post and other phases unobserved, so real post-stage/resource tracing is not complete; tests exercise isolated trace objects.

outcomeResults.description: Prove create/edit/reload changes rendered pixels and that invalid graphs show actionable diagnostics.
outcomeResults.reason: The browser spec includes pixel comparisons across edit and reload and assertions for invalid-graph diagnostics, but no matching retained current-source browser run or pixel receipt was found. The requested proof is deferred live/rendered acceptance.

outcomeResults.description: hierarchy
outcomeResults.reason: Hierarchy supports create, selection, rename, delete and drag/drop reparenting, but arbitrary reparenting is not keyboard-operable. Up/Down reorder bypasses command history and replaces the Scene while existing scene-node commands still reference the old Scene, so subsequent undo may not affect the displayed scene.

outcomeResults.description: Serialize graph, selected resources and editor state with versioned migrations.
outcomeResults.reason: The runtime project envelope persists graph documents, typed resource bindings and editor selections, migrates version 1 selections to version 2, and rejects unsupported versions while allowing editable invalid graph drafts. The app serializer shares this migration.

outcomeResults.description: undo/redo
outcomeResults.reason: Command history, graph/property edits, toolbar actions and keyboard undo/redo are wired, and loading a project clears stale history. Hierarchy reorder is not a command and rebuilds the Scene without clearing or rebinding earlier node-referencing commands, so it cannot itself be undone and can make prior transform/create/reparent undo act on obsolete objects.

outcomeResults.description: avoid fixture-only visualizations.
outcomeResults.reason: The inspection visualizations are not fixture-only: they read real project texture handles and renderer graph-pass/device data, while the profiler uses observed viewport CPU timing or explicitly shows 'Unavailable'. Completeness of phase and GPU telemetry remains a separate partial outcome.

outcomeResults.description: do not introduce remote font services.
outcomeResults.reason: The editor declares self-hosted Whitney WOFF2 files and local fallback faces, and the standalone export embeds a WOFF2 data URI. The inspected editor font declarations contain no remote font service; the existing source contract checks for Google font endpoints.

outcomeResults.description: Supply ledger findings to WP-00, its sole owner. Replace historical exclusion language only when the corresponding implementation and installed entrypoint exist.
outcomeResults.reason: Historical exclusions are labeled as such and the appendix conditions support on an installed entrypoint. The corresponding WP-18 ledger row remains unverified with no recorded source evidence; the inspected artifacts do not establish a findings handoff to WP-00.

outcomeResults.description: Automated source, integration, browser, performance, visual, device and resource-lifetime verification with scoped, honest product claims.
outcomeResults.reason: Source/integration steps, lifecycle assertions and visual/performance acceptance specs exist, but the normal source runner is deliberately blocked before executing them and product documentation still describes a removed renderer as available. Browser, performance, visual and device acceptance are separately unrun, not failed source tests.

outcomeResults.description: examples
outcomeResults.reason: A ten-case typed-asset catalog and a project-construction harness exist, and the referenced mini-game model's current bytes match its manifest hash. Coverage of all required example families is not established: the catalog has no dedicated worker, interchange exporter, audio or XR scenario, although other examples elsewhere in the repository may cover some of these.

outcomeResults.description: Promote only the exact capabilities supported by retained source, browser and device evidence.
outcomeResults.reason: The claims document requires exact candidate, packed-path, browser and device evidence and records bounded historical claims. Ten named 4.5.0 receipt identities and their referenced frame digests were inspected, including a passing software-rendered contact-shadow receipt; they do not certify the changed 4.7.1 working tree. Not every other linked promotion and its exact receipt was independently reconciled, so universal compliance cannot be established.

outcomeResults.description: Keep the ledger current
outcomeResults.reason: The ledger and validator are present, but the current ledger has 1,901 source-incomplete rows, only 25 rows with source evidence and 21 with public entrypoints. Its own WP-18 task remains unverified and empty, so the ledger is not current as a record of implementation and exposure.

outcomeResults.description: complete every row and retain proof of public exposure, not merely internal classes.
outcomeResults.reason: No outcome is marked source-complete; only 21 of 1,901 rows list any public entrypoint and 25 list source evidence. The representative WP-18 row has neither public entrypoints nor retained evidence. These are missing ledger proofs, not proof that all referenced features lack source implementations.

outcomeResults.description: Document actual backend, hardware, resource, format and lossy-export limitations. Each public feature has an Aura3D-owned runnable example with typed assets.
outcomeResults.reason: Backend, resource and format/loss documentation and typed-model examples exist. However, the backend selection description contradicts the current root selection and fallback source, and the example index does not provide a dedicated scenario for each public capability family.

outcomeResults.description: Document backend selection, depth/clipping, draw state, transparency, camera views, color output, shader layouts, hardware requirements, fallback, loss and supported feature matrix.
outcomeResults.reason: The backend page covers the requested categories and labels device claims as unverified, but it says root WebGPU selection does not exist, the profile throws and backend is unknown-typed. Current types, option resolution and compiler implement WebGPU/auto selection and conditional fallback. It also says generic vertex types are float32-only while the source declares signed and unsigned integer types.

outcomeResults.description: Keep supported API examples and claim boundaries current. Exclusive execution owner: wp18_recovery. Source verification: Documentation link and snippet checks.
outcomeResults.reason: The five requested guides and documentation-checker source exist. The app guide still promises a removed safe-basic compatibility renderer/fallback, while scatter-merge calls primitives.custom, which is absent from the primitives namespace; the current custom geometry factory is geometry.custom. The snippets and links were not run against a packed candidate.

outcomeResults.description: Automated source
outcomeResults.reason: The source runner enumerates real typecheck, lint, unit, integration, package and documentation commands, with source-runner tests. But its normal wrapper unconditionally invokes the no-input workspace-admission gate, which throws, and the source image explicitly exits unavailable. Thus this integrated automation cannot currently execute end to end through its intended entrypoint; no source run was attempted in this audit.

outcomeResults.description: Keep the ledger current; complete every row and retain proof of public exposure, not merely internal classes.
outcomeResults.reason: The ledger and structural tests exist, but all 1,901 rows are marked source-incomplete. Current data contains source evidence on 25 rows and public entrypoints on 21, and the WP-18 completion row has neither. The counts describe retained ledger data, not a fresh judgment that all underlying code is missing.

outcomeResults.description: device
outcomeResults.reason: The device-specific disposition requires post-freeze physical-device acceptance, not additional source work for this row. The current matrix promotes no physical device; the existing synthetic matrix test rejects hardware claims without on-device provenance. No physical-device pass is claimed.

outcomeResults.description: Replace obsolete import/export, effects, worker and renderer exclusions with the new optional contracts.
outcomeResults.reason: The generated reference recasts exclusions as historical and mentions root effects, compute and XR, but still describes optional native contracts generically as planned and does not document the current worker and importer/exporter source subpaths as their own contracts. Its appendix is also not synchronized with the source appendix; installed availability remains unverified rather than presumed.

outcomeResults.description: Provide one isolated, runnable scenario per capability family with no unrelated engine runtime.
outcomeResults.reason: The index mounts one selected scenario around a typed hashed model and the harness constructs a project with the matching admitted asset. Its ten cases do not include dedicated worker, optional interchange importer/exporter, audio or XR scenarios, so the required isolated scenario per capability family is incomplete. Candidate build/browser runnability was not established.

outcomeResults.description: static export
outcomeResults.reason: For the editor static-export scope, the editor injects a bundled standalone runtime, snapshots project assets and glTF dependencies, emits HTML, JSON and JavaScript, and exposes downloads. The runtime rebuilds and renders the editor project; unit and browser test source cover these paths, but neither was run and no candidate visual pass is claimed.

outcomeResults.description: Enforce valid owners, statuses, paths, tests, and no unsupported completion claims.
outcomeResults.reason: The ledger test validates owners, statuses, safe paths and multiple completion/evidence conditions. It explicitly cannot prove a check exercised the required behavior or dereference remote artifacts, accepts a completed synthetic row with empty publicEntrypoints, and treats a well-formed remote evidence URI as supporting evidence; consequently it does not itself prevent every unsupported completion claim.

outcomeResults.description: Synchronize source API appendix with generated public documentation and bounded claims. Exclusive execution owner: wp18_docs/public_api_docs. Source verification: API documentation contract tests.
outcomeResults.reason: The source appendix has bounded/historical claim language and the generator has a contract test, but a direct current-file comparison shows its linear-extrusion and WebGPU mip-generation paragraphs are absent from the generated public reference. The two files are not synchronized.

outcomeResults.description: Provide runnable Aura3D-owned examples for each delivered capability family using typed admitted assets.
outcomeResults.reason: The prototype recipes explain admitting a typed model and running ten scenarios and add an advanced-lighting example. Dedicated recipes for each delivered family are not established, including worker and interchange; both principal TypeScript snippets are explicitly exempted from the documentation snippet checker, and the standalone lighting snippet uses primitives rather than an admitted typed asset.

outcomeResults.description: Document each import/export format, optional entrypoint, supported variants, loss cases and request/security rules.
outcomeResults.reason: The format page documents entrypoints, multiple bounded variants, export losses and request/security rules. Several implemented format families are still grouped as requirements to specify versions, units, dependencies and loss per format rather than supplying each contract; the source importer and exporter barrels expose additional concrete implementations. Installed-path and independent-round-trip claims remain explicitly unverified.

outcomeResults.description: honest product claims
outcomeResults.reason: The main rulebook requires evidence-scoped claims and identifies historical receipts, but public-facing documentation is not uniformly current: app-api still teaches safe-basic as an available compatibility renderer and fallback while the actual mount rejects it; scatter-merge also demonstrates a nonexistent primitives.custom call.

outcomeResults.description: browser
outcomeResults.reason: Browser execution is post-freeze acceptance for this row, not missing source implementation. Browser test source exists, but the candidate support matrix says acceptance has not run and no browser combination is promoted; no browser or visual pass is claimed.

outcomeResults.description: network activity are checked for prohibited engine implementation. Authorship requires recorded source provenance
