outcomeResults.description: Restore negotiated depth clear and comparison state across context lifetime. Exclusive execution owner: wp21_lifecycle. Source verification: tests/unit/rendering/native-camera-depth.test.ts.
outcomeResults.reason: The device accepts/stores a reversed convention, but beginFrame still selects LEQUAL and clear always sets depth to 1; the root renderer rejects nonstandard depth. The nominated camera-depth test primarily verifies projection metadata, not this GL lifecycle state.

outcomeResults.description: Scene/context loss, background suspension, resize, async loads, concurrent disposal and repeated remount have deterministic behavior. All owned resources and callbacks are released even when a disposer fails.
outcomeResults.reason: Visibility, async guards and final cleanup are implemented; remount teardown still permits one throwing unsubscribe/compute disposer to prevent the remaining retirements, and ownerless registry descriptors remain global on restore.

outcomeResults.description: Dispose every owned resource even after one disposer fails; aggregate errors and make repeated disposal idempotent. Cover mount/resize/loss/restore/dispose races and shared-resource ownership.
outcomeResults.reason: ResourceLifecycle aggregates failures and handles shared ownership, and final app disposal guards siblings; remount teardown is sequential and an earlier throw can prevent controller/physics cleanup.

outcomeResults.description: Provide bounded redaction helpers for app-scoped errors and asset events. Exclusive execution owner: wp21_lifecycle. Source verification: tests/unit/agent-api/multi-app-isolation.test.ts.
outcomeResults.reason: The helpers redact URL credentials, signed queries and sensitive fields and bound cyclic/getter-bearing data and top-level bigint formatting. Candidate-bound verification remains open.

outcomeResults.description: Bind live atmosphere updates to the correct app.
outcomeResults.reason: App/mount authority, frame invalidation and fog bindings are owner-bound and unsubscribe on disposal. Shared-canvas WebGPU device ownership and complete VFX isolation remain open.

outcomeResults.description: Introduce app/device-owned runtime context for color and shader policy, world/animation flags, caches, atmosphere, events and diagnostics. A newly created app must not reset or modify another active app.
outcomeResults.reason: Owner-keyed color/matrix caches now reach both rendering paths; shader state and actor state are scoped. World builders are still global on the actual public path and canvas-keyed fog can be overwritten by another app.

outcomeResults.description: Preserve async warmup and implement allocation/polling cleanup on shader/link failure, disposal or loss; integrate depth, clipping, state and color contracts requested by their owners.
outcomeResults.reason: Async compilation, polling cancellation and allocation cleanup are present, but the negotiated depth state is not used in beginFrame/clear and the renderer rejects nonstandard depth.

outcomeResults.description: Dispose all owned resources even if one fails; aggregate diagnostics and make repeated disposal safe.
outcomeResults.reason: ResourceLifecycle attempts every owned disposer in reverse order, aggregates errors, retains failed releases for retry and does not repeat successful cleanup.

outcomeResults.description: Add success-aware readiness, app-owned context, bounded errors, event cleanup, loss/restore and deterministic lifecycle races.
outcomeResults.reason: Readiness distinguishes supersession from abort; app-scoped world flags, fog and cleanup paths exist. Full remount cleanup, shared-canvas isolation and candidate-bound race coverage remain open.

outcomeResults.description: real readiness
outcomeResults.reason: React requests the renderer readiness outcome before exposing the app/onReady, handles non-ready results as errors, and checks mounted diagnostics for older settled-only peers.

outcomeResults.description: Fix pooled target double release
outcomeResults.reason: A target-only legacy release retires the object, while token releases check acquisition identity; duplicate releases cannot return a leased target twice.

outcomeResults.description: unregister on dispose and suppress late async completion. Test two apps sharing a page with different strictness, flags, scenes and failing assets.
outcomeResults.reason: Disposal clears the app event scope and suppresses later callbacks, and browser source covers independent apps and owned texture failures. The underlying texture.load is not cancelled and may still resolve a handle or rethrow a raw error after disposal.

outcomeResults.description: Scope diagnostic records and integrity/format statuses to the app; redact sensitive fields.
outcomeResults.reason: Diagnostics state and shader stores are app-owned and sanitized, but validateSceneAssets labels any URL ready without recording an actual integrity/format verification result.

outcomeResults.description: distinguish failure, cancellation, disposal and superseded mounts. Keep existing settled-only behavior during its documented transition.
outcomeResults.reason: Failure, disposal, supersession and signal cancellation have distinct outcomes in current source. Existing expectations conflict with supersession, and the requested migration period is not documented.

outcomeResults.description: aggregate errors and make repeated disposal idempotent. Cover mount/resize/loss/restore/dispose races and shared-resource ownership.
outcomeResults.reason: Final disposal and ResourceLifecycle aggregate sibling errors, but remount teardown makes unguarded sequential callbacks, and the requested comprehensive race matrix is not in the named async lifecycle test.

outcomeResults.description: concurrent disposal
outcomeResults.reason: Final disposal is reentrancy-guarded and controller cleanup can wait for active frames, but a throwing remount cleanup can leave later controller or physics retirement unattempted.

outcomeResults.description: repeated remount have deterministic behavior. All owned resources
outcomeResults.reason: Mount revisions cancel old readiness and abort stale work, but the remount teardown sequence can stop at an earlier throwing unsubscription or disposer before releasing later owners.

outcomeResults.description: Implement the section 3.5 readiness result for renderer and first-frame stages; distinguish failure, cancellation, disposal and superseded mounts. Keep existing settled-only behavior during its documented transition.
outcomeResults.reason: Renderer and first-frame readiness distinguish abort from supersession in current source; the documented migration/transition and complete candidate-bound verification remain missing.

outcomeResults.description: Track exclusive live leases separately from idle ownership; make repeated release safe, preserve nonnegative counts and retire resources by device generation.
outcomeResults.reason: The pool separates owned/idle/live leases, token-checks release and retires outstanding resources on device loss/restore with live nonnegative stats.

outcomeResults.description: diagnostic records
outcomeResults.reason: Per-app shader stores are bound to the runtime owner/device and snapshots sanitize records; the tests create separate stores and check redaction.

outcomeResults.description: Route events only to the owning app; unregister subscriptions on disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: The event-scope implementation dispatches only to the captured owner, clears subscribers on dispose, and isolates the explicit standalone compatibility channel.

outcomeResults.description: Scene/context loss
outcomeResults.reason: Loss guards, per-device registered pool/batch/particle rebuilds and tests now exist; nevertheless optional ownerless registry descriptors rebuild for any restoring device and remount teardown can stop after an early cleanup throw.

outcomeResults.description: Replace shared mutable mode and records with app/device-owned state.
outcomeResults.reason: Shader mode and bounded/redacted records are stored per owner and bound to the app device; legacy state is only the unbound fallback.

outcomeResults.description: Pooled targets have exclusive leases and nonnegative counts; duplicate release and restoration cannot alias active targets. Late shader compilation disposes abandoned programs and settles dead handles accurately.
outcomeResults.reason: Exclusive pool leases and generation invalidation are implemented; stale program completion calls dispose and settles handles, but a throwing disposer is swallowed and its program is not retained for retry.

outcomeResults.description: Verify mount/loss/resize/dispose races and visible recovery on supported paths.
outcomeResults.reason: The required browser specification source covers supersession/disposal and a WebGL loss/resize/restore path with pixel checks. It was not executed and is not a visual/device pass.

outcomeResults.description: Dispose asynchronously compiled programs that arrive after disposal or generation change
outcomeResults.reason: Late successful programs are disposed when stale by cache/device generation, but if that dispose throws the catch sees an already-failed handle and drops the program without a retryable owner or reported error.

outcomeResults.description: Replace process-wide parsing policy with app-scoped policy.
outcomeResults.reason: App registration and both legacy and compiled production frame paths use the same runtimeOwner for color parsing; an untracked test covers strict/disabled policies on both paths.

outcomeResults.description: callbacks are released even when a disposer fails
outcomeResults.reason: Final app disposal protects individual unsubscriptions, but remount invokes the internal loss unsubscribe before compute/controller/physics cleanup without per-action protection.

outcomeResults.description: Dispose every owned resource even after one disposer fails
outcomeResults.reason: ResourceLifecycle tries every tracked owner even on error, but app remount teardown still stops at the first unguarded cleanup failure.

outcomeResults.description: nonnegative counts
outcomeResults.reason: Pool counts are computed from live idle buckets and leased entries rather than decrementing unconstrained counters; tests cover stale and duplicate releases.

outcomeResults.description: Verify two independently configured apps do not affect each other or leak subscriptions.
outcomeResults.reason: The browser specification source creates differently configured apps, tests concurrent app-owned failing texture requests and strict color isolation. It has not been run and therefore does not establish actual browser acceptance.

outcomeResults.description: restoration cannot alias active targets. Late shader compilation disposes abandoned programs
outcomeResults.reason: Pool restoration retires outstanding tokens without aliasing, but an abandoned late shader program whose disposer throws is discarded without a retryable owner.

outcomeResults.description: Test delayed compile success/rejection after disposal, failed partial allocation, loss/recreation, repeated disposal and warmup settlement.
outcomeResults.reason: The nominated test source includes late success and rejection, generation loss/retry, repeated dispose, partial shader allocation/link failures, poll cancellation and warmup settlement.

outcomeResults.description: Scope actor extension flags and callbacks to the owning runtime.
outcomeResults.reason: Actor-extension flags are bound to runtime-owner identities, carried into the typed actor construction and cleared during app disposal; ownerless use retains a compatibility default.

outcomeResults.description: Cover failed/aborted/superseded mount, background resume, disposal and callback races.
outcomeResults.reason: The named async lifecycle source exercises unavailable submissions, concurrent state changes, queued disposal and invalid deltas, but not the requested failed/aborted/superseded mount, background-resume and callback-race matrix.

outcomeResults.description: Scope render-input/matrix caches by app and scene revision.
outcomeResults.reason: The current render-input cache is keyed by runtimeOwner, reset when the scene node array changes, and both compiled and legacy paths forward that owner. New tests cover same-canvas separate caches and both compiler modes.

outcomeResults.description: settle held handles accurately and reject new acquisitions on dead caches. Test partial shader allocations, link failures, polling cancellation, supported retry and warmup settlement.
outcomeResults.reason: Cache disposal/loss marks and settles held handles, refuses dead cache acquisition and precompile reports failure; named test sources cover partial allocations, links, polling, retry and warmup.

outcomeResults.description: Make error formatting safe for cycles, large values, unusual getters and big integers. Bound repeated error records and avoid leaking credentials or signed URLs.
outcomeResults.reason: Cycle-aware sanitization, bounded bigint formatting, worker listener record limits and URL/header redaction exist. Focused worker observer and frame probes cover hostile thrown values; broader transport and candidate-bound verification remain open.

outcomeResults.description: async loads
outcomeResults.reason: Mount requests, dynamic texture jobs and app-owned texture.load have abort/revision guards, including late work cleanup. Full candidate-bound lifecycle and device verification remain open.

outcomeResults.description: Remove cross-app mutable atmosphere state.
outcomeResults.reason: Fog bindings use a WeakMap and guarded cleanup, but the production atmosphere extension keys by canvas, not unique app owner; two apps on one canvas overwrite the same mutable fog binding.

outcomeResults.description: Test throwing disposers, shared ownership, cleanup order and idempotence.
outcomeResults.reason: The source test explicitly exercises reverse cleanup, throwing disposers, shared owners, repeated disposal and retry without repeating successful cleanup.

outcomeResults.description: Prevent acquisition after disposal, dispose late successful compiles, settle cancelled handles and retry only within the correct device generation.
outcomeResults.reason: Dead cache acquisitions are rejected and generations settle cancelled handles; late successful compiles call dispose. However a throwing late disposer is swallowed and the failed resource is no longer retained for retry.

outcomeResults.description: Asset requests, progress events, shader/color policy, render flags, diagnostics, resource ownership and disposal are scoped to the app or device. An app must not observe another app's events or alter its render state. Cleanup runs all owned disposers even if one fails; repeat disposal is safe.
outcomeResults.reason: Scopes, redaction, generations, app-owned world flags and fog, and aggregated cleanup paths exist. Ambiguous multi-app builder scope and the full remount/device race matrix remain open.

outcomeResults.description: disposal
outcomeResults.reason: React cleanup aborts its readiness controller, removes event handlers and disposes its app; shared preload resources abort pending work on final disposal.

outcomeResults.description: duplicate release
outcomeResults.reason: Release checks the unique active token; stale and duplicate releases cannot release a later lease, and legacy releases retire their targets.

outcomeResults.description: Enforce exclusive leases, idempotent release, device generations and accurate ownership. WP-21.
outcomeResults.reason: The pooled-target repair tracks exclusive leases and idle membership, retires lost-generation resources, rejects foreign/stale releases and derives ownership counts from live entries.

outcomeResults.description: Every app exposes truthful readiness, failure and cancellation; parallel apps isolate settings, events, resource ownership and diagnostic records.
outcomeResults.reason: Readiness and app-scoped shader/event stores exist; world builder defaults remain global, canvas-keyed fog is not fully isolated for same-canvas apps, and ownerless registry entries are rebuilt for every device.

outcomeResults.description: Add typed success/failure/cancellation readiness and bounded, redacted error formatting without breaking existing callers. WP-21.
outcomeResults.reason: Additive readiness and legacy ready compatibility are present; top-level bigint formatting is bounded, and focused worker conversion probes handle hostile values. Full candidate-bound verification remains open.

outcomeResults.description: Document the existing guarded remount behavior and the completed readiness and recovery contract.
outcomeResults.reason: The lifecycle document describes explicit remount and settled-only ready(), but not readiness(), readyStrict(), selected stages, a migration period or the newer guarded recovery behavior.

outcomeResults.description: Pooled targets have exclusive leases
outcomeResults.reason: Concurrent acquisitions receive token-specific leases, and active entries cannot be handed to another borrower.

outcomeResults.description: cancellation
outcomeResults.reason: Readiness distinguishes supersession from AbortSignal cancellation; React aborts superseded/unmounted waits and shared preload cancellation is owner-aware. Existing expectations conflict with the new superseded result, and candidate-bound verification remains open.

outcomeResults.description: failure
outcomeResults.reason: Root mount and first-frame failures produce failed outcomes; worker root errorDetails safely reads code/message, and worker observer/frame conversion handles hostile values in offline probes. Complete failure-settlement and candidate-bound verification remain open.

outcomeResults.description: Scope asset callbacks and redacted errors to their owner; unregister on dispose and suppress late async completion. Test two apps sharing a page with different strictness, flags, scenes and failing assets.
outcomeResults.reason: Event scopes and tests isolate/redact callbacks, but direct texture.load cannot be cancelled by app disposal and rethrows raw errors; the root model/other loaders are not wired into this event channel.

outcomeResults.description: Adopt generation-safe exclusive resource leases and per-device rebuild isolation. Exclusive execution owner: wp21_lifecycle. Source verification: tests/unit/rendering/native-resource-lifecycle.test.ts; tests/unit/contracts/impl/prd03-post-resources.test.ts.
outcomeResults.reason: Unlike the stale checkpoint, owned pool, batch and particle registrations carry device identities and ResourceRegistry filters those entries; new isolation tests exist. The registry still accepts ownerless legacy descriptors and deliberately rebuilds them for every device, so general per-device rebuild isolation is not complete.

outcomeResults.description: events
outcomeResults.reason: Emitted texture events are owner-scoped, redacted and unregistered, but the app callback channel is only connected to explicit texture.load, not the mounted model and other asset-loading paths.

outcomeResults.description: Coordinate frame pause/resume behavior with WP-16 and asset request ownership with WP-07/WP-05.
outcomeResults.reason: Frame loop implements visibility and explicit pause/resume; mount ownership and abort signals reach renderer/model work. The direct app-owned texture helper lacks cancellation and other asset formats are not connected to its event scope.

outcomeResults.description: Supported browser
outcomeResults.reason: Browser targets have versioned unverified labels, but those versions are planned Playwright distributions, not supported browser ranges. The current candidate has no promoted supported browser combination; actual support must await matching acceptance evidence.

outcomeResults.description: document unverified cells without blocking the source freeze.
outcomeResults.reason: All documented target cells are unverified, and source-phase producer report validation explicitly requires browser cells to remain not-run while allowing otherwise passing source reports. This source/acceptance distinction does not assert that the source freeze is otherwise ready.

outcomeResults.description: physical-device evidence remain separate
outcomeResults.reason: The policy and schema separate physical from software, injected and emulated evidence, and require physical provenance. However, the physical-label validator scans selected strings only: emulator markers in os.version or the observer are ignored, so not every contradictory physical label is rejected. No actual device provenance is authenticated here.

outcomeResults.description: Publish versioned backend/browser/OS support cells with exact evidence and limitations.
outcomeResults.reason: The published matrix identifies versioned browser/OS/backend targets, tiers and limitations and honestly states that current evidence is unavailable. It does not yet publish exact supported version ranges or candidate-bound evidence for any supported cell; the actual support evidence is post-freeze acceptance.

outcomeResults.description: Reject missing browser versions, false hardware labels and unqualified skipped cases.
outcomeResults.reason: Unit tests and the validator reject missing/placeholder browser versions, generic skip reasons and several false hardware claims. They do not reject an otherwise valid physical record whose os.version alone says it is an emulator: the marker scan does not include that field. Thus rejection of false hardware labels is incomplete, not merely unverified.

outcomeResults.description: backend
outcomeResults.reason: The backend-specific target cells distinguish WebGL2 from experimental WebGPU, and the documented root mount and lower-level explicit/auto selection and fallback correspond to current source. These labels are not a current browser/backend support pass.

outcomeResults.description: feature combinations have versioned support labels. Software
outcomeResults.reason: Software has its own diagnostic project and evidence category, but the versioned browser/backend table does not enumerate support status for individual feature combinations. The six scenario names in the harness do not themselves constitute a versioned feature-by-environment support matrix.

outcomeResults.description: Define supported, experimental, unsupported and unverified browser/device tiers.
outcomeResults.reason: The native browser support document defines supported, experimental, unsupported and unverified tiers and their qualifying limitations. It explicitly states that defining these tiers does not promote any current candidate cell.

outcomeResults.description: Treat automated browser builds, retail browsers, software rendering, injected sessions and physical mobile/desktop devices as separate evidence. Do not claim a physical device from an emulator or spend on hardware automatically.
outcomeResults.reason: The written policy separates automation, retail, software, injected/emulated and physical evidence and does not authorize hardware spending. The source validator checks common misleading labels and asks for physical provenance, but an emulator marker in os.version is not scanned and the supplied provenance is not independently authenticated.

outcomeResults.description: Supported browser, OS, device, backend and feature combinations have versioned support labels. Software, experimental, emulated and physical-device evidence remain separate.
outcomeResults.reason: Versioned browser/backend targets and separate software, experimental and device categories exist, but per-feature combinations are not enumerated and no candidate supported ranges are established. The physical-label validator also overlooks emulator indicators in os.version. Actual device and browser support remains an acceptance question.

outcomeResults.description: Performance, browser and physical-device results report failures and unavailable cases explicitly. Live-device and publication evidence follows code freeze and does not masquerade as source completion.
outcomeResults.reason: Browser scenarios encode failed, unsupported and skipped reasons, performance instrumentation records unavailable metrics and failures, and source reports retain acceptance as not-run. Actual candidate results and publication/device receipts are post-freeze; additionally the cross-browser remote integration currently fails discovery because its restored consumer is outside the example server's allowed repository.

outcomeResults.description: Add default-flags chromium-automation, firefox-automation and webkit-automation projects, plus a separately labeled chromium-gpu-headless project and explicit software/experimental diagnostics.
outcomeResults.reason: The configuration declares default-launch-option Chromium, Firefox and WebKit automation projects, full Chromium GPU-headless, and separately flagged software and experimental projects. Existing source tests inspect project launch options and labels; no browser behavior was exercised.

outcomeResults.description: does not masquerade as source completion
outcomeResults.reason: Source reports explicitly preserve acceptance as not-run and source-phase consumer validation requires pending browser cells; the public claims boundary says source completion is not a browser, device or release receipt. This is phase separation, not an acceptance pass.

outcomeResults.description: Route browser-project forwarding and result/artifact transport through WP-20; document unverified cells without blocking the source freeze.
outcomeResults.reason: Project validation/forwarding, independent exit and upload handling, hashed artifact manifest, and unverified source-phase documentation exist. The WP-22 spec imports a server that rejects the /tmp installed-consumer path exported by the remote task, so the actual combined browser-project path cannot currently reach workload execution.

outcomeResults.description: Capture the exact browser distribution and executable version, operating system, backend, adapter, driver where available, feature flags, fixture hash and test result. Record unsupported and skipped reasons explicitly. Automation builds do not by themselves establish retail-browser support.
outcomeResults.reason: Evidence fields include executable version, distribution, OS, backend, adapter/driver or unavailability, fixture hash and detailed scenarios. Only configured Aura3D feature flags are captured; the complete effective launch arguments are always marked unavailable despite the policy requiring effective flags. No candidate browser record exists, and remote discovery has the separate installed-path conflict.

outcomeResults.description: Exercise rendering, assets, controls, lifecycle and worker entrypoints with backend diagnostics.
outcomeResults.reason: The harness implements typed GLB rendering and pixels, DOM/input/orbit interaction, disposal, backend/adapter diagnostics and a public worker-renderer scenario with an explicit unsupported reason. Its required remote entrypoint is not integrated successfully: the spec imports example-dev-server, which rejects the externally restored installed package path supplied by the remote task.

outcomeResults.description: emulated
outcomeResults.reason: Emulated and injected classes are distinct from physical in the policy/schema, and tests cover common emulation indicators. The validator's physical marker scan omits os.version and observer text, so an explicit emulator indicator confined to those fields can escape rejection.

outcomeResults.description: Build a versioned support matrix with default-flags desktop projects and separately labeled experimental, software and physical-device results. WP-22.
outcomeResults.reason: The versioned target matrix and separate default, software and experimental projects exist; physical-device targets are clearly unverified, not fabricated. However, there are no supported ranges or current physical results, and the physical-label check misses emulator markers in os.version. The missing real-device measurement is post-freeze acceptance.

outcomeResults.description: software results are not visual or hardware proof
outcomeResults.reason: The source evidence policy distinguishes software timings from physical-GPU performance and requires matching browser pixels or runtime assertions rather than treating counters alone as visual proof. Software-rendered pixels remain evidence only for the measured software configuration.

outcomeResults.description: device
outcomeResults.reason: Retail/mobile/physical-device targets are separately marked unverified and physical labels require provenance; no device result is claimed. The validator still misses emulator indicators confined to os.version and cannot authenticate the supplied provenance, so its device-class separation is not complete.

outcomeResults.description: Run the same independent public scenarios on each applicable browser project.
outcomeResults.reason: A shared independent typed-model scenario covers rendering, DOM, input, asset, worker and lifecycle for the named projects. In the actual remote path the spec's imported server rejects the /tmp candidate installation exported by task-run, so the scenario is not integrated for remote discovery/execution; no browser run is claimed.

outcomeResults.description: Define exact supported browser/OS/backend combinations with version ranges and fallback behavior. Start every untested cell as unverified.
outcomeResults.reason: Fallback semantics and unverified target combinations are documented. Exact supported browser/OS/backend ranges are absent: the support policy explicitly declines to infer them from target versions, and establishing them requires matching post-freeze evidence.

outcomeResults.description: Route browser-project forwarding and result/artifact transport through WP-20
outcomeResults.reason: WP-20 forwards the selected project and implements discovery, structured result/artifact inventory and bounded upload with separate exit statuses. Its actual integration with the requested cross-browser scenario is broken by the externally restored consumer versus repository-only example-server alias check. Mocked egress tests are present but were not run.

outcomeResults.description: Run public WebGL2, DOM, input, asset and worker workloads remotely on default-flags chromium-automation, firefox-automation and webkit-automation projects. Use the separate chromium-gpu-headless project for native GPU probes. Keep software and experimental GPU flags in separately labeled projects.
outcomeResults.reason: The requested browser profiles, public workload and remote acceptance commands exist, but the remote runner's externally restored candidate is rejected by the scenario's imported example server before discovery. Running browser projects and GPU probes is separate post-freeze acceptance and was not performed.

outcomeResults.description: browser
outcomeResults.reason: This checklist fragment asks for actual browser results and their failure/unavailability disclosure after freeze. The harness contains explicit scenario statuses and reasons, but no current-candidate browser result was inspected or run; the separate remote discovery defect must be addressed before those results can be obtained.

outcomeResults.description: experimental
outcomeResults.reason: Experimental GPU flags have a distinct diagnostic project and evidence label, separate from default automation and software; the policy forbids treating flagged runs as default evidence. The existing project configuration test is not an executed browser result.

outcomeResults.description: Exercise both declared supported peer major versions, StrictMode double mounts, Suspense, error boundaries, prop updates, input and scene disposal using packed packages.
outcomeResults.reason: The source harness provisions distinct installed React 18/19 peers, validates package identity, and defines the requested StrictMode, Suspense, error, update, input and disposal scenarios. This is authored test coverage, not a claimed execution or browser pass.

outcomeResults.description: deliver cancellation/failure through a stable boundary and do not update unmounted components.
outcomeResults.reason: Failed, cancelled or disposed readiness is converted to AuraCanvasReadinessError and delivered to onError or thrown during render; active-mount and revision checks suppress stale results. Cleanup aborts readiness and disposes the app. Ordinary unmount cancellation is intentionally silent.

outcomeResults.description: support independent subscribers, bounded ownership, eviction and retry after failure.
outcomeResults.reason: Signalled subscribers have independent waits, last-owner cancellation, retain/release, retry and 128-entry LRU lookup eviction. Unsignalled direct Suspense reads set an unbounded interest before commit, and an active owned lookup can be evicted without stopping work, so ownership and in-flight work are not universally bounded. The new optional signal for read/useAuraAsset permits caller-managed cancellation but does not fix the default.

outcomeResults.description: Scope asset resources by effective loader, request/security context and digest; support independent subscribers, bounded ownership, eviction and retry after failure.
outcomeResults.reason: Resources are partitioned by loader, security-context identity and copied ordered descriptors/digests; cancellable subscribers, retry and bounded lookup eviction exist. Default unsignalled direct reads can outlive an abandoned Suspense render and owned evicted flights may continue outside the cache, leaving the explicit bounded-ownership requirement incomplete.

outcomeResults.description: Scope asset resources by effective loader, request/security context and digest
outcomeResults.reason: Shared lookup compares effective loader identity, explicit object-identity request/security scope and copied ordered descriptors including digest; custom shared loaders require a context, and Model defaults custom loaders to separate instance scopes. Callers must rotate identity when credentials or request policy captured in a mutable loader change; this is documented, not automatically inferred.

outcomeResults.description: The existing React integration handles both documented peer majors
outcomeResults.reason: The package declares React 18 and 19, uses their shared hooks including useSyncExternalStore, and supplies a packed-consumer matrix and browser test source for both. This is a source-implementation assessment only: actual compatibility of either installed peer remains unverified until the separate browser acceptance runs.

outcomeResults.description: Complete real browser/SSR lifecycles, true readiness, safe resource ownership, retry and supported peer coverage. WP-23.
outcomeResults.reason: Renderer readiness, SSR-safe snapshots, scoped cache, retry and StrictMode cleanup are implemented and a packed lifecycle suite is authored. Safe ownership is incomplete for default pre-commit Suspense reads, and the hydration test counts dispose calls rather than proving actual renderer/asset resource retirement. Packed-browser and hydration acceptance were not run.

outcomeResults.description: Test both supported peer majors, StrictMode, Suspense, errors, rerenders, input and repeated mount/unmount.
outcomeResults.reason: The packed browser suite covers both peer majors and the named lifecycle scenarios; fresh-process SSR/primitive-instance tests and committed-frame callback tests are also authored. This outcome also references verification that fragment and scene-sibling updates reach a mounted public app: the fragment test invokes applySceneChange on a fake setScene, and the packed fixture does not contain fragment or Scene-sibling declarations. That integration verification is absent.

outcomeResults.description: Test server-safe imports, resource identity, retries, cancellation and late completions.
outcomeResults.reason: The requested unit test source contains no-DOM SSR rendering, scope and descriptor identity, retry, independently cancelled subscribers, and late-result/disposal assertions. Its existence is not a passing test result.

outcomeResults.description: Document supported versions, SSR/hydration, ownership, errors and precise status.
outcomeResults.reason: The README documents declared peers, experimental status, renderer readiness, SSR/hydration, errors, security contexts and default unbounded reads. Current source additionally exposes caller-signalled read({signal}) and useAuraAsset(resource, {signal}), but the ownership/cancellation guidance does not document those public options or how to own a pre-commit signal; its no-argument uncancellable warning remains accurate.

outcomeResults.description: StrictMode
outcomeResults.reason: Canvas cleanup aborts the old readiness waiter, removes listeners and disposes the app. Model retains a committed resource and defers last-owner abort for synchronous StrictMode effect replay. Unit source models both replays and the packed fixture uses a development StrictMode tree; no browser pass is implied.

outcomeResults.description: Make readiness truthful, scope preload/cache by loader and security identity, support retry/cancellation, avoid updates after unmount and clean StrictMode lifecycle.
outcomeResults.reason: The adapter implements successful-renderer onReady, context-scoped preloads, retry, independent signalled cancellation and guarded StrictMode cleanup. Its direct useAuraAsset/read default creates an uncancellable interest before the effect can commit, so an abandoned suspended component can leave loading work alive; optional caller-provided read signals do not make the default lifecycle bounded.

outcomeResults.description: Verify server-side import/render avoids DOM access, and hydrate a real client scene without duplicate render loops or leaked listeners/resources.
outcomeResults.reason: Fresh-process SSR and real packed-client hydration test sources exist; the latter asserts canvas reuse, frame/listener cleanup and app.dispose calls. It does not check actual GPU/asset resource retirement or await disposeAsync, and the first StrictMode mount is not counted before onReady. Thus resource-leak verification is incomplete independently of the unrun browser acceptance.

outcomeResults.description: Make the existing adapter's ready callback reflect successful renderer readiness
outcomeResults.reason: AuraCanvas asks the live app for renderer readiness and announces only a ready result belonging to the current committed mount; an older engine must also report a mounted WebGL2 renderer. This means renderer availability, not first-frame or asset completion.

outcomeResults.description: The existing React integration handles both documented peer majors, real readiness, StrictMode, Suspense, SSR/hydration, cache isolation, cancellation and disposal.

outcomeResults.description: Report unavailable, disjoint and lost GPU scopes separately from CPU timings. Exclusive execution owner: wp25_performance/profiler. Source verification: Profiler source tests.
outcomeResults.reason: Trace export emits separate CPU observations, actual GPU samples and duration-free status events for pending, unavailable, disjoint and lost scopes. Mock-based source tests cover these cases.

outcomeResults.description: Collect rendered startup, frame, memory, resource and available device timing metrics.
outcomeResults.reason: The browser probe implements rendered startup, frame and optional heap/device timing plus observed WebGL resource lifetimes. It does not measure WebGPU teardown, where a lifecycle may complete before a later fence rejection leaves device cleanup pending. Actual GPU residency is explicitly unavailable and no current rendered performance run or physical-device result is retained.

outcomeResults.description: Bind installed bundle reports and acceptance to current candidate identity. Exclusive execution owner: wp25_performance/tree_shaking. Source verification: tests/unit/tools/native-installed-tree-shaking.test.ts.
outcomeResults.reason: The Markdown contract and release acceptance validate candidate, source-report and retained-artifact identities, with synthetic mismatch tests. End-to-end current-candidate installed reporting remains blocked by the unconditional portable-consumer custody guard; the checked-in Markdown is historical.

outcomeResults.description: Pass existing budgets without raising them, add measured workload ratchets and real device timing where available. WP-25.
outcomeResults.reason: Timer and workload-budget source exists, including an opt-in WebGPU selected-pass bridge, but current bundle passes and measured ratchets are not established. The probe permanently marks several required aggregate metrics no-data, so its actual reports cannot currently achieve an aggregate pass even with a valid baseline.

outcomeResults.description: Use real asynchronous device timers where available; label CPU time and unsupported/disjoint GPU results correctly.
outcomeResults.reason: GPUProfiler uses asynchronous WebGL2 elapsed queries and optional WebGPU pass timestamp readback, labels CPU separately and reports disjoint, unsupported and lost results without substituting fabricated GPU timings.

outcomeResults.description: Run at least 3 independent sessions and 300 timed frames per session where the calibrated workload permits
outcomeResults.reason: The source specifies 300 timed frames and launches three independent browser processes, but no current candidate sessions have been run or retained.

outcomeResults.description: Record exact workload, browser, device, baseline, method, budgets and limitations.
outcomeResults.reason: The untracked documentation records fixed workloads, methods, caps and limitations, but explicitly has no collected baseline, candidate browser version, device, residency or measurement result.

outcomeResults.description: Test candidate-bound tree-shaking and canonical report acceptance. Exclusive execution owner: wp25_performance/bundle_recovery. Source verification: Direct Node test for this file.
outcomeResults.reason: The acceptance tests cover mismatched candidate bundle identity, modified tree source report and bundle artifact, and canonical Markdown mismatch. They use synthetic fixtures and were not run in this audit.

outcomeResults.description: Existing bundle budgets pass without being raised; repeated like-for-like workloads report startup, p50/p95/p99, bytes, resource counts and available hardware timing. Counters and software results are not visual or hardware proof.
outcomeResults.reason: The budget and workload instrumentation exists and explicitly limits claims from software and counters, but neither current bundle-budget passes nor repeated same-device workload reports are retained. Actual GPU residency is unavailable and the aggregate analyzer cannot pass with the probe's permanently null metrics. WebGL handle counts do not establish WebGPU fence retirement; a lifecycle can already be disposed when a later fence rejection leaves device cleanup pending.

outcomeResults.description: Test Unicode, direction, kerning, fallback, wrapping, allocation and disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: The named source test covers full-run Unicode/RTL, mocked kerning and fallback, grapheme wrapping, allocation, eviction and disposal; it has not been run in this audit.

outcomeResults.description: reject only specified unsupported variants and never accept and ignore a setting.
outcomeResults.reason: Several unsupported model combinations now have explicit errors, including custom shader plus imported variant. Nonetheless a bounds collider accepts a scaled model while deriving its shape from unscaled asset bounds, so an accepted setting is not faithfully reflected.

outcomeResults.description: Request existing geometry and public type changes from their WP-01/WP-19 owners
outcomeResults.reason: The requested owner-to-owner communication is not established by inspected repository artifacts; the implemented geometry and exports do not prove a request was sent.

outcomeResults.description: Compile font assets, shaping results and atlas updates to visible text.
outcomeResults.reason: The text compiler resolves loaded-font snapshots or the built-in atlas; the primitive compiler creates actual mesh/texture resources and flushes eligible shared-atlas updates. Loaded-font entries are whole-label snapshots, not individually reused glyphs.

outcomeResults.description: Implement capacity-aware retained line/attribute updates, correct distance/color/bounds refresh and disposal of superseded buffers; keep mesh contracts coordinated with WP-01.
outcomeResults.reason: Geometry reuses retained line buffers, refreshes distances/colors/bounds and retires old buffers. The requested WP-01 mesh-contract coordination is not evidenced by source or an inspected owner record.

outcomeResults.description: Apply custom model materials to supported slots and report unsupported cases.
outcomeResults.reason: A custom material factory is applied to imported draw items and incompatibilities are reported. It replaces the whole model rather than selecting slots, and authored texture maps and custom-plus-variant are currently rejected rather than preserved.

outcomeResults.description: Update actual line storage in Geometry.ts, preserving LineGeometry.ts's re-export. Same-capacity edits reuse GPU buffers; growth releases replaced buffers. Test changing positions/colors/distances, bounds and allocation counts over repeated updates and final disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: The Geometry storage and public re-export support in-capacity updates and replacement on growth; the existing test checks changed attributes, bounds, allocation counts, repeated updates and final disposal.

outcomeResults.description: expose an accessible DOM counterpart and dispose glyph/texture resources after final use.
outcomeResults.reason: A default hidden DOM note is populated and removed with the scene layer; geometry, textures and atlas leases are released with resources. The DOM layer requires an HTML canvas and callers may explicitly suppress the note.

outcomeResults.description: Test material overrides, variants, LOD, collider behavior and unsupported errors.
outcomeResults.reason: The named test exercises overrides, variants, imported LOD and unsupported errors, but its collider checks only the serialized node/default physics, not generated collision geometry or scaled collider behavior.

outcomeResults.description: Load admitted licensed font data and metadata with bounded decoding.
outcomeResults.reason: The loader validates required caller-supplied family/license/URL metadata, format, input/table bounds and compressed declared decoded size before FontFace registration; the cap is 16 MiB and disposal unregisters the face. Metadata is not independent license verification.

outcomeResults.description: Request existing geometry and public type changes from their WP-01/WP-19 owners; verify source, pixel output, interaction and resource teardown.
outcomeResults.reason: Relevant source and test definitions exist, but an owner request and candidate-bound source verification are unestablished; the pixel test lacks pointer interaction coverage and no browser acceptance was run.

outcomeResults.description: shaping
outcomeResults.reason: Whole logical lines are measured and painted through Canvas, preserving platform kerning, ligatures and contextual shaping. Platform coverage is not guaranteed and wrapped bidi scopes are explicitly rejected.

outcomeResults.description: clipping
outcomeResults.reason: The line compiler carries material clipping into render items; the forward renderer creates a distinct screen-space clipping shader and rejects unsupported instancing/shader/transform cases. Tests exist, but no GPU pixel pass is claimed.

outcomeResults.description: Support admitted licensed fonts, Unicode shaping, kerning, ligatures, right-to-left scripts, fallback glyphs, multiline wrapping and dynamic atlas updates with bounded allocation.
outcomeResults.reason: Font loading, ordered fallback, platform shaping and bounded layout exist, but open bidi scopes across wrapped lines are rejected and dynamic loaded-font storage is run/whole-label snapshots rather than independently updated glyphs.

outcomeResults.description: fallback
outcomeResults.reason: The built-in glyph fallback remains, and loaded-font shaping constructs an ordered family list. Canvas can choose a system fallback and does not identify the actual font or guarantee glyph coverage.

outcomeResults.description: Complete wide/dashed line widths in world and screen units, per-vertex gradients, segment continuity, pixel-ratio/resize behavior, alpha and clipping; return a stable error for any unsupported combination.
outcomeResults.reason: Widths, gradients, continuous distances, per-frame resolution, alpha and clipping are implemented. Builders and compiler reject gapSize/dashOffset without dashing using coded errors. Complete diagnostic and rendered-output verification remains open.

outcomeResults.description: Apply custom materials to supported imported model slots while preserving variants, textures, shadows, morphs, skinning and instances. Implement model LOD/collider options; reject only specified unsupported variants and never accept and ignore a setting.
outcomeResults.reason: Whole-model custom replacement, LOD and collider paths exist, but no per-slot shader selection is available, authored textures and custom-plus-variant are rejected, and model bounds colliders omit visual scale. Only restricted certified graph skinning is admitted.

outcomeResults.description: Manage bounded glyph allocation, eviction, updates and GPU disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: GlyphAtlas enforces dimension/entry limits, reference counts and LRU eviction, stages dirty updates and disposes its backing; the mounted built-in atlas supplies a real texture-update/disposal adapter. Loaded-font reuse is still whole-label, addressed separately.

outcomeResults.description: Unicode
outcomeResults.reason: Font-backed text takes Unicode strings and delegates full logical runs to Canvas and Unicode segmentation; actual font coverage depends on the browser, and wrapped open bidi scopes are rejected.

outcomeResults.description: dashes
outcomeResults.reason: Line geometry carries cumulative world-transformed distances into the dash shader for screen- and world-width strokes. Invalid dash sizes and zero-length expanded segments are rejected.

outcomeResults.description: verify source, pixel output, interaction and resource teardown.
outcomeResults.reason: Source teardown tests and browser pixel assertions exist, but no candidate-bound source/pixel run is established and the named browser suite has no pointer or keyboard interaction assertion. Pixel acceptance was not run.

outcomeResults.description: Test color gradients, dash continuity, world units, clipping and resizing.
outcomeResults.reason: The named material test exercises gradients, dash continuity, world units and resize uniforms but contains no clipping case; separate clipping tests exist.

outcomeResults.description: gradients
outcomeResults.reason: Per-point colors reach each segment endpoint and are interpolated by the screen-space shader; thin lines also retain endpoint colors.

outcomeResults.description: Regress line hierarchy, dynamic geometry and resource lifecycle. Exclusive execution owner: wp26_text. Source verification: Direct Vitest for this file.
outcomeResults.reason: The named test defines coverage for hierarchy and world transforms, live geometry edits, buffer growth and retirement. Direct Vitest has not been run for this audited source.

outcomeResults.description: direction
outcomeResults.reason: Direction can be ltr, rtl or first-strong auto per paragraph, and is passed to the platform shaper/painter; cross-line open bidi scopes fail explicitly.

outcomeResults.description: unsupported values return stable diagnostics instead of silent approximations
outcomeResults.reason: Clipping and several model incompatibilities have stable coded failures, but solid lines can accept inert gapSize/dashOffset and ordinary dash/width validation throws uncoded errors; model collider bounds also omit model scale.

outcomeResults.description: Integrate line width, gradient and clipping plus dynamic world text and accessibility. Exclusive execution owner: wp26_text. Source verification: tests/unit/rendering/native-line-geometry.test.ts; tests/unit/rendering/native-text-shaping.test.ts.
outcomeResults.reason: Line shader/forward clipping, text textures, DOM labels and the referenced source tests are integrated, but loaded-font shared storage updates whole-label snapshots rather than individual glyphs. The tests and GPU behavior have no candidate-bound pass in the inspected evidence.

outcomeResults.description: Preserve the built-in small-glyph fallback
outcomeResults.reason: The lazy built-in SDF atlas and original extruded glyph path remain available, limited to uppercase A-Z, digits, space, hyphen and period.

outcomeResults.description: layout
outcomeResults.reason: The loaded-font shaper supports width, line height and maximum lines with word/grapheme wrapping. Complex wrapping needs Intl.Segmenter; open cross-line bidi scopes are rejected.

outcomeResults.description: Assert model collider and LOD settings now take effect rather than expecting ignored warnings. Exclusive execution owner: wp26_text. Source verification: Direct Vitest for this file.
outcomeResults.reason: The named test asserts that LOD and collider options are retained without ignored warnings, not that their rendered LOD or collision geometry actually takes effect. A separate test covers LOD; collider scale remains untested there.

outcomeResults.description: Apply custom materials to supported imported model slots while preserving variants, textures, shadows, morphs, skinning and instances. Implement model LOD/collider options
outcomeResults.reason: Custom materials are applied to draw items and LOD is selected, but custom-plus-variant/authored textures are rejected, per-slot custom replacement is missing, and collision shape dimensions ignore model scale.

outcomeResults.description: return a stable error for any unsupported combination.
outcomeResults.reason: Unsupported clipping routes receive stable codes; line dash validation rejects gapSize/dashOffset without dashing with a coded error. Comprehensive option-diagnostic coverage remains unverified.

outcomeResults.description: Shape Unicode, ligatures, kerning, fallback, direction and line layout.
outcomeResults.reason: Whole-run Canvas shaping supplies ligatures, kerning, fallback and direction with bounded wrapping, but wrapped open bidi scopes are rejected and other wrapped lines are resolved independently rather than as full bidi paragraphs.

outcomeResults.description: Implement required model LOD/collider options and preserve variants/overrides; return explicit errors for unsupported shape/backend variants.
outcomeResults.reason: Model LOD, variant forwarding and bounds/auto collider options are wired with several explicit unsupported errors; however collider shape ignores node scale and missing bounds default to [1,1,1]. Custom replacement plus a material variant now fails explicitly.

outcomeResults.description: Implement the required model/line behavior; reject only explicitly unsupported variants and test rendered results. WP-26.
outcomeResults.reason: Line source and model options have browser-test definitions, but per-slot custom materials and textured/custom-variant preservation are not provided and scaled bounds colliders are wrong. No rendered-result receipt for the current source was found.

outcomeResults.description: Regress line buffers, bounds and disposal. Exclusive execution owner: wp26_text/line_geometry. Source verification: Direct Vitest for this file.
outcomeResults.reason: The named line-geometry test checks in-place attribute/bounds changes, buffer reuse, growth, allocation counts, invalid updates and final disposal; its direct Vitest run is not established.

outcomeResults.description: Add licensed font assets, shaping, fallback, atlas lifecycle and accessible text. WP-26.
outcomeResults.reason: Caller-admitted font bytes, platform shaping/fallback, bounded atlas ownership and accessible text exist, but loaded-font glyphs are rasterized as complete runs/labels instead of independently cached and dynamically updated glyphs.

outcomeResults.description: Document font/label capabilities, accessible counterparts and verified limits.
outcomeResults.reason: The current document explains font admission, platform shaping and fallback limitations, shared atlas and text resource lifecycle, accessible notes and the fact that multilingual browser pixels remain acceptance work.

outcomeResults.description: Preserve the public re-export contract for the real line implementation in Geometry.ts.
outcomeResults.reason: LineGeometry publicly re-exports Geometry and its segment types; the named test checks the export identity and exercises an update.

outcomeResults.description: Preserve per-vertex colors and complete wide/dashed line compilation.
outcomeResults.reason: The compiler carries endpoint colors into thin and expanded geometry, routes wide/dashed lines through the screen-space material, and refreshes distances and resolution on updates.

outcomeResults.description: dynamic atlases
outcomeResults.reason: Bounded atlas allocation and dirty uploads are integrated, but loaded fonts cache full shaped label snapshots and rerasterize on changes rather than retaining independently reusable dynamic glyphs.

outcomeResults.description: alpha
outcomeResults.reason: Endpoint alpha and material opacity cause blending and disabled depth writes, and line fragment output multiplies base and vertex colors; the source test asserts the blend state.

outcomeResults.description: Replace the bounded atlas-only path with licensed, dynamic glyph atlas support while preserving built-in fallback.
outcomeResults.reason: Built-in fallback and loaded-font SDF snapshots exist, but each shaped line is placed in a temporary atlas and the retained shared path caches whole labels, not the requested dynamic individual loaded-font glyphs.

outcomeResults.description: Verify pixels and interactions for line/material/model options.
outcomeResults.reason: The named browser spec defines pixel assertions for width, dashes, DPR, mutation, variants and custom material, but no pointer/keyboard interaction case. It was not run and supplies no current candidate-bound pixel receipt.

outcomeResults.description: Preserve the built-in small-glyph fallback; expose an accessible DOM counterpart and dispose glyph/texture resources after final use.
outcomeResults.reason: Built-in glyphs remain available, the default DOM note is attached to text, and compiled geometry, textures and atlas leases are retired. OffscreenCanvas has no DOM layer and the caller owns loaded font handles.

outcomeResults.description: World text covers licensed fonts, Unicode, shaping, fallback, direction, layout, dynamic atlases and accessible alternatives. Lines preserve width, dashes, gradients, clipping and alpha.
outcomeResults.reason: Text and line paths cover many listed features, but loaded-font shared atlas entries are whole-label snapshots rather than reusable glyphs, bidi wrapping has a rejected case, and the current browser output is unverified.

outcomeResults.description: Verify multilingual text, layout, dynamic glyphs and accessible labels.
outcomeResults.reason: The browser spec defines multilingual text, layout, accessible-label and update pixel checks, but its glyph-atlas update is a standalone atlas operation, not a per-glyph update in loaded-font rendering. The browser spec has not been run.

outcomeResults.description: Update actual line storage in Geometry.ts, preserving LineGeometry.ts's re-export. Same-capacity edits reuse GPU buffers
outcomeResults.reason: The real Geometry owns native line storage; LineGeometry re-exports it and same-capacity edits retain buffers.

outcomeResults.description: Expose typed font, shaping, layout, fallback and lifecycle options.
outcomeResults.reason: The typed builder exposes loaded fonts, fallback, direction, layout, atlas and accessible-label options; LoadedFont has explicit dispose and incompatible option/backend combinations are rejected.

outcomeResults.description: Implement width, dash, gradient, clipping and alpha behavior.
outcomeResults.reason: The material exposes width/dash/alpha uniforms, endpoint colors are passed by the geometry and shader, and the forward renderer selects the clipping variant. Unsupported clipped paths fail explicitly.

outcomeResults.description: World text covers licensed fonts
outcomeResults.reason: Public loadFont registers validated font bytes and metadata and text3D consumes the handle; the caller attests licensing and platform glyph coverage is not independently verified.

outcomeResults.description: growth releases replaced buffers. Test changing positions/colors/distances, bounds and allocation counts over repeated updates and final disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: Growth replaces and retires vertex and index buffers; the existing test covers position/color/distance changes, bounds, repeated allocations/reuse and final disposal.

outcomeResults.description: Support or explicitly reject world-unit dashes, width and color combinations.
outcomeResults.reason: Fat-line options expose world/screen width and per-point color; the compiler combines these with dashed screen-space geometry and validates malformed widths and dash sizes. Clipping has separately enforced limits.

outcomeResults.description: accessible alternatives. Lines preserve width
outcomeResults.reason: Text exposes a default hidden DOM note and line material/compiler provide both screen- and world-unit width. The note can be explicitly suppressed and is unavailable for OffscreenCanvas.

outcomeResults.description: Complete wide/dashed line widths in world and screen units, per-vertex gradients, segment continuity, pixel-ratio/resize behavior, alpha and clipping
outcomeResults.reason: The source supports world/screen widths, vertex gradients, transformed continuous dash distances, per-frame resolution/DPR, blending and clipping. Clipped custom/instanced paths and invalid transforms reject; rendered pixels are not verified here.

However the full game still returns a public shell whose loading-progress and track methods silently do nothing, and its unconfigured/headless HUD silently ignores banner, toast and damageNumber calls; thus not every exposed game path is implemented.

outcomeResults.description: do not re-export through a dependency cycle.
outcomeResults.reason: The legacy root exports a contract stub instead of re-exporting the package that imports the root; the full game has a separately registered slot, avoiding that reverse dependency cycle. A subpath migration test exists.

outcomeResults.description: Complete or explicitly reject root behaviors, prove collider/joint/vehicle/game lifecycle and retain optional backend boundaries. WP-27.
outcomeResults.reason: Root migration diagnostics, collider/joint/vehicle and lifecycle implementations exist, and the old input/evidence ownership defects are fixed in source. But the 4.x root still eagerly imports the optional solver despite the requested non-physics isolation, directly contradicting the current optional-boundary test; the independent native world is not a public backend. Full-game shell and fallback HUD also contain silent no-ops.

outcomeResults.description: Expose supported body, collider, joint, vehicle and query options with explicit errors.
outcomeResults.reason: The public physics namespace supplies bodies, shapes, joints, controllers and queries with validation, and independent native source modules and numerical tests exist. The referenced native solver explicitly remains an internal experiment, is not exported/selected by the public world/provider, and documents restricted CCD and no Rapier parity; the grouped independent-backend integration/no-downgrade requirement is therefore not established.

outcomeResults.description: Complete supported ready/input/HUD/audio/effects/reset and disposal behavior on the full game entrypoint.

The current input type correctly includes undefined, but without a configured HUD the returned HUD silently ignores visual operations, and the returned shell has inert progress/track operations. Trails explicitly reject and application-owned state must be restored via onReset.

outcomeResults.description: fixed/hinge/spring/motor joints
outcomeResults.reason: Fixed, hinge, spring and motorised-hinge constraints validate and create solver joints; motor options on other kinds reject. Behavioral source tests cover the requested kinds.

outcomeResults.description: Complete wheel, contact, reset and disposal behavior.
outcomeResults.reason: The physical vehicle exposes wheel setup and commands, contact reporting, pose reset and teardown, with validation and tests for reset/contact invalidation and disposed handles. A dynamic chassis is required.

outcomeResults.description: keyboard operation
outcomeResults.reason: Configured game input installs and removes keyboard listeners and there is a scripted installed-game keyboard fixture. The checklist requires correct keyboard operation for each supported surface; neither complete per-surface source evidence nor a manual installed-device result is established. autoListen:false intentionally disables listener installation.

outcomeResults.description: Verify scene/physics synchronization with parent transforms, multiple worlds, character/vehicle reset and teardown. Report unsupported backend or shape combinations explicitly.
outcomeResults.reason: There are parent-transform and multiple-world tests, a public-world held-vehicle reset test, a lower-level character resetTo test, and code to recreate both controller kinds. No corresponding public-world held-character reset test was found; unsupported backend and shape combinations are reported.

outcomeResults.description: Keep the full game entrypoint working and cycle-free. Replace the ambiguous root headless behavior with an actionable, versioned migration error; do not re-export through a dependency cycle.
outcomeResults.reason: The root fails with a versioned migration diagnostic, while the separately registered full-game implementation avoids a root-to-game reverse re-export. The full game nevertheless exposes inert shell progress/track methods, and the agent documentation still describes the obsolete warning-only root behavior.

outcomeResults.description: Keep the full game entrypoint working and cycle-free. Replace the ambiguous root headless behavior with an actionable, versioned migration error
outcomeResults.reason: The root migration error includes code, version, the full-game import and opt-out guidance; the recommended subpath has a real slot implementation. Full-entry working behavior is incomplete for exposed loading progress/track, and current agent docs still promise the old warn-and-return stub.

outcomeResults.description: Complete and test supported primitive, convex, static-mesh and heightfield collision; fixed/hinge/spring/motor joints; contact/sensor/layer queries; deterministic stepping and continuous collision.
outcomeResults.reason: The production world covers the requested supported colliders, joint kinds, filtered contact/sensor queries, fixed deterministic stepping and CCD, with relevant existing source tests. Non-static plane/mesh/heightfield and invalid backend requests reject; this is not a test-pass claim.

outcomeResults.description: reset
outcomeResults.reason: Physics world reset reconstructs its owned bodies, constraints and controllers; full-game reset clears game-owned effects and invokes onReset while suspended. Source tests exist for both. Game reset explicitly delegates app-owned physics, input, HUD, replay and audio restoration to the caller.

outcomeResults.description: replay
outcomeResults.reason: Input recording, deterministic replay and optional pointer/gamepad sample replay are implemented with scoped source tests. This is not automatic full game-state or physical hardware replay. The input records a prior mutable-tree pass without a run ID or current candidate binding, so it is not a candidate pass.

outcomeResults.description: Correct joint transforms, game pause, concurrent evidence ownership, hierarchy and supported migration behavior. Exclusive execution owner: wp27_physics. Source verification: tests/unit/physics/native-root-physics.test.ts and targeted physics/game source tests.
outcomeResults.reason: Joint world anchors are converted to body-local frames, game pause owns runtime suspension, parent transforms are staged, and channel/beacon releases are owner-aware. Current duplicate-id/alias tests and migration warning tests replace the stale checkpoint's reported defects; the targeted tests exist but were not run here.

outcomeResults.description: Synchronize scene transforms, parent transforms and physics ownership safely.
outcomeResults.reason: The bridge enforces node/world ownership, stages kinematic and parent-first dynamic transforms and releases ownership on disposal. Existing tests cover affine parents, preflight and multiple-world rejection; shear, reflection, singular poses and collider-scale synchronization remain explicit bounds.

outcomeResults.description: audio
outcomeResults.reason: When configured, the sound facade is wired to the game and session suspension/disposal; a supplied soundAdapter instead owns playback. Scoped source tests and the installed-game fixture exist, but no audible browser/device acceptance is claimed.

outcomeResults.description: Complete deterministic stepping, contacts, sensors, continuous collision and lifecycle behavior.
outcomeResults.reason: The production PhysicsWorld owns Rapier bodies, deterministic fixed-step state, contact/sensor collection, optional adaptive CCD and teardown. Existing tests cover replay and fast-body behavior; the only production backend is Rapier and the CCD budget can reject.

outcomeResults.description: Physics/game paths expose only implemented behavior; advanced shapes, joints, vehicles, input, reset, replay, audio, HUD and disposal have scoped evidence.
outcomeResults.reason: Advanced physics and scoped game/input/replay/audio/HUD/disposal tests exist. The previous input-undefined type mismatch and shared-channel deletion have since been corrected, but full-game shell loading-progress/track and unconfigured HUD visual operations still silently do nothing, contradicting the broad only-implemented-paths claim.

outcomeResults.description: Complete fixed, hinge, spring and motor joint behavior and unsupported diagnostics.
outcomeResults.reason: Constraint and production world implement fixed, hinge, spring and motorised-hinge joints; invalid kinds/options, motor calls and limits explicitly reject. Numerical behavioral tests exist.

outcomeResults.description: contact/sensor/layer queries
outcomeResults.reason: Contacts and sensor lifecycle, ray/sphere/overlap queries and layer-mask filtering are wired and have tests. Collision layers are limited to 16 bits and invalid masks are rejected.

outcomeResults.description: Document and enforce optional backend capabilities and teardown.

The physics README also says CCD is unsupported and omits convex/heightfield although the public solver implements them. Installed v5 declarations and full compatibility are explicitly unverified.

outcomeResults.description: joints
outcomeResults.reason: Scoped solver joint behavior and explicit invalid-option diagnostics have public numerical source tests.

outcomeResults.description: Complete supported primitive, convex, static-mesh and heightfield contracts.
outcomeResults.reason: Shape descriptors and factories validate and clone primitive, convex, triangle mesh and heightfield geometry. The public world rejects terrain shapes on non-static bodies and tests cover the supported cases.

outcomeResults.description: Validate installed games with manual keyboard and touch, HUD, audio/effects, pause/reset, replay and cleanup. Promote only features backed by the applicable root or subpath evidence.
outcomeResults.reason: The installed-candidate browser probe is authored, but manual keyboard/touch, HUD, audio/effects, pause/reset, replay and cleanup validation on a frozen installed candidate has not been run or tied to a retained receipt. Synthetic browser events are not a manual/device pass.

outcomeResults.description: HUD

outcomeResults.reason: Validated primitive and convex descriptors and static mesh/heightfield collision are connected to the production solver, with collision tests. Dynamic mesh and heightfield combinations reject explicitly.

outcomeResults.description: input

Tests cover absent/configured input and ownership for legacy and v5. autoListen:false is an explicit opt-out.

outcomeResults.description: Test the versioned diagnostic and supported full-entry migration.
outcomeResults.reason: The named test checks code/version, the subpath and flag guidance, no scene evaluation, full-entry lifecycle and explicit opt-out. The updated separate warning test also expects the versioned error. Neither was run in this audit.

outcomeResults.reason: The named test covers runtime input/tweens and pause, independent game ownership on scene changes, and idempotent disposal; separate tests cover game reset and deterministic replay. These tests exist but are not a passing receipt.

outcomeResults.description: disposal have scoped evidence

The older checkpoint's duplicate-channel deletion problem is corrected: releases compare descriptor ownership and restore the previous live owner. outcomeResults.reason: Root helper validates projection-specific ranges, offsets and mode, but the orthographic/isometric public builders pass it options without their mode, breaking their declared near/far contract.

outcomeResults.description: sprite
outcomeResults.reason: Sprite node carries texture, center, rotation and attenuation; standalone material parity and clipped native WebGPU/shadow geometry remain bounded.

outcomeResults.description: Test half-spaces, transforms, union/intersection, invalid planes, bounds, lifecycle and backend limits.
outcomeResults.reason: The named test specifies normalization, transforms, union/intersection, limits, bounds, lifecycle and shadow/depth cases.

outcomeResults.description: depth of field
outcomeResults.reason: Public depth-of-field options route to postprocessing; native WebGPU requires validated single-surface linear depth.

outcomeResults.description: Implement section 3.7 clipping through root scene/material APIs, compiler, graph, forward, depth and shadow paths. Define local/global composition, retained half-spaces, invalid-plane errors and supported mesh/line/point/sprite semantics.
outcomeResults.reason: Scene/material groups, compiler, generated and certified graph shaders integrate clipping, but arbitrary custom shaders and clipped specialized depth/shadow draws are rejected.

outcomeResults.description: Temporal state belongs to the full frame identity. Multiple passes with one frame ID share the same previous transforms and depth; commit history once when the frame finishes. Resets, camera cuts, scene swaps, disjoint views, device loss and resource retirement cannot mutate another app's history. Keep separate current/previous depth ownership, dimensions and attachment identity. Motion-blur weights sum to one, sample offsets are centered, and one sample or zero motion preserves the input.
outcomeResults.reason: Per-view/frame temporal history, resets, attachment identity, once-only commit and scene identity are integrated; the v2 blur shader centers taps, normalizes weights and preserves one sample/zero velocity. WebGPU retains failed fence leases and retries post-target cleanup, but ResourceLifecycle can complete before a waiting fence later rejects and cannot be re-enrolled. That completion gap does not itself demonstrate cross-app history mutation; complete alternate blur and retirement isolation remains unestablished.

outcomeResults.description: line
outcomeResults.reason: Line color, width and dashes are supplied by public line nodes, but the standalone line material mapping remains approximate.

outcomeResults.description: Test near/far mapping, large depth ranges, tiled seams, clipping transforms, animated/instanced geometry, target changes, depth-aware effects and unsupported-device fallback through source and packed-browser paths.
outcomeResults.reason: Source and packed-browser specifications cover much of the named matrix; separate mock-queue specifications cover target teardown and later fence failure. Zero-near ortho fixtures and allowed depth fallback disagree with current source, and complete combination coverage is not established. The specifications were not run.

outcomeResults.description: multi-view
outcomeResults.reason: Camera arrays and stereo produce per-view viewport and camera inputs with lifecycle tests; nonstandard and mixed stereo configurations are explicitly bounded.

outcomeResults.description: Add focal-length/film controls, view offsets and depth options while preserving current FOV defaults.
outcomeResults.reason: PerspectiveCamera implements film gauge, shift, focal-length override, tiled offsets and validated projection options, preserving the FOV default.

outcomeResults.description: Phong
outcomeResults.reason: PBR clearcoat gives an approximation but there is no direct Phong shininess/specular material contract.

outcomeResults.description: Carry explicit projection/depth metadata instead of recovering every mode from conventional finite-matrix coefficients.
outcomeResults.reason: FrameGraph prefers explicit depth/projection metadata, checks convention agreement and computes or carries inverse; conventional inference is limited to legacy cameras.

outcomeResults.description: Lambert
outcomeResults.reason: Lambert diffuse math exists but public Lambert migration uses approximate PBR rather than a distinct diffuse-only material.

outcomeResults.description: tiled/asymmetric views
outcomeResults.reason: Perspective and orthographic offset paths crop the full-image frustum and reject invalid rectangles; separate root near=0 validation remains defective.

outcomeResults.description: reflections
outcomeResults.reason: Public SSR and planar/refraction paths exist, but reflection-surface diagnostics explicitly keep SSR bindings unsupported in the cited route.

outcomeResults.description: point
outcomeResults.reason: Point-node authoring carries size, map, attenuation and alpha, while standalone point material mapping is approximate.

outcomeResults.description: Tone mapping, exposure, color management, environment prefiltering, HDR, sky, fog, volumetrics, water, reflections, refraction and depth-aware transparency; document fallback quality.
outcomeResults.reason: Exposure, fog, water, reflections and depth-aware transparency have source paths, but broad refraction/volume and complete fallback-quality documentation are not established.

outcomeResults.description: Points, sprites, thin/wide/dashed lines, line segments, wireframes and mesh primitives; indexed, non-indexed, instanced, batched, skinned and morphed geometry.
