outcomeResults.reason: Primitive and deformation families are present, but packed multi-draw and some clipped point/line/sprite depth combinations are explicitly rejected.

outcomeResults.description: shadows
outcomeResults.reason: Shadow clipping is opt-in and supported on eligible meshes; clipped specialized geometry and uncertified graph depth are rejected.

outcomeResults.description: Implement global/local clipping planes, intersection/union semantics, shadow participation and material/graph integration. WP-30.
outcomeResults.reason: Global/material groups and certified graph/depth integration exist; arbitrary custom shaders and specialized clipped depth remain unsupported.

outcomeResults.description: line segments
outcomeResults.reason: lines.segments validates and emits independent segment pairs, with optional dashed/wide routes.

outcomeResults.description: Regress declared infinite perspective and depth-convention support. Exclusive execution owner: wp30_depth. Source verification: Direct Vitest for this file.
outcomeResults.reason: The requested camera-clipping unit file covers standard near/far and infinite perspective, but does not regress declared depth-mode requests; separate depth-option tests exist.

outcomeResults.description: Add physical film/focal-length perspective controls and tiled/asymmetric view offsets. Define precedence when FOV and focal length are both supplied
outcomeResults.reason: Root and scene cameras construct physical focal/film projection and tiles, with focal length explicitly taking precedence over FOV.

outcomeResults.description: Regress supported clipping/section view options. Exclusive execution owner: wp30_depth. Source verification: Direct Vitest for this file.
outcomeResults.reason: The named kit test exercises supported section planes and the retained unsupported measurement capability.

outcomeResults.description: water
outcomeResults.reason: Public water surface uses a world-water node with tiered reflection/refraction when enabled and a band/foam fixture otherwise; buoyancy is telemetry, not physics.

outcomeResults.description: section views apply consistently to supported primitives
outcomeResults.reason: Section groups work for supported generated primitives, but specialized clipped depth/shadows and packed multi-draw are rejected.

outcomeResults.description: Centralize clip range, clear/compare, bias, reconstruction and negotiated standard/reversed/logarithmic depth behavior.
outcomeResults.reason: DepthConvention centralizes negotiation, compare, clear, bias, encode and reconstruction; devices use it for standard/fallback negotiation. Production renderer currently accepts only standard mode.

outcomeResults.description: sprites
outcomeResults.reason: Public sprites create billboard nodes with map, center, rotation and attenuation; clipped WebGPU and sprite shadow-depth paths are explicitly limited.

outcomeResults.description: normalized/integer/multiple-stream/per-instance vertex formats
outcomeResults.reason: Typed layouts and native state reach both device binders, but material-facing state is narrower, WebGPU rejects some generated alpha-to-coverage, and integer shader-input pixels are not covered by the located browser fixture.

outcomeResults.description: Integrate clipping/depth/output into program generation and warmup; a change in shader-affecting state must select the correct variant, while ordinary uniform edits must not cause needless recompilation.
outcomeResults.reason: Clipping/output feature selection and warmup are wired, while nonstandard camera depth is rejected by Renderer and the forward selector does not select log depth from the active convention. Depth variants are not included in generated warmup.

outcomeResults.description: sorted fallback
outcomeResults.reason: Weighted passes, whole-group sorted fallback and sampleable opaque depth are implemented, but public renderer integration is restricted to eligible WebGL2/mock frames and explicitly declines multiview and WebGPU.

outcomeResults.description: Regress raw typed byte storage and upload lifecycle. Exclusive execution owner: wp31_recovery/vertex_buffer. Source verification: Direct Vitest for this file.
outcomeResults.reason: The 39-reference bundle has meaningful typed-byte, stream/deformation, consolidation, stencil, identity, callback and resource-lifetime code and specifications. Renderer-owned static batching requires a trust predicate that always returns false, while renderer.test.ts still expects one merged mock draw; native pair attestation is unavailable and the packed-loop color feature is staged, not registered by production. WebGPU interop retains failed-fence leases and exposes failure on later device disposal, but a synchronous ResourceLifecycle may already have released its device while the fence was waiting and cannot be retroactively re-enrolled if it rejects. The tests were not executed.

outcomeResults.description: Bind expanded vertex layouts and preserve/reset full render state across draws, views and targets.
outcomeResults.reason: WebGL binds typed streams, divisors and integer pointers, invalidates its winding/blend shadows with the shared state cache and applies supported state per draw. Independent attachment state, partial sample masks and nonzero offset clamps explicitly fail rather than realizing the full command-state surface.

outcomeResults.description: Add independently designed weighted transparency with depth/alpha semantics, per-view resources and an explicit sorted fallback. WP-31.
outcomeResults.reason: The old claim that only sorted blending exists is outdated: the renderer can select a bounded weighted pass. It remains restricted to eligible unlit WebGL2/mock frames and sorts the rest, including WebGPU.

outcomeResults.description: Integrate clipping/depth/output into program generation and warmup
outcomeResults.reason: Structural clipping/output features and uniform inputs exist, but the renderer rejects nonstandard depth, the forward path does not derive log-depth selection, and generated depth programs are excluded from warmup.

outcomeResults.description: independent view resources
outcomeResults.reason: Accumulation, revealage, sampled depth, compositing and per-view storage exist in the lower-level pass; the renderer declines multi-view and WebGPU requests and uses sorted fallback for many materials and frame options.

outcomeResults.description: Support typed buffer reads, writes, safe uploads and stream validation. Exclusive execution owner: wp31_recovery/vertex_buffer. Source verification: tests/unit/rendering/native-vertex-buffer.test.ts.
outcomeResults.reason: VertexBuffer uses typed DataView access and raw byte windows, validates updates and slots, tracks dirty ranges, and owns per-device/generation uploads and retirement. The scoped typed-buffer requirements are implemented; separately, a synchronous WebGPU ResourceLifecycle owner can complete before a waiting fence later rejects, although interop retains the native lease. The requested source test exists but was not run.

outcomeResults.description: Test every supported state, variant key, integer/normalized layout, separate instance stream and invalid combination.
outcomeResults.reason: The named unit test specifies many WebGPU state/key, typed-value and invalid-layout cases. It does not cover every backend and program variant; the located browser fixture tests normalized instance pixels but not integer shader-input pixels.

outcomeResults.description: Test accumulation/composition math, order stability, fallback, formats, alpha, MSAA and ownership.
outcomeResults.reason: The named source specification covers accumulation/composition, order, premultiplied alpha, occlusion, float targets, per-view ownership, fallback, allocation failure and teardown. MSAA is tested as a fallback condition, not as supported weighted multisampling. This test-file-specific outcome does not establish asynchronous WebGPU fence-owner completion; a separate unrun source specification documents the late-rejection gap. No test was run.

outcomeResults.description: complete pipeline/program cache identities
outcomeResults.reason: Both devices implement extensive draw state and typed streams, but public material state omits native command fields and backend restrictions remain. Located state pixels cover normalized instance input, not integer shader-input pixels.

outcomeResults.description: Preserve stable opaque/masked/transmissive/transparent ordering and explicit render ordering. Implement weighted accumulation/revealage and composition with defined alpha/depth/MSAA rules, capability limits and sorted fallback.
outcomeResults.reason: Sorting and bounded weighted passes exist, but the real forward path treats masked materials as opaque instead of selecting a mask bucket, split graph phases override cross-bucket renderOrder, and weighted renderer eligibility excludes WebGPU and multiview.

outcomeResults.description: a change in shader-affecting state must select the correct variant, while ordinary uniform edits must not cause needless recompilation.
outcomeResults.reason: Structural keys, clipping and sRGB selection exist, with clipping uniforms distinct from shader features. Renderer rejects nonstandard depth and excludes generated depth programs from warmup, leaving the complete requested depth-variant path unresolved.

outcomeResults.description: Implement every supported depth/stencil/blend/color-mask/cull/winding/offset/sample field in each device
outcomeResults.reason: WebGPU resolves deterministic fixed pipeline state and applies dynamic state; WebGL applies native state. The material API omits several command fields and WebGL and generated WebGPU reject some combinations, so complete public draw-state fidelity is not established.

outcomeResults.description: Represent shader-affecting material, geometry, clipping and target features consistently.
outcomeResults.reason: Program features model material, geometry, clipping and output switches and canonicalize their keys. Forward/warmup do not consistently select active log-depth features, and some graph/depth combinations explicitly reject, so the full set of requested axes is not integrated.

outcomeResults.description: Use byte-preserving format-aware hash and equality for batch identities. Exclusive execution owner: wp31_recovery/vertex_buffer. Source verification: tests/unit/rendering/native-vertex-buffer.test.ts.
outcomeResults.reason: Batch identity includes stream/attribute layout, exact current vertex/index bytes and counts, two hashes and bytewise collision checks. The named unit specification covers edits and format differences but has not been run.

outcomeResults.description: Connect normalized/integer/interleaved/multiple-stream/per-instance vertex layouts to actual buffer slots, shader inputs and draws. Test values and pixels, not only descriptors.
outcomeResults.reason: Forward submission and both native binders carry stream slots and typed/instance layouts, including GL integer pointers and WebGPU native/conversion paths. Tests inspect actual bytes and normalized-instance pixels, but located pixels do not exercise integer shader inputs; native acceptance was not run.

outcomeResults.description: Weighted order-independent transparency with explicit approximation
outcomeResults.reason: The pass performs approximate weighted accumulation and revealage, alpha composition and opaque-depth sampling with per-view allocations and sorted fallback. The public renderer limits it to generated unlit WebGL2/mock frames and excludes multi-view.

outcomeResults.description: Pixel-check culling, custom blend, stencil, color masks, polygon offset, depth comparison and instance data on each backend.
outcomeResults.reason: The browser specification defines WebGL2 and WebGPU pixel checks for culling/winding, depth comparisons, bias, stencil, masks, custom blending and separate instance streams. It can skip unavailable devices; the specification was not executed and is not a pixel-pass receipt.

outcomeResults.description: Preserve stable ordering and explicit overrides across opaque, masked, transmissive and blended buckets.
outcomeResults.reason: The general sorter defines stable tie handling and explicit ordering for four buckets. Actual forward bucketing never emits mask, and the split renderer graph draws opaque, transmission and transparent in separate phases even if renderOrder would cross those phases.

outcomeResults.description: Carry temporal identity and global/material clipping through draw-item contracts. Exclusive execution owner: wp31_recovery. Source verification: tests/unit/rendering/native-clipping.test.ts; tests/unit/rendering/native-temporal-frames.test.ts.
outcomeResults.reason: RenderItem carries a stable temporal object key and independent global/material clipping groups; clipping and temporal-frame source specifications exist and were not run.

outcomeResults.description: alpha composition
outcomeResults.reason: The lower-level weighted implementation includes separate view resources, depth and alpha equations and sorted fallback; it is not available in the renderer for multiview or WebGPU and declines many combinations.

outcomeResults.description: Test intersecting transparent layers under different submission orders, opaque occluders, premultiplied alpha, multisampling, views and teardown. Document weighted transparency's approximation and keep refraction/dispersion in their own supported path.
outcomeResults.reason: The browser fixture describes intersecting layers, order permutation, premultiplication, occlusion, views, cleanup and MSAA fallback, and approximation and transmission boundaries are documented. The fixture uses a handwritten WebGPU shader and a caller-injected transmission reason, not the integrated renderer paths. A separate source specification documents that ResourceLifecycle may complete before a waiting WebGPU fence later rejects; no acceptance or unit test run was performed.

outcomeResults.description: Carry complete state, clipping, depth and ordering into actual draw submissions.
outcomeResults.reason: DrawSubmit forwards state and streams and ForwardPass selects clipping and sorting. Material state omits several command fields, nonstandard renderer depth is rejected, and split phases do not preserve cross-bucket renderOrder.

outcomeResults.description: Full depth/stencil/blend/cull/color-mask/offset/sample state on both devices
outcomeResults.reason: Device implementations cover broad native state and typed vertex streams, but RenderState cannot type all RenderCommandState fields, WebGL has explicit state limitations, and generated WebGPU alpha-to-coverage is rejected.

outcomeResults.description: Preserve typed buffer bytes during batching or explicitly reject unsupported layouts. Exclusive execution owner: wp31_recovery/vertex_buffer. Source verification: tests/unit/rendering/native-vertex-buffer.test.ts.
outcomeResults.reason: The packed pool copies complete bytes including padding and non-float storage. It rejects non-single-vertex-stream layouts and the planner passes unsupported layouts through instead of corrupting them; the named source test exists.

outcomeResults.description: Full depth/stencil/blend/cull/color-mask/offset/sample state on both devices; normalized/integer/multiple-stream/per-instance vertex formats and complete pipeline/program cache identities.
outcomeResults.reason: Expanded state, vertex streams, weighted math and structural program keys are present, but the material surface is narrower, integer pixels are not specified, weighted renderer views/WebGPU are unavailable and active log-depth selection is not integrated.

outcomeResults.description: Weighted order-independent transparency with explicit approximation and sorted fallback, opaque depth interaction, alpha composition and independent view resources.
outcomeResults.reason: The prior missing-weighted finding is superseded by an actual bounded renderer route with diagnostics and whole-group fallback. It admits only generated unlit WebGL2 alpha triangles; WebGPU generated weighted WGSL and renderer multiview are not enabled.

outcomeResults.description: Include all shader-affecting fields, separate device/target generations and avoid recompiling for ordinary uniform changes.
outcomeResults.reason: Program keys normalize structural features, the per-device program cache invalidates on device generation, and WebGPU pipeline keys include target/device generations. Forward log-depth selection and full graph/depth dependencies are incomplete, so universal variant correctness and uniform-only reuse are not established.

outcomeResults.description: distinguish dynamic state from pipeline state and include all relevant attachment/layout/feature fields in cache identity.
outcomeResults.reason: The native GPU fixed/dynamic split and identity are wired to pipeline creation, but this row repeats the two-device task: Material lacks command fields, WebGL rejects several requested combinations and generated GPU materials reject alpha-to-coverage.

outcomeResults.description: Integrate clipping/depth/color and graph outputs; preserve independently implemented generation and complete variant dependencies.
outcomeResults.reason: Generator and selectors include clipping, output, graph outputs and live physical map/UV features. However the renderer rejects nonstandard camera depth, generated depth warmup is excluded, graph-mask depth and weighted WGSL variants explicitly reject, so complete variant dependencies are not integrated.

outcomeResults.description: opaque depth interaction
outcomeResults.reason: Weighted fragments sample the matching opaque depth and the renderer requires a live sampleable depth target. This fixes the old absence for its eligible WebGL path, but the renderer declines WebGPU and multiview weighted frames; no current occlusion pixel receipt exists.

outcomeResults.description: Implement every supported depth/stencil/blend/color-mask/cull/winding/offset/sample field in each device; distinguish dynamic state from pipeline state and include all relevant attachment/layout/feature fields in cache identity.
outcomeResults.reason: WebGPU uses fixed-state pipeline keys and dynamic commands; WebGL applies state per draw. Material-facing state lacks winding, sample mask, blend constant and attachment overrides, while backend restrictions are explicitly rejected.

outcomeResults.description: Render intersecting layers in permuted submission order, compare bounded output, and verify depth/transmission fallback, views and cleanup.
outcomeResults.reason: A browser fixture specifies ordered/permuted intersections, depth, view isolation and teardown. Its WebGPU weighted shader is fixture-authored, transmission fallback is injected as a reason rather than triggered by a transmissive material, and device absence can skip the case; it is not integrated renderer acceptance. A separate source specification documents synchronous lifecycle completion before a late WebGPU fence rejection. Neither was run.

outcomeResults.description: Carry graph variant identity and preserve rendering state through static merge planning. Exclusive execution owner: wp31_recovery. Source verification: tests/unit/rendering/native-render-state.test.ts.
outcomeResults.reason: Static merge identity includes shader variant and full render-state signature, and materials whose variants would be lost by synthesized PBR are explicitly passed through. A separate vertex-buffer specification exercises variant passthrough; the named native state test covers fixed-state keys. Neither was run.

outcomeResults.description: Define full named/custom blend, depth and alpha semantics consumed by both devices.
outcomeResults.reason: The shared blend contract defines named/custom color and alpha factors, equations and depth comparisons; both native binders consume the resolved state. Existing tests specify named and custom mappings, not a current passing receipt.

outcomeResults.description: refraction
outcomeResults.reason: A separate bounded scene-color transmission/refraction path, IOR/dispersion parameters and fallback documentation exist. The full referenced cross-domain checklist also names volumetrics and water, for which the environment source explicitly reports bounded or helper/unsupported capabilities; it is not defensible to mark the entire row complete from refraction alone.

outcomeResults.description: Map full draw state to native pipeline/dynamic state and a deterministic cache key including attachment/layout requirements.
outcomeResults.reason: NativeRenderState validates supported formats and combinations, resolves primitive/color/depth/multisample and layouts, separates dynamic state, and constructs a deterministic device/target/shader/layout key. WebGPU consumes the result when creating and selecting pipelines.

outcomeResults.description: Carry every supported state field into pipeline creation and cache identity; reject invalid combinations before submission. WP-31 with WP-03/WP-05 integration.
outcomeResults.reason: The original observation that native GPU ignores most command state is outdated: native fixed and dynamic mappings are submitted. Complete state remains limited at the material boundary, and unsupported WebGL states and generated GPU alpha-to-coverage reject.

outcomeResults.description: Implement bounded weighted accumulation/revealage with opaque-depth testing, composition, per-view lifetime and explicit sorted fallback.
outcomeResults.reason: The exported lower-level pass implements bounded accumulation/revealage, sampled depth, premultiplied composition, per-view targets and fallback. Renderer integration admits a narrow WebGL2/mock route and explicitly declines multiview and WebGPU, so the per-view and backend requirements are not fully integrated. For WebGPU resources, interop retains a failed-fence lease, but a synchronous lifecycle can have completed while that fence was waiting and cannot be retroactively re-enrolled after rejection.

outcomeResults.description: Validate complete render-state combinations and backend requirements; version any change to currently rejected blended depth writes.
outcomeResults.reason: Material preserves the existing blended-depth-write rejection and native backends validate many combinations before drawing. Material validation is narrower than the shared command validator and its state type omits native fields; the command validator checks the blendedDepthWrite token's value but does not enforce an opt-in for blended depth writes.

outcomeResults.description: Support typed/normalized integer inputs, alignment, separate streams and per-instance step modes.
outcomeResults.reason: VertexFormat represents typed, normalized and integer attributes, aligned byte offsets, multiple slots, vertex/instance step modes and divisors with validation. WebGPU's divisor-one restriction is explicitly enforced at submission; source specifications exist.

outcomeResults.description: Preserve existing video polling, canvas uploads and data subregion updates. Extend only gaps demonstrated in the declared 3D/layer/mip/media contract; keep correct source lifetime, orientation, dimensions, color metadata and storage reuse.
outcomeResults.reason: Polling, retained array rectangles, whole-mip updates and borrowed-source cleanup exist, but 3D subregions and compressed fallback revisions are unavailable; WebGPU lacks equivalent VideoFrame dimension/lifetime preflight. Fence-retired native texture storage can outlive a completed ResourceLifecycle if a waiting fence later rejects.

outcomeResults.description: Verify known color vectors, HDR values above one and below zero, output readback, layered/mip update isolation, changing media frames, compressed-block validation and final cleanup on supported backends.
outcomeResults.reason: Test specifications cover HDR/color vectors, readback, media, subresources and blocks, but the packed color spec expects a missing diagnostics.output.colorSpace field and its P3 fixture is WebGL2-only. The dynamic browser fixture does not observe WebGPU native-handle retirement; a mocked test exposes completion before a later fence rejection. No test was run.

outcomeResults.description: Reuse the shared conversion path and remove type-only claims of unsupported color spaces.
outcomeResults.reason: Production conversions delegate to the shared managed converter and declare only implemented spaces. The associated WGSL variants, independent output cases and BC1 tests for WebGL/WebGPU and ownership are present.

outcomeResults.description: Negotiate output color space and apply one final tone/gamut/transfer transform with explicit alpha handling.
outcomeResults.reason: OutputPass validates negotiation and alpha, requires a premultiplied linear input warranty for alpha preservation, and selects a tone/gamut/transfer shader variant. Unsupported P3 render targets and unverifiable canvas alpha are rejected.

outcomeResults.description: HDR
outcomeResults.reason: HDR-preserving scene conversions and float intermediates exist with bounded tone-mapped output and fallback; physical HDR display swapchain output is explicitly not exposed.

outcomeResults.description: Add HDR-preserving conversion and negotiated output color spaces; preserve existing dynamic textures and extend only verified gaps in their declared resource contract. WP-32.
outcomeResults.reason: HDR conversion, app policy forwarding and negotiated output exist. Dynamic contracts remain incomplete for WebGPU external-frame dimensions/lifetime, 3D regions and compressed fallback revisions; a later fence failure can outlive ResourceLifecycle completion, and direct-path runtime output changes can be ignored.

outcomeResults.description: Support requested sRGB and Display-P3 output when the context supports them
outcomeResults.reason: WebGL2 and WebGPU negotiate P3 and report a fallback, but WebGPU proactively restricts P3 to opaque unorm and does not negotiate a potentially supported premultiplied canvas.

outcomeResults.description: HDR-preserving color transforms, negotiated wide-gamut output, data-map/alpha handling and truthful output labels; retained dynamic media/layer/mip updates and clean source disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: Managed transforms, negotiated labels, data-map handling, media updates and borrowed-source cleanup exist. WebGPU constrains P3; 3D subregions and compressed-fallback revisions are unavailable. Native storage is fence-retired, but ResourceLifecycle can complete before a later rejection.

outcomeResults.description: clean source disposal
outcomeResults.reason: Source disposal notifies owners, clears polling and references without closing borrowed sources; compiler-owned bitmaps are closed by their owner. This source-ownership finding does not certify native WebGPU storage retirement, which is fence-gated and has a separate late-rejection lifecycle gap.

outcomeResults.description: texture/clear/save/output stages
outcomeResults.reason: The post graph implements an output stage and texture-based effects, and clear-mask is supported. Separate public texture, clear and save stages required by this checklist are not established by the current post stage/effect types.

outcomeResults.description: Implement shared scene-referred color transforms with extended-range linear identity, independently derived primary conversion and explicit tone/gamut/output stages. Preserve existing normalized helpers through a versioned contract where necessary.
outcomeResults.reason: The separate managed API derives D65 primary conversions and preserves extended scene-linear identity, with explicit tone/gamut/transfer stages; legacy normalized helpers retain clamping.

outcomeResults.description: Test retained update/storage identity, source orientation, layer/mip/range validation, media frame lifetime and disposal.
outcomeResults.reason: The named untracked test includes WebGL storage, orientation, layer/mip/range, disposal and mocked closed-VideoFrame preflight cases. Separate WebGPU mock tests cover upload disposal and fence ownership, including late rejection, but equivalent external-frame preflight coverage on WebGPU is not established.

outcomeResults.description: negotiated wide-gamut output
outcomeResults.reason: Both backends negotiate P3 or sRGB fallback, and the app now reads the negotiated value rather than hard-coding sRGB. WebGPU limits P3 to opaque unorm surfaces.

outcomeResults.description: report active output/fallback and distinguish float rendering, wide gamut and physical HDR display evidence. Keep colorless maps linear and alpha handling consistent.
outcomeResults.reason: The visual report separates negotiation/fallback, float and physical HDR, and mounted app diagnostics observe active color or unknown; data and alpha are handled explicitly. The app output diagnostics do not expose the requested/active/fallback object expected by the packed test.

outcomeResults.description: Shader-buffer layouts use typed byte storage, explicit signed/unsigned/bool representation, array/structure alignment, matrix stride and padding for each target language and uniform/storage address space. A Float32Array view is not an integer encoder. Tests compare exact byte patterns, offsets and uploaded/read-back values, including mixed fields and non-square matrices.
outcomeResults.reason: Typed staging, target-specific layouts and bool-to-u32 lowering exist. Exact bytes, mixed fields and non-square matrix tests exist, but uploaded/read-back mixed-field values are checked with MockRenderDevice rather than a real backend round trip.

outcomeResults.description: HDR-preserving color transforms
outcomeResults.reason: Managed conversions preserve finite negative and above-one linear values and derive primary transforms; old normalized helpers remain separately clamped.

outcomeResults.description: Preserve source color/unpack state and existing dynamic updates; implement declared layer/mip/subregion variants with correct storage reuse and context isolation.
outcomeResults.reason: WebGL restores unpack state and supports retained 2D/array updates and complete mip edits across contexts; 3D subregions and compressed fallback updates remain unavailable.

outcomeResults.description: video
outcomeResults.reason: The public video-element factory polls readyState/currentTime per bind, retains color and orientation policy, and releases its borrowed source and callback on disposal. This finding does not assert generic VideoFrame support.

outcomeResults.description: Dynamic image/video/frame textures define source ownership, dimensions, color metadata, orientation, alpha mode, update cadence, partial ranges/layers/mips and cancellation. Update retained storage when capacity/layout permits; release replaced storage and stop callbacks on final disposal. Reject invalid compressed-block alignment and external-frame lifetime errors before upload. Separate frame availability from successful rendered output.
outcomeResults.reason: Borrowed ownership, polling, flip, per-mip data, callback cleanup and fence-retired WebGPU storage exist; WebGL rejects zero-dimension closed frames. WebGPU lacks equivalent frame dimension/preflight, source alpha is undeclared, and 3D/compressed partial ranges are unsupported. ResourceLifecycle may complete before an accepted fence later rejects.

outcomeResults.description: Test known primaries, HDR identity, transfer round trips, alpha/data-map behavior and invalid inputs.
outcomeResults.reason: The named test contains independently referenced primaries, signed/HDR identity, round trips, alpha, data semantics and invalid-input cases. It was not run in this audit.

outcomeResults.description: truthful output labels
outcomeResults.reason: The current mounted-app report reads the verified device negotiation and publishes sRGB, P3 or unknown; the preset is explicitly a default, not the active label. This supersedes the checkpoint's hard-coded-label finding.

outcomeResults.description: Verify changing video/canvas/data pixels, dimension changes, layer/mip updates, app isolation and resource cleanup.
outcomeResults.reason: The packed browser spec covers both backends for changing media, dimensions, layers/mips and isolation, and checks logical cleanup. Its WebGPU cleanup snapshot precedes device disposal, nativeHandlesAfterDispose is null, and it does not wait for or verify actual native retirement; mock fence tests do not replace that backend check. None was run.

outcomeResults.description: partial uploads
outcomeResults.reason: UniformBlock can opt into aligned coalesced dirty-byte uploads, with full initial/invalidation writes and lifecycle protection; the contract assumes exclusive writes.

outcomeResults.description: Report actual negotiated color/output capabilities and fallback; keep physical HDR display distinct from float intermediates.
outcomeResults.reason: The visual report exposes requested/active/fallback, gamut, float support versus observed rendering, and unverified physical HDR. The earlier hard-coded app label has also been replaced by an observed or unknown value.

outcomeResults.description: Separate transfer, primaries and scene/display domains; preserve extended-range linear values and implement independently derived color transforms.
outcomeResults.reason: Managed spaces separate transfer and primaries, derive matrices from chromaticities and preserve finite scene-linear values; an explicit output transform provides display stages.

outcomeResults.description: Expose app-scoped output policy while preserving the default sRGB behavior.
outcomeResults.reason: Per-app policy is validated, defaults to sRGB/opaque and is forwarded at mount. Runtime changes can be ignored on the direct path and canvas alpha cannot be changed after creation.

outcomeResults.description: mip generation/update
outcomeResults.reason: Generated RGBA8 mipmaps and isolated full-mip replacement exist; raw-data generation is limited to RGBA8 and region updates cannot address a nonzero mip or 3D subvolume.

outcomeResults.description: Preserve existing video polling, canvas uploads and data subregion updates. Extend only gaps demonstrated in the declared 3D/layer/mip/media contract
outcomeResults.reason: Video polling, canvas and bounded array/data updates are implemented, but 3D subregion and compressed fallback update variants remain absent.

outcomeResults.description: Verify texture-to-lighting-to-post-to-presentation/readback and truthful wide-gamut fallback through packed APIs.
outcomeResults.reason: The packed spec drives textured lighting/post and readback, but its P3/fallback assertions require diagnostics.output.colorSpace; collectOutput currently returns no such field. The fixture is WebGL2-only. This is a source mismatch, not a claimed test result.

outcomeResults.description: Support requested sRGB and Display-P3 output when the context supports them; report active output/fallback and distinguish float rendering, wide gamut and physical HDR display evidence. Keep colorless maps linear and alpha handling consistent.
outcomeResults.reason: Negotiation, active/unknown app labels, visual capability distinctions, data-map and explicit alpha handling exist. The public output diagnostic omits the fallback object expected by the browser spec, and WebGPU rejects P3 with premultiplied presentation.

outcomeResults.description: canvas
outcomeResults.reason: Public canvas textures support dirty uploads, color and flip metadata, changing dimensions and borrowed-source cleanup.

outcomeResults.description: keep correct source lifetime, orientation, dimensions, color metadata and storage reuse.
outcomeResults.reason: Borrowed lifetime, orientation, color tags and retained storage exist; WebGL validates closed-frame dimensions. WebGPU ignores VideoFrame displayWidth/displayHeight and lacks equivalent preflight, and a completed ResourceLifecycle cannot reclaim its owner automatically after a later native-retirement fence rejection.

outcomeResults.description: data
outcomeResults.reason: Public data and data-array factories validate format and dimensions, and retained data updates support bounded 2D/array rectangles with typed content.

outcomeResults.description: retained dynamic media/layer/mip updates
outcomeResults.reason: Media revisions, array rectangles and full mip updates are retained; 3D subregions and revisions while using a decoded compressed fallback are rejected.

outcomeResults.description: color management
outcomeResults.reason: Managed HDR conversion, negotiated output and current observed app labels exist, but texture input tags are limited to sRGB/linear and WebGPU P3 output excludes premultiplied canvases.

outcomeResults.description: Keep the default linear working space and sRGB output stable. Add declared sRGB/linear-sRGB and Display-P3/linear-Display-P3 conversions with independently derived matrices and transfer functions. Preserve finite HDR and negative linear values in internal conversion; clamp only at a declared bounded output or explicit policy. Colorless data maps never receive color transfer functions. Wide-gamut canvas output and extended-range display are distinct capabilities; floating-point intermediate targets alone prove neither.
outcomeResults.reason: The declared sRGB/P3 transfer and primary families, finite extended-range conversion, explicit bounded output, linear data semantics and distinct gamut/float/physical-HDR reporting are present. The public diagnostic no longer assumes sRGB.

outcomeResults.description: Expose negotiated output and correct 3D texture sampling and format behavior. Exclusive execution owner: wp32_color. Source verification: tests/unit/rendering/native-color-management.test.ts; tests/unit/rendering/native-dynamic-textures.test.ts.
outcomeResults.reason: Device negotiation and 3D formats, target-specific sampling and WRAP_R exist; the prior 2D/3D sampler-key collision is fixed. However the public output collector lacks the negotiated color/fallback object required by the packed source test.

outcomeResults.description: data-map/alpha handling
outcomeResults.reason: Managed data semantics bypass transfer, material data bindings require linear metadata, and output explicitly validates alpha association and surface capabilities.

outcomeResults.description: Color-managed textures
outcomeResults.reason: sRGB/linear texture tags, sRGB storage and linear data bindings exist, but texture input metadata cannot express Display-P3 or linear-Display-P3, so the broader managed converter is not a P3 texture input path.

crossResults.description: Scalars, angles, interpolation, seeded randomness, color conversion and color spaces; 2D/3D/4D vectors; quaternions and Euler angles; 3×3/4×4 matrices; rays, planes, spheres, boxes, frustums, triangles, capsules, oriented boxes and spatial trees.
crossResults.reason: The public math package exports the listed vector, rotation, matrix, color, intersection and spatial-tree families. However SeededRandom accepts seed 0 and the xorshift state then remains zero forever, so its random draws, picks and shuffles are degenerate for an accepted seed. Numerical and random tests exist but were not run.

crossResults.description: Scene hierarchy, world/local transforms, pivots, reparenting, events, visibility, layers, metadata, cloning, serialization, traversal, disposal, bounds, skeleton and animated-object state.
crossResults.reason: Current scene code includes pivot-aware hierarchy, preserve-world reparenting, ancestry visibility, cloning, metadata, bounds, node disposal and serialization of skinning palettes and morph weights. Transform dirty notifications exist, but a general scene-node event dispatcher was not found; the serializer explicitly does not reconstruct live skeletons, clips or mixers without caller-owned adapters. The animated-rig adapter in the test is test-owned, not a built-in runtime restoration path. Separately from node disposal, a ResourceLifecycle tracking a borrowed WebGPU device can complete while a fence is waiting; a later rejection is retained and exposed by the device/interop, but cannot retroactively re-enroll the completed lifecycle.

crossResults.description: Perspective, orthographic, cube, array and stereo cameras; per-view projection, viewport/scissor, culling, postprocessing and camera controls.
crossResults.reason: Perspective, orthographic, cube, array and stereo authoring, per-view rectangles, camera controls and view-specific rendering paths exist. Per-view behavior is incomplete: scene-source frustum culling requires a Camera object even for a matrix-only view; mixed stereo projection kinds are rejected; and the native WebGPU depth-of-field route rejects multiview. Production camera depth also permits only standard depth.

crossResults.description: Points, sprites, thin/wide/dashed lines, line segments, wireframes and mesh primitives; indexed, non-indexed, instanced, batched, skinned and morphed geometry.
crossResults.reason: Public point, sprite, line, wireframe, mesh, instance and batch paths exist, with skinning and morph submission/query code. The combined primitive/deformation/depth coverage is bounded: native WebGPU point submissions reject instancing and deformation, WebGPU point depth is rejected, and packed multi-draw depth is unsupported. Clipped billboard, point and screen-space-line shadow paths also have explicit exclusions.

crossResults.description: Box, sphere, plane, circle, ring, cylinder, cone, capsule, torus, torus knot, polyhedra, lathe, extrude, shape, tube, rounded box, convex hull, decal, text, parametric, loft and patch geometry.
crossResults.reason: Public primitive builders and rendering dispatch cover the named basic, swept, polyhedral and rounded geometries; convex hull, projected decal and 3D text have separate public paths. The rendering package exports parametric, loft and the bicubic-patch teapot generators, and they can feed the root custom-geometry path. Limits are explicit: the patch reference is the teapot, and loaded-font text uses SDF rather than extrusion. Existing numerical and browser specifications were not run.

crossResults.description: Paths, splines, cubic and quadratic curves, ellipses, arcs, shapes, contours, holes, triangulation, rational curves/surfaces/volumes, derivatives and consistent arc-length sampling.
crossResults.reason: Paths, splines, Bezier/ellipse/arc curves, shapes and bounded triangulation are public; rational curves, surfaces and volumes implement weighted evaluation and derivatives. Arc-length sampling is approximate and has a concrete mutable-path cache gap: after CurvePath.add(), the inherited cached getLengths() table is not invalidated, although getLength() recomputes the total, until updateArcLengths() is called.

crossResults.description: Attribute formats and normalization; interleaving; shared buffers; update ranges; deindexing; merge, weld, remap, crease normals, tangent generation, morph evaluation, group preservation, mesh memory estimation and safe bounds.
crossResults.reason: Typed/normalized attributes, interleaving, shared-buffer ownership, dynamic updates, deindex/merge, weld/remap, crease normals, position morph evaluation, generated tangents and position bounds have source paths; the newer tools are publicly exported through the opt-in geometry-tools subpath. WebGPU interop retains native buffer leases through failed fences, but a ResourceLifecycle tracking a borrowed device can complete before an initially waiting fence later rejects; the device and interop still expose the failure, while that lifecycle stays completed. A general mesh-memory estimator was not established: the available batching estimate assumes four bytes per index even when IndexBuffer uses uint16 and does not account for all additional streams. Crease recomputation explicitly rejects directional morph deltas.

crossResults.description: Runtime simplification, edge split, tessellation, curve deformation, UV unwrapping, mesh compression helpers, deterministic surface sampling and topology validation.
crossResults.reason: The current public geometry-tools subpath exposes simplification, edge split, tessellation, curve deformation, bounded UV atlas generation and deterministic weighted surface sampling. Modifiers validate triangle inputs and preserve or report supported channels. A general topology-validation/reporting API and runtime mesh-compression encoder were not established: the located compression paths are offline GLB optimization or adapters around injected glTF decoders. Atlas unwrapping is explicitly bounded rather than general.

crossResults.description: Physical film/focal-length camera projection, tiled/asymmetric views, explicit depth conventions and valid near/far/infinite-far behavior; clipping planes and section views apply consistently to supported primitives, materials and shadows.
crossResults.reason: Physical lens and tiled projection, near/far validation, depth-convention math, scene/material clipping and supported depth/shadow bindings exist. The production compiler and renderer reject reversed and logarithmic depth rather than implementing the required negotiated cross-pass modes; clipped point, billboard and screen-space-line depth and packed multi-draw depth are explicitly unsupported. Source and browser specifications exist without a current-candidate pass.

crossResults.description: UV atlas charting, seams, gutters, density and packing with preserved/remapped groups, attributes and morphs; generated UVs reach the real baking path.
crossResults.reason: Public bounded atlas generation returns chart, seam, gutter, density and vertex/index remap data and preserves supported streams; a public adapter feeds its result to the native CPU lightmap baker, and a root lighting attachment path exists. The source test that feeds a real generated atlas to the baker uses authored ambient lighting, which the production lightmap binding rejects; the browser bake fixture supplies a hand-authored atlas. A test showing the actual generated atlas baked and used by a scene was not found.

crossResults.description: WebGL2 and native WebGPU backend selection, capability negotiation, async initialization, explicit fallback, resize, multi-view, device/context loss, recovery, diagnostics and disposal.
crossResults.reason: Backend selection validates required features and explicit fallback, app code remounts after WebGPU loss, and teardown retains and reports observed native cleanup failures. A waiting fence is transferred to interop and can let ResourceLifecycle report disposed before the fence later rejects; the device then exposes the error but the lifecycle cannot re-enroll it. Multi-view composition rejects preserved alpha and alternate native paths fall back for multiple views.

crossResults.description: Forward and clustered lighting plus independently implemented deferred, meshlet and visibility-buffer drawing paths where the hardware supports them; per-object/per-view culling, batching, render bundles, transparency, sorting and deterministic fallback.
crossResults.reason: Forward/clustered lighting, distinct native deferred/meshlet/visibility routes and integrated render-bundle capture exist; bundle retirement retains individually failed cleanup steps. Alternative native routes fall back or reject multi-view frames, and deferred does so for fog, shadows and more than one directional light; broad path parity is incomplete.

crossResults.description: Basic/unlit, Lambert, Phong, standard/physical, toon, matcap, normal, depth, distance, line, point, sprite, shadow, custom shader and typed node materials; front/back/double side, alpha, blending, clipping and wireframe behavior.
crossResults.reason: Public builders now include physical, toon, matcap, normal, depth, distance and shadow materials. Lambert and Phong migrate to approximate PBR, specialized materials have restricted routes, custom blend factors are rejected and subtractive blending maps to alpha; the full material/side/clipping/wireframe family is incomplete.

crossResults.description: Base color, metalness, roughness, normal/bump/displacement, emissive, occlusion and light maps; layered clearcoat, transmission, diffuse transmission, volume, IOR, sheen, anisotropy, specular, iridescence, dispersion, retroreflection and rough diffuse with relevant maps/UV channels.
crossResults.reason: The physical material exposes numerous lobes, maps and UV selections, including low-level diffuse transmission, and a separate lightmap baker exists. The root material slots do not expose a displacement map or a distinct light map; the occlusion slot is described as AO/lightmap, and extension combinations remain bounded.

crossResults.description: Ambient, hemisphere, directional, point, spot, rectangular-area, photometric and projected lights; physically meaningful units, shadow maps/filters, cascades, environment lighting, reflection probes, light-probe grids, incremental light baking and voxel-based indirect lighting where supported.
crossResults.reason: Typed light builders, photometric profiles, cascades and bounded voxel/probe/bake implementations exist. Projected spots currently require WebGL2 and one projection per direct-light packet, and clustered projection/profile indexing is explicitly unsupported.

crossResults.description: Color-managed textures, data, canvas, video, cube, 2D array, 3D, compressed, depth and storage textures; format selection, filtering, anisotropy, wrapping, mip generation/update, upload and readback.
crossResults.reason: Texture factories and upload paths cover data, media, cube, arrays, 3D and storage, with per-mip updates; sampled-native texture cleanup retires leases and budget charges. Native compute depth sampling requires a same-device single-sampled depth attachment, graph storage bindings are 2D, compressed 3D is rejected, and WebGPU's active-target pixel readback does not implement the generic target-readback contract.

crossResults.description: Render targets with color/depth attachments, multiple outputs, cube/array/3D layers, multisampling, resolving, copy and readback; correct resource sharing, synchronization and ownership.
crossResults.reason: Attachment hazard validation, WebGL copy/resolve/readback, bounded native WebGPU color copy/pixel readback, and same-queue ownership and fenced retirement are present; target disposal tracks individual attachment failures. The descriptor cannot express 3D target layers; WebGPU rejects layered/depth-only targets and multisampled sampleable depth, omits the generic async target-transfer methods, and an owner can complete before a later fence failure is visible.

crossResults.description: Tone mapping, exposure, color management, environment prefiltering, HDR, sky, fog, volumetrics, water, reflections, refraction and depth-aware transparency; document fallback quality.
crossResults.reason: HDR targets, exposure/color transforms, environmental lighting, water and depth-aware transparency have real routes. Native WebGPU tone mapping only admits a subset of operators, weighted depth transparency has explicit restrictions, and the HDR display swapchain is not exposed; full feature-by-feature fallback quality is not established.

crossResults.description: Bloom, depth of field, AO variants, reflections, indirect lighting, anti-aliasing, film/grain, color lookup and grading, glitch, halftone, dot-screen, pixelation, transition, afterimage, masks, texture/clear/save/output stages, motion blur, lens dirt and outlines.
crossResults.reason: Numerous effect builders and WebGL GTAO, SSR, SMAA and temporal stages are present, with a browser effect specification. WebGPU retains failed native post/history cleanup for retry, but its post admission rejects passes outside bloom, tone mapping, color grade, FXAA and TAA (separate bounded native effects/DoF routes also exist); full effect family and texture/save stages are not established.

crossResults.description: Typed shader graphs, functions, flow control, variables, arrays, structs, math, noise, color, texture sampling, UV transforms, lighting hooks, screen/depth inputs, storage, atomics, barriers and compute dispatch. Generate and validate shaders for each supported backend.
crossResults.reason: The current untracked graph implementation now includes authored structs, arrays, functions, noise, control statements, GLSL/WGSL generation and a material adapter. Material graphs reject statements, graph types exclude matrices, and compute binding validation rejects aggregate buffer types even though the IR represents them; backend compiler/pixel coverage is unverified.

crossResults.description: GPU sorting, compute/render interop, indirect/instanced work, query/readback, resource lifetime and memory budget behavior. Unsupported features must produce precise diagnostics.
crossResults.reason: A bounded GPU sorter, same-queue compute/render leases, indirect meshlet culling, specialized timestamp queries and target-memory inventory exist. Interop keeps failed or unavailable-fence leases until confirmed invalidation and reports observed failures; however, ResourceLifecycle can complete while an accepted fence is still waiting, before its later rejection, and cannot retroactively retain the owner. General cross-backend query and comprehensive device-wide memory-budget behavior remain unestablished.

crossResults.description: Gaussian splats and scalar volumes: format parsing, camera-dependent projection/order, covariance, spherical harmonics, alpha/depth, volume slicing and transfer functions.
crossResults.reason: Splat projection/sorting and scalar volume slices, transfer functions and clipping exist, including untracked renderers; the native splat adapter guards borrowed depth and retains ambiguous scratch cleanup failures. KSPLAT decoding requires an explicitly supplied codec and compressed PLY also needs one; the typed-scene node and transport options expose no codec-injection contract.

crossResults.description: Full depth/stencil/blend/cull/color-mask/offset/sample state on both devices; normalized/integer/multiple-stream/per-instance vertex formats and complete pipeline/program cache identities.
crossResults.reason: Typed normalized/integer vertex attributes and multiple/per-instance streams reach backend routes, and the native pipeline key includes generation and fixed state. Material-level RenderState omits front-face, blend constant and sample mask even though lower-level command state has them; WebGL rejects arbitrary masks and polygon-offset clamp, so complete public state/cache coverage is not established.

crossResults.description: Weighted order-independent transparency with explicit approximation and sorted fallback, opaque depth interaction, alpha composition and independent view resources.
crossResults.reason: The weighted pass implements approximate accumulation/revealage, sorted fallback, opaque-depth input and view-keyed resources. Renderer integration is restricted to WebGL2/mock and explicitly blocks multi-view frames; the WebGPU shader is source-only rather than an active native path.

crossResults.description: App/view/frame-owned current/previous transforms and depth, once-per-frame commits, reactive/disocclusion masks, documented temporal reconstruction and normalized centered motion blur.
crossResults.reason: View/frame-scoped transform history, reactive input/disocclusion checks and centered, normalized WebGL motion blur exist. Skin/morph/instance pixels are marked reactive until real deformation history is supplied, and native WebGPU explicitly rejects temporal reconstruction v2.

crossResults.description: Byte-correct mixed shader data, uniform/storage arrays and structures, matrix strides, alignment, partial uploads and independent async readback ownership.
crossResults.reason: Recursive target-specific layouts encode signed/unsigned integer bits, matrices, arrays and structs; partial uniform uploads and separate compute and native pixel readback staging exist. WebGPU pixel staging is leased and retired after mapping, but current graph compute binding rejects aggregate uniform/storage resource types and the graph IR cannot express matrix values, so the entire public shader-data path is not integrated.

crossResults.description: HDR-preserving color transforms, negotiated wide-gamut output, data-map/alpha handling and truthful output labels; retained dynamic media/layer/mip updates and clean source disposal.
crossResults.reason: Extended-range conversions, negotiated Display-P3, truthful mounted output diagnostics, video polling and retained mip updates exist; WebGPU sampled texture disposal tracks subscription, retirement and budget cleanup failures. Texture.dispose drops borrowed media references but suppresses listener errors. P3 requires an opaque unorm canvas, 3D updates require whole mips, compressed fallback updates are rejected, input texture tags only cover linear/sRGB, and a later fence failure cannot re-enroll a completed synchronous lifecycle.

crossResults.description: Typed identity, hashes, licenses, dependency discovery, lifecycle, caching, progress, cancellation, independent subscribers and security-context isolation for documents, buffers and images.
crossResults.reason: Typed asset references carry hashes and optional license metadata; the manager and glTF paths implement dependency ownership, digest checks, progress, request-context keys and independently cancellable subscribers. However, directly invoked ImageLoader fetches the raw request URL without resolving LoadContext.baseUrl, so a relative image can target a different URL or fail the intended policy; the complete image identity and request guarantee is not integrated across public paths.

crossResults.description: glTF/GLB geometry, buffers, textures, compression, materials, animation, skins, morphs, cameras, lights, variants, instancing and every declared material extension, including diffuse roughness and bump.
crossResults.reason: The glTF loader and render resources cover substantial geometry, material, animation, instancing and variant paths, including optional diffuse-roughness and bump bindings. Required KHR_animation_pointer is supported for a bounded set of validated targets, including emissive strength when its material extension is present; unsupported required targets such as camera leaves are rejected rather than all required pointers being rejected. The support matrix still declares the two draft diffuse-roughness and bump extensions parse-only and not accepted when required, and the loader rejects them as required; omitted punctual-light ranges also default to 10 rather than unlimited. Thus the complete declared-extension and light contract is not met.

crossResults.description: FBX, USD/USDZ, Collada, 3MF, 3DM, AMF, 3DS, VRML, LDraw, KMZ, OBJ/MTL, PLY, STL, VOX, SVG, BVH, MD2, MDD, PCD, PDB, VTK, XYZ, NRRD and GCode, with each format's supported versions and loss boundaries recorded.
crossResults.reason: There are substantial scene, mesh, scientific, animation and legacy-format importers, with several source tests and documented bounded variants. The 3DM adapter requires an application-supplied decoder rather than decoding the archive itself, the default registry installs only glTF, and the documentation does not yet record supported versions and loss boundaries for each listed format; data parsers are not automatically renderable adapters.

crossResults.description: EXR, HDR, JXL, UltraHDR, DDS, PVR, KTX1/KTX2, TGA, TIFF, ordinary web images, photometric profiles, cube environments, 3DL/image color tables and MaterialX documents, subject to explicit codec capabilities.
crossResults.reason: EXR, specialized image formats, photometry, cube background, LUT, MaterialX and a separate production Radiance environment loader exist; JXL and UltraHDR explicitly require application-supplied codecs. However, the public assets HDRLoader.load returns a file diagnostic rather than fetching and returning a decoded HDR asset, leaving that named loader path incomplete despite the renderer's separate HDR support.

crossResults.description: PLY/SPLAT/KSPLAT/SPZ and registered glTF splat data with versioned validation and resource limits.
crossResults.reason: The splat loader validates bounded PLY, SPLAT, SPZ v1-4 and glTF/GLB splat paths, including point, byte and decoded-array limits. KSPLAT has no native version/section decoder or validation: it requires an injected codec, and the typed app's splat mount constructs the loader without providing one, so that listed format is not integrated on that public route.

crossResults.description: GLTF/GLB, OBJ, PLY, STL, USDZ, compressed mesh, EXR and KTX2 export; embedded/external dependencies; independent round-trip validation and explicit structured loss reports.
crossResults.reason: All named exporter entrypoints, dependency outputs and structured warnings exist, and source tests exercise several independent readers and loss cases. The glTF snapshot/writer now preserves verified required animation-pointer provenance, including an authored explicit or implicit default emissive strength, and errors on detected loss or retargeting; source tests exercise material remapping, self-reloads and identity loss. This is bounded by in-memory source identity: without a loader lookup, original requiredness is unknown and warnings replace the verified-required guarantee; mixing required with optional or unknown pointer channels is rejected. Independent semantic round-trip validation across every exporter is still not established: the USDZ test parses the ZIP but checks USDA text rather than reading the stage with an independent USD reader, while PLY/STL cases mainly inspect selected bytes and fields. No current-candidate passing round-trip receipt was established.

crossResults.description: Identical request/integrity/cancellation guarantees for public audio, image, scene and generic model loaders; explicit canonical fixtures, accurate orientation and no unrelated fallback success.
crossResults.reason: Audio and scene loaders use the shared fetch/integrity path, the bitmap loader forwards orientation and closes late results, and canonical scenes require explicit selection with no unknown-file fallback. The public ImageLoader nevertheless fetches the unresolved request URL rather than the URL resolved against its LoadContext, unlike audio and scene loaders; this can fetch or validate the wrong context-relative target, contradicting identical request and integrity behavior for direct calls.

crossResults.description: Production decoder/worker URLs match development URLs under root/nested deployment bases; emitted same-origin workers, documented content policy, MIME validation and offline resource cleanup.
crossResults.reason: The Vite plugin maps root and nested bases for Basis, Draco and Meshopt, emits the KTX2 worker, and the worker pool checks MIME and terminates on disposal; deployment/CSP guidance and corresponding tests exist. The SPZ Zstandard worker instead uses a separate module-relative or packaged-manifest URL outside that plugin mapping, and matching development/production URLs for every emitted worker and deployment base remain unestablished.

crossResults.description: Numeric, boolean, string, color, vector, quaternion, matrix, morph and material-property tracks; step, linear, smooth, Bézier and glTF cubic-spline interpolation.
crossResults.reason: Scalar, discrete, vector, color, quaternion and morph values and the listed curve modes have implementations; discrete tracks explicitly reject nonlinear interpolation. A matrix is only representable as a generic number-array: a matrix-specific public scene/application contract and test were not established. Live glTF material-pointer playback is restricted to mapped leaves and reports other leaves unsupported.

crossResults.description: Clip/action lifecycle, duration, negative/positive time scale, repeat, ping-pong, crossfades, weights, mixing, masking, event timing, synchronization, serialization, root motion and retargeting.
crossResults.reason: Actions, signed repeat/ping-pong traversal, fades, mixing, masks, synchronization, root motion, retarget math and serialization exist, with focused source tests. However the public actor retarget operation silently returns an empty result when the animation flag is off or the runtime is unavailable, and PoseMixer cannot serialize an active inertial transition; the unrestricted integrated lifecycle/serialization contract is therefore incomplete.

crossResults.description: Skeleton hierarchies, bind/inverse matrices, skinned rendering, morph targets, facial controls, procedural poses, two-bone and iterative IK, animation bounds and disposal.
crossResults.reason: Skeleton hierarchy and inverse-bind palettes, skinned/morph bounds, facial morph mapping, two-bone and iterative IK, and runtime palette cleanup exist. The public actor pose setter and IK registration become silent no-ops when A3D_QR_ANIMATION is off (or IK is used before the actor is loaded); the checklist does not limit procedural poses or IK to the flag-on path. A visible skinned-pixel test exists, but no current-source pass was established.

crossResults.description: Audio listeners, positional emitters, orientation, distance/cone models, buffers, media elements, streams, external audio nodes, effects, analysers, detune, loop regions, playback-rate changes and pause/resume.
crossResults.reason: The public audio surface supplies listener/spatial graphs, world orientation, distance/cone models, effects and analysis, buffer playback with detune, loop regions, rate changes and pause/resume, plus media-element, stream and external-node adapters. The adapter contract explicitly limits non-buffer transports: stream/node pause mutes the private route, and loop regions, detune and scheduled starts are buffer-only.

crossResults.description: Orbit, map, arcball, trackball, fly, first-person, pointer-lock, transform and drag controls, including pointer capture, touch, keyboard, cancellation, focus and cleanup.
crossResults.reason: All named control classes are exported; drag handles per-contact capture, cancellation and parent transforms, and shared input supplies keyboard, touch and focus handling. TransformControls exposes caller-driven ray methods rather than owning a browser capture/focus bridge, and the control documentation still incorrectly says the package owns no DOM listeners and that Arcball lacks cursor zoom/two-finger gestures despite the current source. Thus the required integrated, accurately documented coverage is not established.

crossResults.description: Exact ray and screen picking, instances, deformed meshes, material side, UV/face/normal output, interactive groups and marquee selection.
crossResults.reason: Mesh-mode world-ray/camera-NDC queries implement triangle hits, sides, UV/face/normal, instances and CPU skin/morph deformation; interactive groups and instance-aware marquee selection exist. Exact queries nevertheless return no hits for custom vertex shaders, instance attributes or wind deformation, and marquee/interactive groups default to bounds, needing caller-supplied live bounds or exact hits. The broad deformed-mesh and integrated exact-selection coverage is therefore incomplete.

crossResults.description: Immersive and inline sessions, per-eye views, cameras, controllers, hands, joints, hit tests, planes, depth, light estimation, session permissions, reference-space changes and disposal; separate real-device verification.
crossResults.reason: The controller negotiates inline/immersive sessions and samples controllers, hands/joints, viewer, hit tests, planes, depth and light; the app renders per-eye and handles session/reference-space lifecycle. Public app presentation is specifically tied to a WebGL2 context and refuses unavailable render bridges, so WebGPU XR presentation is not established. The separate physical-device checklist remains open; injected fixtures are not device evidence.

crossResults.description: Timestamp-based, contact-ID-stable gestures and correct client/CSS/framebuffer coordinates; cancellation never activates input, and asynchronous XR startup cannot outlive its owner.
crossResults.reason: Contact records retain IDs, timestamps and client/CSS/framebuffer positions; the recognizer uses elapsed tap time and stable pinch IDs. Pointer cancellation, capture loss, blur and disconnect are separated from release and suppress tap/click activation. XR session startup and app runtime use generation/ownership checks and close late-acquired sessions; native-shaped cancellation and coordinate tests exist.

crossResults.description: Large-step animation event traversal, reflected/reverse time, bounded catch-up, shape-preserving key optimization and animation-group cache resubscription without stale bindings.
crossResults.reason: The action/event traversal handles signed multi-wrap and reflected time with explicit bounded overflow, and compiled-pose and glTF paths route through that playback. Optimization retains curved/tangent-bearing keys, and object-group membership/subscription maps invalidate stale bindings. Existing focused tests compare large/small updates, sampled curve preservation and uncache/resubscribe behavior.

crossResults.description: Environment helpers, reflection/refraction surfaces, sky/water, lens flares, marching surfaces, grounded backgrounds, procedural tree/forest/terrain/city/street objects, sculpting, tube painting and convex fracture.
crossResults.reason: Environment stages, a horizontal mirror, capture-bound glass refraction, sky/water, lens flares, grounded sky, marching surfaces, seeded generators and sculpt/tube/fracture addons have source paths. Coverage is incomplete: native WebGPU rejects several publicly exposed sky models/effects, water's planar reflection redraw currently wires terrain only, and the root surface namespace exposes a mirror but not a standalone refractor. Lens-flare occlusion is frustum-only rather than geometry-aware. Relevant unit and browser specs exist; this is not a rendered pass.

crossResults.description: Axes/grids, camera/light/skeleton/audio/probe/physics/normal/tangent/texture helpers; dynamically updated transforms and resources.
crossResults.reason: The public helpers namespace includes axes, grids, camera, lights, skeleton, audio orientation, probes, collider, texture, normals and tangents. The dynamic adapter resamples caller-provided state each frame, replaces changed registered line nodes and unsubscribes/removes its owned node on disposal. The texture helper previews caller-supplied CPU pixels, not arbitrary GPU-resident textures; tests exist but were not run in this audit.

crossResults.description: Spatial DOM labels, embedded interactive DOM surfaces, vector output, text output, stereo/anaglyph/parallax output and accessible event behavior.
crossResults.reason: Opt-in addons implement screen and perspective DOM elements with interactive pointer routing, ARIA visibility and restoration, clipped SVG, ASCII text capture and side-by-side/over-under/anaglyph/parallax stereo outputs. Limits are explicit: DOM occlusion is a caller-provided anchor test, SVG is static and flat, and stereo rejects shared temporal history. Unit and browser specifications exist, but browser, pixel and iframe-specific behavior were not verified here.

crossResults.description: Scene/project editor, hierarchy, properties, assets, animation, live shader graph, frame inspector, texture inspector, profiling, serialization, undo/redo and static export.
crossResults.reason: The editor mounts hierarchy, properties, assets, timeline, live shader graph, texture/frame inspectors and profiler, with serialization, undo/redo and static export. However its asset import buttons select a generated triangle or a fixed Fox fixture. Reimport changes recorded settings and revision, triggering reload of referenced meshes, but the reload does not pass those import settings to the loader. Timeline controls change a local model without ticking or driving the viewport preview, although imported node animation can advance in global play mode. Frame inspection explicitly reports partial phase coverage and null whole-frame timings; the current profiler correctly labels unavailable CPU samples.

crossResults.description: Worker-owned rendering, input/resize bridge, task pool, resource transfer, worker failure and teardown.
crossResults.reason: Worker-owned rendering, canvas/buffer transfer, input and resize forwarding, a bounded task pool, failure handling and teardown are implemented with unit/browser specifications. Resource synchronization is narrower than the combined requirement: texture handles are copied only for bounded CPU-backed 2D color data, with other live, storage, attachment and shared-mutable backings rejected and host updates requiring a new scene snapshot. Normal dispose resolves on forced-termination timeout without an acknowledgement; disposeStrict reports that timeout.

crossResults.description: Typed public entrypoints, optional addon modules, ESM/CommonJS installed consumers, tree shaking, declarations, examples, asset licensing and deterministic package builds.
crossResults.reason: Typed export maps, optional addon subpaths, a math CommonJS bridge, packed-consumer/tree-shaking checks, example scenarios and license screening exist. The explicit require condition and packed CommonJS test cover math, not a broadly established root/Node-version matrix. The consumer matrix currently unconditionally refuses both npm and pnpm execution. Complete example and shipped-asset license coverage and byte-identical repeated package builds were not established.

crossResults.description: Automated source, integration, browser, performance, visual, device and resource-lifetime verification with scoped, honest product claims.
crossResults.reason: Source/integration inventories, browser and resource-soak specs, subject-aware visual checks, performance analysis and evidence-tier documentation exist. However the source runner's no-input workspace admission unconditionally fails before staging, and the consumer matrix similarly rejects execution. Candidate browser, visual, performance and physical-device results are not established; documentation states acceptance has not run. Product-claim accuracy is also incomplete: the public app guide still describes a safe-basic fallback that the mount implementation says was removed.

crossResults.description: Every app exposes truthful readiness, failure and cancellation; parallel apps isolate settings, events, resource ownership and diagnostic records.
crossResults.reason: The app has mount-scoped renderer/first-frame outcomes, cancellation, strict readiness and app-owned asset events; device-owned pool registrations are now filtered on restore. The shared registry still accepts registrations without a device and rebuilds those for any device, so isolation of every app-owned registration is not established. The remount cleanup path can also stop before retiring the old controller if an earlier cleanup throws.

crossResults.description: Scene/context loss, background suspension, resize, async loads, concurrent disposal and repeated remount have deterministic behavior. All owned resources and callbacks are released even when a disposer fails.
crossResults.reason: ResourceLifecycle attempts all disposers and retains failed final releases for retry; app lifecycle and shader tests cover selected cancellation, loss and disposal cases. However, scene remount calls the loss unsubscriber, compute disposal, controller retirement and physics disposal sequentially inside one try: a throw skips later cleanup. GameAppRuntime likewise marks itself disposed before unguarded unsubscriptions and owned-input/loop/app disposal, preventing a later retry of skipped work. Universal cleanup on disposer failure is therefore not implemented.

crossResults.description: Every supported loader handles parent-relative dependencies, duplicate/shared references, cycles, cancellation, retries, decoder failures, memory limits and secure request/cache partitioning.
crossResults.reason: AssetManager implements identity-partitioned sharing, dependency-cycle detection, per-subscriber cancellation, retry and rollback; bounded codec work and graph/request tests exist. The exported loader and adapter surface is much wider than those exercised paths, and the conformance inventory explicitly leaves many formats unverified. The complete dependency, failure, memory and security contract for every supported loader was not established.

crossResults.description: Content integrity verifies actual admitted bytes and subresources; manifests, redirects, cache identities and strict/fallback diagnostics describe exactly what rendered.
crossResults.reason: The typed asset path validates document/dependency digests, request identity, redirects and security-sensitive texture failures; tests exercise changed bytes and redirect mismatches. Texture load issues contain a fallback boolean, but the root actor converts them to code plus detail and drops that field; the detail says the texture failed without identifying the actual substituted texture. Thus the complete strict/fallback diagnostic contract for what rendered is not established.

crossResults.description: Conformance fixtures have documented provenance, license, digest and independent expected output. Claimed variants are decoded and rendered; classification counts do not stand in for runtime behavior.
crossResults.reason: The versioned fixture manifest records independently authored expectations, provenance, license and SHA-256, and selected bytes are decoded and checked by source tests. The documented initial corpus is narrow: for example, the extension matrix has Draco and Meshopt decoder-required paths but the conformance corpus lists uncompressed and Basis glTF combinations rather than those combinations. The root rendering spec exists, but its existence is not a rendered result and full claimed-variant conformance is not established.

crossResults.description: Supported browser, OS, device, backend and feature combinations have versioned support labels. Software, experimental, emulated and physical-device evidence remain separate.
crossResults.reason: A versioned compatibility matrix defines browser/OS/backend target cells and explicit supported, experimental, unsupported and unverified labels, with software, emulated, experimental and physical evidence separated. It does not enumerate the requested individual feature combinations as support cells. All current target cells remain unverified; this is not a claim that any browser or device passed.

crossResults.description: Rendered option behavior is checked end to end; unsupported values return stable diagnostics instead of silent approximations.
crossResults.reason: There are explicit unsupported-option errors and fidelity diagnostics, including the actual glTF UV set used, and a browser spec exercises selected material options through rendered pixels. That spec covers emissive strength, variants and pointer animation, not the full rendered option surface, and other extension paths are explicitly parsed with rendering limits. End-to-end checks and stable diagnostics for all unsupported values are not established.

crossResults.description: World text covers licensed fonts, Unicode, shaping, fallback, direction, layout, dynamic atlases and accessible alternatives. Lines preserve width, dashes, gradients, clipping and alpha.
