crossResults.reason: Licensed-font metadata, native run shaping and fallback, DOM accessible counterparts, bounded atlas resources and line width/dash/color/clipping paths exist with focused tests. Loaded-font shared-atlas entries are whole shaped label snapshots, not individually cached dynamic glyphs; wrapped bidi scopes can be rejected and selected glyph coverage remains platform-unverified. The full dynamic-atlas and text/line breadth is therefore not established; browser pixels are separate acceptance.

crossResults.description: The existing React integration handles both documented peer majors, real readiness, StrictMode, Suspense, SSR/hydration, cache isolation, cancellation and disposal.
crossResults.reason: The adapter has strict readiness handling, scoped resource identities, cancellation, StrictMode-safe ownership and SSR paths; a packed React 18/19 hydration spec is authored. Model starts its cancellable preload after commit, but default direct resource.read/useAuraAsset reads made before the first commit are uncancellable unless a request signal or explicit disposal is provided. The combined lifecycle contract is not complete, and the two-major browser exercise has not run for this candidate.

crossResults.description: Public exports and types have a versioned stability policy, independently reproducible API comparisons, deprecation windows and migration guidance.
crossResults.reason: The stability policy, deprecation windows and migration-record requirements exist. Tooling compares packed declarations, bounded static runtime exports and condition targets against digest-checked prior archives, but metadata origin/freshness and a current candidate-bound complete comparison and migration record remain unestablished.

crossResults.description: Every supported documentation snippet, example, starter and installed consumer is built from packed packages without undeclared harness repairs. Test JavaScript, TypeScript, module conditions, optional peers, SSR and workers.
crossResults.reason: Catalog discovery, candidate archive binding and tests for installed consumers exist. Capability and standalone examples use generated package/configuration harnesses; these are recorded, but do not establish the behavior of every supported original example or scaffold. More decisively, the source consumer-matrix producer stops at an unconditional pnpm execution-isolation guard after preflight; the following producer is also explicitly unavailable. The required complete JS/TS, conditions, peer, SSR and worker matrix is not produced.

crossResults.description: Existing bundle budgets pass without being raised; repeated like-for-like workloads report startup, p50/p95/p99, bytes, resource counts and available hardware timing. Counters and software results are not visual or hardware proof.
crossResults.reason: Versioned fixed workloads, budget analysis and no-data handling exist, and the documented budgets were not raised. The only checked-in bundle table is historical and records several overruns; it explicitly is not a current candidate measurement. There is no established current passing bundle report or like-for-like rendered workload result. GPU residency and complete JS allocation counts are explicitly unavailable rather than inferred from counters.

crossResults.description: Physics/game paths expose only implemented behavior; advanced shapes, joints, vehicles, input, reset, replay, audio, HUD and disposal have scoped evidence.
crossResults.reason: Physics implements bounded collider, constraint and vehicle paths, and game input, reset, evidence ownership and disposal have scoped source tests. The root game stub rejects its unavailable implementation rather than pretending to supply a game. The direct GameAppRuntime disposal path, however, marks itself disposed before unguarded unsubscribers and input/loop/app disposers; one throw can leave subsequent owned objects live with no retry. Full disposal maturity is therefore not established.

crossResults.description: Package release planning, tarball validation and generated exports use one versioned inventory; historical package sets remain reproducible.
crossResults.reason: Release planning and archive admission use explicit versioned historical and native package inventories, preserving historical sets. Generated exports instead originate from aura.exports.json, while package tiers are a separate static map; these are not one versioned inventory shared by all named consumers.

crossResults.description: Source, generated assets, dependency graphs, tarballs and network activity are checked for prohibited engine implementation. Authorship requires recorded source provenance and review, not only absence of fingerprint hits.
crossResults.reason: Source/payload and dependency scanners, candidate archive inspection and a runtime-network classifier exist; the scanner explicitly treats fingerprint hits and their absence as review leads, not authorship proof. The current ledger has no completed evidence or provenance for this requirement, and complete per-file reviewed source provenance and a current candidate-bound packed/network audit were not established. Network observation is a later acceptance activity.

crossResults.description: Error messages, support documentation, licensed assets, keyboard operation, reduced-motion/high-contrast behavior and accessibility labels are correct for each supported surface.
crossResults.reason: The error overlay exposes an alert, world text has accessible DOM alternatives, and game accessibility reads reduced-motion and contrast preferences; the fixture manifest documents licenses. But mounted touch controls use divs with role=button and pointer handlers, without a tabindex or keyboard activation handler, so keyboard operation is not correct for every supported surface. Correct behavior and license coverage across all surfaces and assets remain unestablished.

crossResults.description: Performance, browser and physical-device results report failures and unavailable cases explicitly. Live-device and publication evidence follows code freeze and does not masquerade as source completion.
crossResults.reason: Performance reports distinguish failures and no-data with reasons; browser evidence validates scenario failures and reasons, and source reports explicitly mark acceptance not-run. The browser scenario schema has passed, failed, unsupported and skipped but no distinct unavailable status, although the evidence policy requires unavailable, unsupported, skipped and failed to remain distinct. Its automated producer also leaves physical class unverified; actual live-device and publication evidence belongs after freeze, not this source audit.

crossResults.description: Pooled targets have exclusive leases and nonnegative counts; duplicate release and restoration cannot alias active targets. Late shader compilation disposes abandoned programs and settles dead handles accurately.
crossResults.reason: Token leases separate active from idle targets, reject stale releases and retire generations on loss; counts derive from live collections. ProgramCache settles cancelled handles and disposes normal late compilation successes, with corresponding tests. If a late program disposer throws, however, the cache's rejection handler loses the program reference and has no retry path; the native device may retain it until device teardown, but unconditional abandoned-program cleanup is not established.

crossResults.description: Source-only jobs stage all required current files and run all selected suites; packed-consumer reports are phase-specific and bound to candidate, tarball and project hashes. Generated resolution maps and modern API baselines agree.
crossResults.reason: Source staging, suite inventories, phase separation and candidate/archive/project hash validation are implemented, as are generated resolution-map checks and prior-release baseline tooling. A read-only comparison found all 119 registry paths match both generated and base tsconfig paths, and the CLI registry copy is byte-identical; this is not a full generation check. The source launcher invokes the no-input workspace-admission path, which unconditionally refuses before staging or running suites; the packed-consumer source producer also unconditionally refuses. Modern baseline preparation requires registry metadata and archives, and a current candidate comparison has not been established.

crossResults.description: Every G01–G55 row and every item in section 6 has a ledger entry with owner, exact implementation files, public entrypoint, tests, limitations and evidence. No row is unowned or untriaged.
crossResults.reason: The ledger and contract tests exist, and G01 now has implementation files, symbols, an entrypoint and a focused check. Across 1,901 outcomes, 1,271 have no implementation files and 1,879 have no public entrypoints; universal completed triage remains false.

crossResults.description: All confirmed P0 defects are reproduced by regression tests before correction and pass afterward.
crossResults.reason: A targeted G01 index-width regression is authored, but the complete confirmed-P0 inventory has no candidate-bound before-fix failure and after-fix passing record. The G27 P0 ledger entry remains confirmed-defect/incomplete with its required checks not run.

crossResults.description: Every listed CREATE/MODIFY file is implemented; no placeholder, mock-only implementation or silently ignored option is counted as complete.
crossResults.reason: All 1,314 literal section-4 CREATE/MODIFY paths currently exist, but existence is not implementation. The listed consumer-matrix producer unconditionally rejects both npm and pnpm execution for lack of an isolation/custody issuer; app disposal also leaves its onFrame callback set uncleared. Therefore not every required path is complete.

crossResults.description: Each importer and exporter has independent valid/invalid fixtures, format-variant coverage, bounded resource usage, explicit losses and independent round-trip or open-standard validation.
crossResults.reason: Independent fixture/digest tests, resource-limit tests, exporter loss checks and independent OBJ/STL readers exist. The conformance manifest still explicitly marks FBX, USD, USDZ and numerous other formats unverified; other format-specific tests exist, but independent valid/invalid, variant and round-trip coverage for every importer and exporter is not established.

crossResults.description: Geometry tests cover index-width boundaries, inverse-transpose normals, mixed inputs, groups, morphs, dynamic bounds, nested transforms, triangles and instances.
crossResults.reason: Authored geometry tests cover synthesized and explicit index boundaries, inverse-transpose normals, mixed indexed/unindexed streams, groups and morphs, dynamic deformed bounds, nested transforms, triangle hits and instance IDs. This classifies the test source coverage only; no current passing run was established.

crossResults.description: App readiness distinguishes successful renderer/first-frame outcomes from failed, cancelled or disposed states. Multiple apps isolate flags, diagnostics, asset events and resources; no subscriptions remain after final disposal.
crossResults.reason: Separate renderer/first-frame outcomes and failed, cancelled and disposed states are implemented, with app-scoped flags, asset events and diagnostic tests. However onFrame adds to a per-app Set even after disposal, and dispose clears device listeners but never clears that frame-callback Set; the no-remaining-subscriptions clause is not met.

crossResults.description: Asset graph tests prove nested relative paths, duplicate/shared reference counts, cycle rejection before await, independent cancellation, digest verification and final release.
crossResults.reason: The authored graph tests assert nested relative resolution, duplicate/shared edge counts and final release, cycle rejection, independent subscriber cancellation and digest-checked texture acquisition. The manager contains the corresponding cycle and subscriber ownership paths. These tests have not been shown to pass for this candidate.

crossResults.description: Required model custom materials, variants, LOD/colliders, line gradients/dashes and Unicode world text render as documented; only specified unsupported variants return an error.
crossResults.reason: Custom material, imported LOD, line and shaped-text source paths and rendered-test specifications exist. However the model bounds collider computes half-extents without model scale, and a whole-model custom material explicitly rejects a material variant; the roadmap requires supported custom materials to preserve variants and model collider behavior. Rendered and Unicode browser results are not established.

crossResults.description: React consumers pass server rendering, hydration, StrictMode, Suspense, retry, error boundaries, both declared peer majors and repeated mount/dispose from packed packages.
crossResults.reason: React 18 and 19 are declared peers and the packed-browser specification covers hydration, Suspense, retry, StrictMode, errors and repeated cleanup. A real packed matrix cannot currently execute: the shared npm/pnpm execution guard always throws pending an isolation/custody issuer. There is no current candidate-bound packed or browser pass.

crossResults.description: Each supported browser/backend/device cell has exact versioned evidence; software, experimental and physical-device cells are not conflated.
crossResults.reason: Exact browser/backend/physical-device evidence is a post-freeze acceptance disposition, not a new source implementation. The evidence policy distinguishes software and physical results and says current acceptance has not run; the retained September hardware report is bound to an older git SHA, not this candidate.

crossResults.description: Asset tests cover headers, credentials, cache separation, cross-origin dependency policy, same-URL concurrent callers, cancellation, progress and retries.
crossResults.reason: Authored tests cover header/credential/progress forwarding, policy-based cache identity, same-URL concurrent subscribers, independent cancellation and retry, and a cross-origin dependency rejection. This is source coverage, not a claim that the tests passed.

crossResults.description: Rendering tests prove the active backend, actual output pixels, materials, lights, shader compilation, compute dispatch, targets, resize, effects and cleanup.
crossResults.reason: Source and browser-test definitions cover active WebGL2/WebGPU selection, material/light pixels, real shader compilation and compute readback, resize, effects and lifecycle cleanup. Queue-shaped unit doubles do not execute WGSL or rasterize, and no candidate-bound rendered proof is claimed.

crossResults.description: Animation/audio tests cover interpolation, timing, fades, playback-rate changes, spatial orientation and actual visible or audio-graph effects.
crossResults.reason: Authored animation tests cover interpolation and traversal timing; audio tests cover fades, rate changes and orientation. The browser specification asserts visible skeletal deformation and a connected spatial audio graph with nonzero analyser output, but that specification has not been run for this candidate.

crossResults.description: Interaction/XR tests cover native-shaped browser objects, permission/session lifecycle, hit testing, hands, pointers, cancellation and listener/resource cleanup.
crossResults.reason: Authored source tests exercise browser-shaped XR frames, iterable hands, hit testing, session cancellation and listener cleanup, together with pointer capture and cancellation. A browser spec uses an injected XR session; it is not physical-device evidence and has no current acceptance run.

crossResults.description: Editor and alternative output tests cover keyboard access, graph persistence, real renderer state, resize, errors, accessible content and visual changes.
crossResults.reason: Authored editor tests exercise keyboard graph creation, persistence, errors and changed renderer pixels; alternative-output specifications exercise accessible DOM labels, resize, SVG pixels, ASCII and outlines. Source existence does not prove browser pixels or keyboard acceptance passed.

crossResults.description: A packed consumer successfully imports the root and each opt-in entrypoint; unsupported combinations fail with actionable diagnostics.
crossResults.reason: The packed consumer fixture imports the engine root and several opt-in entrypoints, and source tests check entrypoint mappings and optional-peer diagnostics. The producer's execution guard unconditionally rejects npm and pnpm installation, so a successful current packed consumer importing every opt-in entrypoint is not established.

crossResults.description: The required install profile, transitive lock graph, tests, runtime and packaged artifacts contain no external 3D engine dependency or imported, bundled, wrapped or copied engine implementation. Explicitly identified source/data replacements and the absence of external source fetches have independent provenance and retained review evidence.
crossResults.reason: Dependency/source/archive audit tooling exists, but the public math subpath still says its method bodies follow the three.js r185 reference, and the G27 P0 entry records independent replacement/review as incomplete. A complete reviewed current provenance inventory, packaged-artifact inspection and post-freeze network observation are not established; a fingerprint scan alone cannot establish authorship.

crossResults.description: Full source commands and the applicable remote browser commands pass. Failed and unavailable cases remain visibly open; retain logs and outputs.
crossResults.reason: The source command inventory and remote acceptance plan exist, but no current-candidate full passing run with retained results was found. The source image explicitly exits as unavailable, and browser acceptance remains locked until the global code-complete gate. This is not evidence that an unrun browser command failed.

crossResults.description: Existing critical-path and starter gzip budgets pass without being increased; optional packages remain absent from consumers that do not import them.
crossResults.reason: The enforced critical-path and starter budgets and installed optional-package exclusion checks exist. The retained October bundle report failed the core and three starter budgets, but is not bound to the current worktree; the current candidate has no established passing budget or installed tree-shaking report. Source comments still label the restored caps expected red, which is not a current measurement.

crossResults.description: Performance results record fixed workload revision, package version, sample size, backend, hardware and browser. Do not claim an improvement without a reproducible baseline.
crossResults.reason: The performance harness records workload digest, browser, backend, adapter/device and session samples and the policy requires a comparable baseline, but the produced report does not explicitly record the package version: baselineVersion is populated with the frozen commit, and the candidate identity contains hashes rather than a package version. The candidate has no collected baseline or measurements; the older 4.1.2 comparison is software-WebGL-only and cannot establish current hardware performance.

crossResults.description: Packed API/type compatibility, every supported documented example, untouched installed consumers and versioned package inventory pass with no skipped required checks.
crossResults.reason: Packed API comparison, clean-consumer and matrix validators exist, and an older clean-install report says pass, but that report is not bound to this candidate. The current matrix source producer and npm/pnpm execution custody fail closed, so the full installed-consumer, example, versioned inventory and compatibility checks have no current-candidate pass with zero required skips.

crossResults.description: Every claim in the support matrix and documentation matches the exact tests, backend and device evidence available.
crossResults.reason: The versioned browser matrix carefully labels candidate cells unverified and distinguishes software, injected and physical evidence. However, an all-claims reconciliation is not established; the generated public API reference also omits the current appendix's extrusion and WebGPU mip passages, despite the generator's appendix contract. Existing tests are not passing receipts.

crossResults.description: Required production code paths and source tests are complete before freezing the code-complete state. Live/device acceptance follows separately and must not be mislabeled as source completion.
crossResults.reason: The phase boundary and fail-closed gate policy are defined, but the global source freeze is not established. The ledger records source completion incomplete and acceptance not-run, the source job exits unavailable, and production WebGPU temporal v2 is explicitly disconnected. WebGPU now retains failed fences and exposes their errors, but a synchronous ResourceLifecycle can already have reported completion before a waiting fence later rejects. No candidate-bound CODE_COMPLETE_GO record was found in the native-capabilities reports directory.

crossResults.description: Public documentation and claims are updated only for the exact API, backend, device and evidence level actually verified.
crossResults.reason: The candidate evidence policy limits claims to their actual API, backend and device evidence and does not promote unrun browser or device cells. The generated public API reference is nevertheless out of sync with the current appendix, and an exhaustive reconciliation of all public claims against this candidate has not been demonstrated.

crossResults.description: Duplicate pooled-resource release cannot produce duplicate live leases; late compiled programs and failed partial allocations are disposed exactly once and dead handles cannot become ready.
crossResults.reason: The target pool uses acquisition-specific tokens and ignores stale releases; the program cache disposes late obsolete compilations and prevents stale handles from becoming ready. WebGPU partial allocations are retired behind a fence and failed fences retain their leases safely until invalidation. However, a synchronous ResourceLifecycle can report completion while that fence is waiting and cannot reacquire the owner if the fence later rejects; the allocation can remain owned and undestroyed until invalidation. Complete exactly-once cleanup and lifecycle accounting across that failure ordering are therefore not established. Tests were inspected, not run.

crossResults.description: Temporal history is isolated by app/device/view/frame, preserves previous color/depth, advances once per frame and handles reactive content, deformation, dynamic resolution and centered energy-preserving blur.
crossResults.reason: Per-owner/view history, once-per-frame commit, depth history, reactive classification and temporal tests exist. However, previous-depth handling explicitly reports an approximation without an expected-depth producer, deformation/instance pixels are treated as reactive rather than supplied full motion history, and WebGPU temporal reconstruction v2 is not connected to its native resolve. Cross-backend behavior and centered blur have no current candidate-bound pass.

crossResults.description: Clip planes, physical/tiled projection and depth conventions produce matching geometry, culling, shadows, post effects and readback. Every supported GPU render-state and vertex-layout field changes the intended actual behavior.
crossResults.reason: Physical and tiled projection helpers and native vertex/state mapping exist. The production camera and renderer explicitly reject nonstandard depth or clip range because forward, shadow and post paths do not share those conventions, while the roadmap requires negotiated reversed and logarithmic depth end to end. Actual GPU behavior of every supported state/layout field remains unverified.

crossResults.description: Weighted transparency passes order-permutation tests within its declared approximation; HDR identity and wide-gamut fallback behave as documented without conflating intermediates with display capabilities.
crossResults.reason: Weighted equations and order tests, extended-linear identity tests and output negotiation diagnostics exist; the documentation explicitly limits weighted rendering to eligible WebGL2 draws and reports sorted fallback elsewhere. No current-candidate passing order-permutation or rendered wide-gamut receipt was found, and float intermediates are explicitly reported separately from an unverified physical HDR display.

crossResults.description: UV atlases preserve/remap geometry data and supply correct baking inputs; repeated same-capacity line/media updates retain storage and dispose superseded resources.
crossResults.reason: The atlas copies and remaps geometry data and the public lighting adapter feeds generated chart bounds and geometry to the baker. Line updates reuse buffers within capacity; WebGL and WebGPU media paths retain storage for eligible unchanged layouts and retire superseded resources. On WebGPU a failed retirement fence retains the native lease and its charge until invalidation, but a ResourceLifecycle may already have reported completion before the failure, leaving complete superseded-resource disposal accounting unestablished. Source tests were inspected, not run, and do not prove browser/device behavior.

crossResults.description: Every public loader honors request/integrity policy and actual content identity. Unknown inputs fail explicitly; audio cache clear/dispose and image cancellation cannot resurrect or leak resources.
crossResults.reason: Shared policy and integrity fetches, explicit unknown-format failure, audio request-context identities and cancellation-safe cache publication are implemented, with tests for late image/audio results. The universal claim over every public loader and content-identity path is not established by the inspected sample or any current-candidate full asset-suite receipt.

crossResults.description: Animation multi-loop events, reverse/reflected time and group resubscription pass; pointer cancellation and asynchronous XR startup preserve owner state and never emit spurious activation/start events.
crossResults.reason: Traversal, group subscription ownership, pointer cancellation and generation/owner-guarded XR startup have implementations and targeted tests, including late-session closure and no cancelled click. The checkbox explicitly requires the animation cases to pass; no passing result bound to the current worktree was found, and native browser/headset behavior remains unrun.

crossResults.description: Packed decoder/worker assets work at root/nested deployment bases under the documented content policy, with explicit optional codec failures.
crossResults.reason: The Vite decoder plugin maps root and nested same-origin bases, explicit decoder-unavailable errors exist, and a packed-consumer browser spec exercises the Basis worker at both bases under a stated CSP. The inspected spec covers Basis rather than demonstrating all optional codecs, and no matching current-candidate packed deployment/browser receipt establishes the complete working claim.

crossResults.description: Source jobs stage required fixtures/templates and run complete asset/contract/release tests. Source/browser consumers have distinct current candidate-bound reports; installed tree-shaking has no browser prerequisite and modern API baselines are verified.
crossResults.reason: Staging inventories fixtures/templates and enumerates asset, contract, release and packed checks; tree-shaking is explicitly source-only and API baseline verification is implemented. The source image exits unavailable, clean-install custody is unconditionally unavailable and the isolated matrix producer is not implemented, so complete current candidate-bound source/browser reports and verified baselines are absent. The older clean-install pass is unbound.
